name: Used-phone repair and resale shop customer/IMEI/origin register (municipal laws)
buyer: Phone repair shops (assistências técnicas), used-phone resellers and used-parts sellers in cities that pass these laws
trigger: Porto Alegre Lei 14.156 (30 Dec 2024): keep up-to-date register of devices (customer name, signature, CPF, address, phone, brand, model, IMEI, copy of ID), open to municipal inspection; fines 500 UFM, 1,000 UFM on repeat, closure on second repeat. Belo Horizonte law (PL 651/2026, published 25 Sep 2026, in force about 24 Dec 2026): fields incl. colour, IMEI, delivery time, signed proof-of-origin declaration on the entry note, 5-year retention, LGPD, fines up to R$5k, licence revocation. SP city PL 588/2025 pending. Goiás Lei 15.076/2005 requires police registration of used-goods stores.
duty: Belo Horizonte Lei 12.144 (from PL 651/2026, published in the city's Diário Oficial (DOM) on 25/09/2026, 90 days to comply, so it should apply from about late Dec 2026). Shops that repair or resell used phones must record, for every device received, the owner's name, CPF, address and phone or email, plus brand, model, colour, IMEI, date and time of drop-off, and the purpose. The owner must sign a declaration that the phone was lawfully obtained and belongs to them. Records must be kept for at least 5 years on paper or electronically, in line with LGPD. Police, the Ministério Público and municipal inspectors can request them. Penalties: a written warning first, then R$1,000, then R$5,000, then loss of the operating permit and closure. Porto Alegre Lei 14.156 (published 30/12/2024, in force after 60 days) covers shops repairing or selling new or used phones. They must keep a current register with the customer's name, signature, CPF, address, phone, a copy of ID, and the phone's brand, model and IMEI, easy for the municipality to inspect. Fines are 500 UFM, then 1,000 UFM on a repeat, then closure on a second repeat. Not found: any regulation decree or named inspecting body for either city, and any court challenge. Carapicuíba (SP) has a similar municipal law. Serra (ES) has a 2025 bill (PL) whose status I did not confirm. I found no enacted law in São Paulo city, Curitiba, Recife, Salvador or Fortaleza; the search may not have reached municipal official gazettes.
market: Not found: there is no published count of shops under CNAE 9512-6/00 (repair of communication equipment), and the code also covers non-phone equipment. A count would need the Receita Federal open CNPJ data filtered by city (BH, Porto Alegre, Carapicuíba). That likely means a few thousand shops in total across the cities with laws, many of them informal or MEIs (micro-entrepreneurs).
competitor: I found no compliance-specific product, no state upload portal, and no mention of software in the BH or Porto Alegre coverage. Phone-shop service-order and ERP software is common and already stores customer details, CPF and IMEI. The missing pieces are the signed declaration, the ID copy and 5-year retention, which incumbents can add easily. Federally, the Celular Seguro app and the national register of phones flagged as stolen (Cadastro Nacional de Celulares com Restrição, IMEI lookup) let anyone check a phone, which is useful for an integration but does not keep the shop register. Searches for software tied to 'termo/declaração de procedência' and these law numbers returned nothing.
killer: No single product or rule kills this (unverified). The partial substitutes are: 1. generic service-order and phone-shop ERP software, which already holds the customer, CPF, IMEI, photos and digital signature; 2. a paper declaration form, which both laws allow; 3. the free CNCR IMEI check in the Celular Seguro app. On scope: the laws cover only Porto Alegre (Lei 14.156/2024), BH (reported as Lei 12.144/2026) and Carapicuíba. São Paulo, Serra and Embu das Artes have only bills, and there is no evidence of active inspection.
reason: The duty is real but limited to certain cities. BH Lei 12.144 was published 25/09/2026 with 90 days to comply. It requires owner and IMEI data, a signed declaration that the phone was lawfully obtained, and 5-year retention. Penalties start with a written warning, then R$1k, then R$5k, then losing the operating permit. Porto Alegre Lei 14.156 (in force 60 days after 30/12/2024) carries 500/1,000 UFM fines and closure. Carapicuíba has a similar law, and Serra has a pending bill. I found no compliance-specific product, no upload portal and no software mentioned. But this is a few fields plus a signature added to the work order, which existing phone-shop ERPs can add cheaply. Enforcement is lenient, the shops are tiny, demand is split city by city, and I found no shop count. Best sold as an add-on feature.
challenge_reason: I found nothing that kills this outright, but it is weak. Searches turned up no product, no association tool and no municipal upload portal built for this duty. Neither law requires electronic submission: shops only keep a register, on paper or electronically, and show it on request. The federal CNCR, checked through the Celular Seguro app, is a free IMEI lookup for consumers and police. It does not keep a shop's register. A web search summary says BH Lei 12.144 was published and takes effect 90 days later. Fines start with a written warning, and enforcement is not documented. Generic phone-shop service-order systems already store CPF and IMEI and capture digital signatures and photos. A free printed form or an add-on feature does most of the job. Only two to three cities have such laws, so the market is small.

name: Jewellery shop COAF compliance pack (SISCOAF registration, AML policy, annual negative declaration)
buyer: Small jewellers, gold buyers and precious-stone dealers, often family firms
trigger: Lei 9.613/1998 art. 9 plus COAF Res. 23/2012 (current version unverified): register in SISCOAF, keep AML policy proportional to size, send annual negative declaration if no suspicious operations; sanctions seen: R$100k for non-registration and R$171k for missing declarations 2019-2023. PL 3025/2023 gold framework (Câmara approved 22 Apr 2026, Senate pending) would add traceability; NF-e Ouro Ativo Financeiro under IN RFB 2.138/2023.
duty: Lei 9.613/1998 arts. 9-11 plus Res. Coaf 23/2012, still the legal basis cited in Aug 2026 Coaf decisions; complementary IN Coaf 7/2021, and IN Coaf 1 of 16 Jul 2026 is listed for the sector (content unverified). The duty: Siscoaf registration, customer identification and records, operation logging, cash and suspicious-operation reports, an AML policy, and an annual CNO due 31 Jan for the prior calendar year. Penalties: Decisão Coaf 29/2026 (published DOU 28 Aug 2026) fined R$100k for non-registration plus R$171k for 2019-2023 CNOs, with the partner fined an extra 25%. Safischer was fined R$382.8k (R$205.2k for missing CNOs). H. Minas was fined R$654k (Decisão 15/2026) for KYC and cash-reporting failures. PL 3025/2023 passed the Câmara on 22 Apr 2026; the last Senate status I found was 'aguardando despacho'.
market: I could not get a national count of active firms under CNAE 4783-1/01 (jewellery retail) plus gold and gem dealers. A Sebrae page (fetch timed out) reports jewellery firms in 94% of municipalities, with large city counts (São Paulo about 15.7k, Rio about 9.6k, Brasília about 5.9k), but these figures span 4 CNAEs and the method is unclear. CAGED data shows about 17k hires a year in the CNAE, which points to a sizeable formal sector. The number of firms actually registered in Siscoaf is unknown. Likely tens of thousands of firms carry the duty, but this is an estimate I did not verify.
competitor: I found no jeweller-specific PLD/Siscoaf SaaS in Portuguese searches. Existing alternatives: the free Coaf Siscoaf portal (the CNO itself is a simple online form), the IBGM/FGV/Feninjer AML guide for jewellers (free), accountants and law firms offering PLD consulting, and generic PLD consultancies (e.g. Compliasset blog). Generic PLD/KYC platforms aimed at financial firms exist, but I did not check their pricing or fit for jewellers.
killer: None found. Not reached: the number of registered jewellers (Coaf supervisao.pdf returned 404 when fetched, and search could not read the table). Also not checked: pricing of generic PLD/KYC platforms and whether they fit jewellers.
reason: The duty is real and enforced. Res. Coaf 23/2012 under Lei 9.613/98 still applies to jewellers: register in Siscoaf, keep customer records and operation logs, report cash operations and suspicious ones, and file a negative declaration (CNO) by 31 January each year. In August 2026 Decisão Coaf 29/2026 fined Pena & Mello R$100k for not registering plus R$171k for missing CNOs. 2026 fines also hit Safischer and H. Minas (R$654k). I found no jeweller-specific SaaS. Still, the CNO is a free, once-a-year Siscoaf form, and accountants or lawyers cover it cheaply. Recurring value would have to come from customer-record (KYC) and cash-operation logging. Buyers are fragmented, have little awareness of the duty and may pay little. A new Coaf instrução normativa (IN 1/2026, 16 July 2026) exists, but I did not check its content.
challenge_reason: I found nothing that kills it. Coaf Res. 23/2012 still seems to be the rule for jewellers: IN Coaf 7/2021 and a 2022 Coaf supervision bulletin both cite it, and I found no newer resolution replacing it. Enforcement is heavy and aimed at this sector. In 2023, R$32.4m of Coaf's R$38.3m in fines fell on jewellery, stones and precious metals. Fines reached R$96.8m in 2025, and in June 2026 a jeweller was fined R$654k. Portuguese searches found no software built for jewellers and no ERP add-on that does this job. The free Siscoaf portal only covers registration and filing. It does not handle customer ID, cash-transaction records or the AML policy. Two points remain unclear: the size of the market (I could not read the per-sector count in Coaf's 'Grandes Números') and whether jewellers will pay for software. PL 3025 is still waiting in the Senate.

name: SISAGUA monthly reporting and sampling plan for private collective water solutions (SAC)
buyer: Condominiums, small factories, shops, rural communities and associations that supply water from their own well or tanker
trigger: Portaria GM/MS 888/2021 (federal, annex XX of PC 5/2017) plus state/municipal rules: SISAGUA cadastro, sampling plan, monthly data entry (SP rule: by day 10; plan updated by 10 Jan), accredited-lab reports (Sao Paulo capital: laudo under 6 months, Portaria 550/2025), responsible technician with ART.
duty: Federal: Annex XX of PC 5/2017 as amended by Portaria GM/MS 888/2021, art. 14. The SAC responsible must control water quality, monitor it under a sampling plan, and send the plan to the health authority every year and whenever asked. São Paulo municipality (UVIS authorization page, Portaria 550/2025): use of the water needs prior authorization tied to the outorga, the responsible technician must keep up monitoring and regular SISAGUA data entry under Annex XX and Res. SS 65/2016, and changes must be reported within 30 days. São José dos Campos also requires SISAGUA registration, a DAEE outorga, chlorination, an ART and periodic reporting. SS 65/2016 sets the plan update by 10 Jan and monthly data entry by day 10; this comes from search snippets only, because the PDF returned 503. Penalties: not found on the pages I opened. The 6-month laudo rule in Portaria 550/2025 was not verified, because the PDF text could not be extracted.
market: No national count of SACs was found. A CVS-SP communiqué (from a search snippet; the PDF itself returned 503) says about 11,000 responsible technicians for SAA and SAC enter data in SISAGUA in São Paulo state. Paraná's 8th Health Region alone had 611 active SACs in 2022, and SAC numbers in Paraná grew about 110% over ten years (UNIOESTE/UTFPR thesis). The national total is probably in the tens of thousands, but this is unverified.
competitor: I found no dedicated software for SAC/SISAGUA compliance. Searches for SISAGUA management software, LIMS integration and SISAGUA bulk import found nothing; whether SISAGUA has an API or bulk upload is unverified. SISAGUA is a free federal system that the responsible technician fills in by hand. The core job is done as a service by accredited labs and responsible technicians: a Santa Cruz do Rio Pardo (SP) tender has the lab take technical responsibility for feeding SISAGUA. Environmental consultancies are probably a channel too, but this is unverified.
reason: The duty is real and in force. Under Annex XX of PC 5/2017 (as amended by Portaria 888/2021, art. 14), the person responsible for a SAC must run quality control under a sampling plan and send that plan to the health authority every year. São Paulo city and São José dos Campos require SISAGUA registration, an ART and regular data entry. The monthly deadline (day 10) comes from SP state Res. SS 65/2016, read only in search snippets. I found no dedicated SAC/SISAGUA software. However, labs already sell sampling plus SISAGUA data entry as a bundle (Santa Cruz do Rio Pardo tender), and the responsible technician owns the task. So the job is done as a service, not left unserved. Buyers are scattered and lab-dependent, data entry is manual, there is no API, and willingness to pay is weak.

name: C1. Retail fuel station certified electronic stock/price/sales register and monthly ANP delivery (CNPE Res. 10/2026 + LMC in EFD)
buyer: Independent fuel stations (revendedor varejista), small bandeira-branca chains, state sindipostos
trigger: CNPE Resolução 10/2026 (DOU 14 Aug 2026): exclusively certified electronic records; ANP to update LMC rule within 180 days (~Feb 2027); fiscal side Ajuste SINIEF 14/2025 (LMC in EFD from 1 Sep 2025).
duty: Daily LMC per fuel/tank/nozzle (Res. ANP 884/2022, updating Portaria DNC 26/1992; electronic form allowed; LMC kept 6 months for inspection). Monthly LMC inside the EFD ICMS/IPI (records 1300/1310/1320/1350/1360/1370) since 1 Sep 2025 under Ajuste SINIEF 14/2025. Guia Prático 3.1.9 added the CAP_TANQUE field from Jan 2026. CNPE Res. 10/2026 (approved 14 Jul, DOU 14 Aug 2026) recommends that ANP update the LMC rule within 180 days to require certified electronic records of stock, price, purchases and sales with at least monthly transmission to ANP. It is a recommendation, and no ANP draft or public consultation was found. ANP sanctions apply under Lei 9.847/1999 (not re-checked this session). The 180-day mark falls around Feb 2027.
market: 44,678 fuel stations at end-2024 (ANP, via Agência Brasil). The 2025 count is in ANP Anuário 2026 table 3.17, but its values were not reached. Many are bandeira-branca independents.
competitor: Station management and automation ERPs: per the TOTVS 'sistema para posto de combustível' article (seen as a search summary; the page returned 402 when fetched), they offer pump/tank management and integration with volumetric gauges and concentrators. TOTVS also publishes an LMC explainer. e-Auditoria's e-Auditor audits the LMC from the SPED Fiscal file, checking tank-by-tank stock, nozzle sales and LMC against fiscal documents. Webposto, Linx Postos and AutoSystem were searched for, but no vendor pages were reached. The certified-system spec is pending from ANP, and incumbent vendors are likely to absorb it.
reason: The duty is real. Stations must keep the LMC daily (Res. ANP 884/2022, electronic form allowed), and since 1 Sep 2025 they must also report it monthly in the EFD ICMS/IPI under Ajuste SINIEF 14/2025 (records 1300/1310/1320). CNPE Res. 10/2026 (DOU 14 Aug 2026) only recommends that ANP require certified electronic records with monthly transmission within 180 days, and the ANP rule and certification spec are not out yet. Station automation ERPs (TOTVS and others) already integrate pumps and tank gauges and produce the LMC and EFD data, and e-Auditoria already checks LMC/SPED consistency. A certified-register spec will most likely be absorbed by these vendors and may need certified hardware. The buyers are already locked into their ERPs, so this is a poor fit for a solo founder.

name: C2. Compliance suite for alarm-monitoring, remote-concierge (portaria virtual) and camera-monitoring firms entering PF control (Lei 14.967/2024)
buyer: Small electronic-monitoring and portaria-remota companies (CNAE 8020-0/01), previously outside PF control
trigger: Lei 14.967/2024 art. 40 and art. 60 (adaptation to 9 Sep 2027); Decreto 13.012/2026 (10 Jun 2026); IN DG/PF 340 (4 Aug 2026): prior PF approval of articles of association before Junta Comercial registration, authorisation, registered supervisors and operators (courses, PF registration), GESP 3.
duty: The duty is real and in force under federal law. Lei 14.967/2024 (Estatuto da Segurança Privada) art. 40 requires electronic-monitoring firms (CNAE 8020-0/01) to get PF approval before their articles of association are registered at the Junta Comercial. They also need a PF operating authorisation, renewed every 5 years for monitoring firms (art. 40 I/b), against every 2 years for guard firms. Operators, monitoring supervisors and external technicians need specific courses and PF registration; per PF course handbooks, technicians must also be bound to the firm. Decreto 13.012/2026 (published 10 Jun 2026) has its own chapter on monitoring firms and art. 34 §4-6 covers isolated sales, multi-state remote monitoring, and a ban on guards doing technical inspection. IN DG/PF 340/2026 was published in the DOU on 4 Aug 2026. Transition under art. 60 runs to about Sep 2027. Decree fines run R$1,000-30,000, tripled for some cases; the source cited them for hiring irregular services. Frequency is mostly a one-off onboarding wave before Sep 2027, then a renewal every 5 years plus continuous staff course and registration upkeep. Not confirmed: whether portaria remota (remote concierge) counts as monitoring. No PF act found on this, and a Migalhas analysis says remote access control without weapons does not automatically make a firm private security. IN 340's monitoring-specific provisions were not read in full; only a news summary was reached.
market: ABESE's 2021 Panorama counted about 13,000 24h-monitoring firms, monitoring more than 12M properties. The same period reported 600+ portaria-remota firms serving about 4,000 condominiums (later sources say about 12k). No post-2021 count was found, and there is no PF register yet, because the PF page says no monitoring-only firm has been authorised so far.
competitor: No third-party tool for the new PF regime was found. Searches for monitoring software vendors (Segware/Sigma) plus Lei 14.967 or GESP found nothing on compliance features. These alarm-monitoring platforms are already installed in central stations and could add PF modules. The PF's own process is email to DPSP/CGCSP plus GESP for authorised firms. Specialist lawyers and consultancies are the likely substitute for the one-off authorisation. Sector ERPs for guard firms are unverified.
killer: None found. Main risks: lawyers and consultancies handling the one-off authorisation; staffing minimums (2 supervisors, 4 technicians, 4 operators) shrinking the pool of small firms; portaria remota without guards possibly falling outside the statute (unverified).
reason: The duty is real and new for about 13k small monitoring firms: PF pre-approval of articles, authorisation by about Sep 2027, renewal every 5 years, and course and PF registration for operators, supervisors and technicians. No dedicated tool was found. But the core pain is a one-off legal and registration push that suits consultancies and lawyers, and the recurring part is thin: 5-year renewal plus staff credential tracking. Incumbent monitoring-software vendors (Segware/Sigma etc.) own the buyer's daily workflow and could bundle a compliance module. The ABESE channel helps distribution. Portaria-remota coverage is legally unclear. A done-for-you authorisation service plus a credential and expiry tracker is plausible, but it has a deadline cliff.
challenge_reason: I found nothing that kills it. The duty is real: a PF orientation says CNAE 8020-0/01 firms must adapt by 9 Sep 2027 (Lei 14.967 art. 60). Per LegJur's text of Decreto 13.012, they also need prior PF approval of their articles, at least 2 supervisors, 4 external technicians and 4 operators with PF-registered courses, and certified premises. GESP 3 has been live since Aug 2026. PF expects the sector to grow from about 7k to over 17k firms. I found no third-party compliance tool; Segware/Sigma/Moni and GESP integrations showed nothing. Weaknesses: the minimum staffing will push many micro firms out, so the market is smaller. Authorisation is a one-off job for lawyers or consultants. Portaria remota without guards may fall outside the statute (unverified). There is no public GESP API.

name: C3. Condominium 'organic security' authorisation and records under Lei 14.967
buyer: Condominiums running own doormen or guards (síndicos, administradoras)
trigger: Estatuto requires services by authorised specialised firms or authorised in-house services; Decreto 13.012/2026.
reason: Duty is real. Lei 14.967/2024 art. 40 and Decreto 13.012 (9 Jun 2026) require Polícia Federal authorization for condominiums with in-house armed or vigilante security. It is renewed every 2 years, needs inspection, and requires notifying the state security secretariat within 10 working days. Fines run R$10k-30k. The adaptation deadline is about 10 Sep 2027. Plain doormen doing access control without firearms are expressly excluded. So the buyer pool is only the minority of condominiums with own vigilantes, which is small and mostly outsourced to licensed firms. The filing is a one-off plus a biennial renewal, and PF handles it through an electronic request. I found no dedicated software. I did not check this closely and found no register count. Weak market, low frequency.

name: C4. DOF+ yard stock reconciliation and Sinaflor tracing for small sawmills and timber yards
buyer: Small sawmills, timber yards, charcoal and wood traders (Amazon and southern states)
trigger: IN IBAMA 16/2022 (yard must be registered and homologated in DOF+); IN IBAMA 11/2025 (automatic balance migration from 30 Jun 2025); legacy DOF closing 1 Jan 2026; virtual balance must match physical stock; state systems (SP Sistema Madeira, MT/MG/PR control exotics).
duty: In force. IN Ibama 16/2022 created DOF+ Rastreabilidade: yards (pátios) must be registered and approved by the state environmental agency, and an A3 digital certificate is required. When the DOF+ virtual balance and physical stock disagree, the user is subject to environmental sanctions (Lei 9.605/1998; IN Ibama 1/2017 on DOF suspension and blocking). Adjustments go through the state agency (e.g. IDAF-ES NP 010). IN Ibama 11/2025 ran automatic migration of legacy balances from 30/06/2025 to 31/12/2025; remaining legacy origins were then cancelled, and later transfers need a manual request plus mandatory inspection. The gov.br service page (modified 06/02/2026) states the legacy DOF closes on 01/01/2026, except for lookups. The DOF+ service is free. The work is ongoing: every entry, conversion within yield coefficients, and final disposal (destinação final) must be recorded. Some states also control exotic species (MT, MG, PR).
market: No current national count of approved DOF+ yards was found. An older O Eco article says Pará had 1,268 firms registered in DOF, 30-40% of them blocked. Early-DOF reports put the sector at about 15k firms (Ibama/IBGE estimate), with 2,300 then registered. Both figures are dated. PA and MT were integrating their own systems (Sisflora) into DOF+ and could keep using the legacy DOF until integration finished; current status not verified. Realistic target: a few thousand small yards and sawmills, mainly outside PA/MT plus integrated states. An Ibama LAI (access-to-information) request would be needed for exact numbers.
competitor: No commercial software that reconciles DOF+ yard balances was found. Searches covered 'software controle estoque pátio DOF+', 'ERP madeireira integração DOF', 'sistema para serraria DOF' and 'DOF+ API webservice'. The only official tool is DOF+ itself, which can export yard balances as CSV; the SP SIGAM romaneio spreadsheet is used to check the virtual balance against physical stock. The Madeireiro app (App Store) is a sawmill production/romaneio tool and does not mention DOF. The Embrapa CalcMadeira only estimates yield. No public DOF+/Sinaflor API was found (the system was built by Serpro), so integration would mean CSV or manual entry. Environmental consultancies probably fill this need as a service; not verified.
killer: None found. No commercial software or association tool for DOF+ or Sisflora yard reconciliation turned up in 8 searches. Weakening facts: Pará and Mato Grosso run separate state Sisflora systems (SEMAS-PA and SEMA-MT rules), and there is no public DOF+ API.
reason: I confirmed the duty. Under IN Ibama 16/2022, sawmills and traders must register their yard in DOF+ and get it approved. A DOF+ yard balance that doesn't match physical stock leads to sanctions under Lei 9.605/1998 and to DOF blocking. Under IN 11/2025, automatic balance migration ran from 30 Jun to 31 Dec 2025; after that, moving balances needs a manual request and an inspection. Six searches found no product that reconciles DOF+ yard balances. The only sawmill tool found, the Madeireiro app, does not mention DOF. No public DOF+ API was found, so an MVP would rely on CSV import. That, plus A3-certificate access and consultants likely owning these clients, limits the score. The market is a few thousand yards (old figures: ~15k firms, 1,268 in Pará), and PA/MT partly use their own systems.
challenge_reason: I found no product that kills this. Eight Portuguese searches for ERPs, apps and consultancies that reconcile DOF+, Sisflora or yard balances turned up regulations and state guides, but no commercial software for the job. The duty is real. Yard balance must match physical stock, and in MT and PA the tolerance is 10%; a mismatch is an infraction. IN 11/2025 migrated balances and cancelled remaining legacy origins after 31 Dec 2025, with the legacy system expected to close on 1 Jan 2026. Three things weaken it. Pará and Mato Grosso, the biggest Amazon timber states, use their own state Sisflora systems rather than DOF+, so two separate integrations are needed. There is no public API. The buyers have little tech and probably rely on consultants (not verified). The number of yards was not found.

name: C5. EUDR geolocation and due-diligence pack for non-certified small coffee/cocoa cooperatives and exporters
buyer: Small coffee and cocoa cooperatives and exporters in Brazil, and family producers
trigger: EU Regulation 2023/1115: 30 Dec 2026 for medium/large operators, 30 Jun 2027 for micro/small; plots over 4 ha need polygons, under 4 ha points; UFRJ study (Jun 2026) warns cooperatives will be hit hardest.
reason: The EUDR is real and the dates hold: 30 Dec 2026 for large and medium operators, 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small. The Commission's May 2026 review did not reopen the text. I found nothing on a further delay, but my sources stop around May 2026. The core problem is the buyer. Non-EU producers have no direct EUDR duty; the pressure comes through EU buyers. Brazilian co-ops therefore pay only as suppliers, with no penalty on them and an unclear willingness to pay. Competition is heavy: Fairtrade Plot Insights is free for certified co-ops, the Cecafé-Serasa platform serves exporters, and osapiens is a commercial vendor. I did not check Brazil's risk class, co-op counts or pricing. The Portuguese-language gap for non-certified co-ops is thin and depends on buyer demand.

name: C6. ANM Relatório Anual de Lavra (RAL) for small titleholders: garimpo permits (PLG), extraction registers, sand/clay/crushed-stone licences
buyer: Small mining titleholders and mining co-operatives (garimpeiros, areeiros, ceramic-clay and quarry operators)
trigger: Annual RAL due 15 Mar (16 Mar in 2026) and 31 Mar for licence registrations without an approved PAE; late or missing filing is an infraction with a fine; the CFEM distribution calculation depends on it.
reason: Duty is real. The RAL is annual: due 16 Mar 2026 for most titles, including PLG and registros de extração, and 31 Mar for licence registrations without an approved PAE. Decreto 11.197/2022 makes late filing an infraction, and ANM Res. 223/2025 sets the fines. A free official channel (RALWeb, gov.br login) exists. The filing needs a habilitated Responsável Técnico (Portaria 155/2016) and prior SDC registration, so the buyer is the RT or consultancy more than the garimpeiro. The only software found is Trimble Landfolio, aimed at large miners. Small-vendor competition was not searched. No count of small titleholders was found (WWF figure: 1,943 gold titles, undated). The filing is largely a form on a free state portal, so willingness to pay is weak and the market is fragmented and hard to reach. Not checked: CFEM or TAH bundling.

name: C8. ESC, factoring and fomento-mercantil compliance (COAF, ECD, IOF)
buyer: Empresas Simples de Crédito and small factoring firms
trigger: LC 167/2019; Lei 9.613/1998 (COAF identification, records, reports, annual no-occurrence declaration by 31 Jan); ECD via SPED.
duty: Lei 9.613/1998: COAF registration and annual no-occurrence declaration (January); fines such as R$25,000 (2022 case). LC 167/2019 subjects ESCs to COAF and to ECD.
market: 891 ESCs in May 2022 (Fenacon/RedeSim), plus an unknown number of factoring firms
competitor: Sebrae-indicated ESC software vendors (names not retrieved); OfficeFactoring (open source, covers factoring, FIDC and ESC)
reason: The duty is real. Factoring firms are persons obliged under Lei 9.613/1998 and must register with COAF and file an annual no-occurrence declaration in January. A 2022 COAF fine of R$25,000 on a factoring firm for not reporting no-occurrence is cited. ESCs are subject to COAF under LC 167/2019. I could not confirm the current COAF resolution number or the 2027 deadline, so those are inferred. The market is small: 891 ESCs in 2022 (Fenacon), plus an unknown number of factoring firms. Competition exists: Sebrae keeps a list of ESC software vendors that cover COAF reporting and SPED, and OfficeFactoring is open source. The niche is small and already served, and it is probably handled by accountants. Active ESC counts for 2025-26 and the vendor names were not reached.

name: C10. Short-term-rental host registration and condominium consent tracker (STJ Tema 1.443, municipal registries)
buyer: Individual hosts and small STR managers; condominium managers
trigger: STJ 7 May 2026 (5-4) requires assembly authorisation for platform rentals in residential condominiums; Tema 1.443 repetitive appeal with national suspension from Sep 2026; municipal registries (Salvador Lei 9.877/2025, Ubatuba Lei 4.050/2017).
competitor: No dedicated STR-consent tracker found; portaria apps (Portaria na Nuvem, ControlOneApp, SIT Portaria Remota) do not handle STR registration; Airbnb and channel managers not checked in depth
reason: The legal trigger is real, but there is no single recurring duty a tool could serve. STJ Tema 1.443 (Segunda Seção, paradigm REsps 2.272.537 and 2.272.536) is suspending related cases nationally. The judgment has no date, and it creates no filing duty. A separate STJ ruling requires 2/3 assembly approval for short stays in residential-only condominiums. It is a one-off consent issue, not a recurring workflow. Salvador Lei 9.877/2025 requires hosts to hold a municipal registration and ISS is withheld by platforms. Rules differ by city, and I found no federal register. I found no dedicated product for tracking STR consent. Portaria apps exist but do not cover STR. Market size was not counted. Buyers are scattered individual hosts and condominium managers. Weak fit.

name: C15. Shooting-club and CAC habitualidade records and PF Sinarm-CAC compliance (clubs, ranges, gun shops)
buyer: Shooting clubs and ranges, gun and ammunition shops, CAC associations
trigger: Decreto 11.615/2023; PF took over registration and inspection of CACs on 1 Jul 2025; habitualidade (8 trainings or competitions in 12 months for the higher levels) and club attendance affect CR renewal; the PF has said the Sinarm-CAC system has identification problems and is planning a habitualidade module.
duty: PF Instrução Normativa DG/PF 311/2025 (in force since PF took over CACs on 1 Jul 2025; amended by IN 322/2026 on CR validity), under Decreto 11.615/2023. Art. 71 sets habitualidade levels: level 1 = 8 trainings or competitions in distinct events per 12 months; level 2 = 12 trainings + 4 competitions; level 3 = 20 trainings + 6 competitions. Proof is per representative weapon type and covers the whole CR validity at revalidation (Art. 22 §§3-4). Art. 72 says shooting entities must supply training and competition information from their own participation records. Art. 84 says entities must publish their modalities, events, weapons and calibres on their websites. Consequences fall on the shooter: CR not renewed or cancelled, and no new CR for 12 months (Arts. 22 §5, 30, 75). The IN states no specific penalty for an entity that fails to provide records. A July 2026 news report (maisgoias, which returned 403 so I couldn't read it) describes a proposed change to prove habitualidade by use type instead of per weapon; its status is unverified. Gun-shop duties (Sicovem ammunition sales control run by CBC; SIGMA) were not checked in detail.
market: About 2,038 shooting clubs in Brazil in 2024 (ABIAMB letter to the Câmara, May 2025, an interested party). 1,941 clubs by March 2022 (Poder360, from Army LAI data). New club registrations were suspended in Jan 2023 (56 granted in 2023, per Metrópoles). About 1.02 million active CAC certificates (PF, via SBT News), and about 30% of CACs own no registered gun and rely on clubs. I found no count of gun or ammunition shops.
competitor: Nothing found that does the core job (club-side habitualidade logging per weapon type and calibre, plus declarations or exports for Sinarm-CAC). Found: CAC Pro (mwm.ai), an app for individual shooters that tracks CR, CRAF and GT documents but not club habitualidade; Anolla, a foreign range-booking tool; Intarso, scoring software; Elite Clube and ASC Club, generic Brazilian club ERPs with no shooting-specific compliance; and the official systems (Sinarm-CAC, SIGMA, SisGCorp, Sicovem). I did not check whether the PF's planned habitualidade module exists or how it works. Brazilian niche vendors may exist that my searches missed, so treat competition as only partly checked.
killer: SCM Fire, club management software from SCM Concept Tecnologia da Informação Ltda, plus its member app Fire Mobile on the App Store. Clubs that use SCM Fire record habitualidades with the date, time and the shooter's own registered weapon (release notes say this was added for the January 2024 legal change). Since v1.6.2 in June 2024 the app also shows each member's habitualidade count per calibre. It has been on sale since 2021 and is still updated (v1.6.5). That is the club-side habitualidade logging the first check found nothing for.
reason: The duty is real and in force. PF IN 311/2025 (Sinarm-CAC) sets habitualidade levels: 8 trainings or competitions in 12 months for level 1, 12+4 for level 2 and 20+6 for level 3. Proof is needed per representative weapon type across the CR's validity, and missing proof means the CR is not renewed or is cancelled (arts. 22, 30, 71, 75). Art. 72 makes shooting entities supply the records. About 2,038 clubs (ABIAMB, 2024) is a reachable niche, but new club registrations have been frozen since 2023. In six searches I found no Brazilian club or gun-shop product for this, only individual CAC apps, foreign range tools and generic club ERPs. That could be a gap in my searches, not proof that none exist. Risks: frequent rule changes (a July 2026 report says habitualidade may move to one proof per use type), a possible PF module, and political risk.
challenge_reason: The first check found no club-side tool. I found one: SCM Fire, a Brazilian club management system whose member app logs habitualidades by weapon and calibre, with updates tracking legal changes since 2021. I did not confirm whether it exports to Sinarm-CAC or issues PF declarations. The market is also small and shrinking: few new clubs are being registered (Metropoles), and ABIAMB says fewer than 200,000 shooters stay active. The rules keep changing too, with a recent deal reported to cut habitualidade to one restricted-use and one permitted-use weapon (not confirmed in force). The PF's own habitualidade module, if it ships, could take over the declaration step. A new entrant would face an established incumbent in a small, politically volatile niche. I did not search for other vendors exhaustively.

name: Artisanal fisher paperwork keeper: RGP, REAP and Seguro Defeso eligibility checker for colônias, associations and cooperatives
buyer: Colônias de pescadores, fishers' associations, cooperatives and the lawyers/despachantes who serve members; fishers themselves are low-ability-to-pay
trigger: RGP must stay active (annual REAP, prova de vida, recadastramento) for Seguro Defeso; benefit moved toward MTE and tighter checks (CadÚnico, biometrics, Fundacentro interviews) with R$5bn of savings targeted; Codefat resolution 25 Feb 2026 extended filing deadlines for defeso periods to 30 Jun 2026; MP 1323/25. Lei 11.959/2009.
reason: The duty is real. Artisanal fishers need an active RGP, an annual REAP filed with the Ministry of Fisheries (MPA), CadÚnico enrolment and biometrics to get Seguro Defeso. MP 1323/2025 became Lei 15.399/2026 (published 5 May 2026, per news only; I did not open the Diário Oficial). The Lei 15.399/2026 REAP catch-up deadline for 2021-2025 is 31 Dec 2026, which creates a deadline spike. The benefit has been run by the MTE since Nov 2025. I found no commercial software for colônias. But the filing runs through free government systems (SisRGP, PesqBrasil, gov.br), and the fishers are poor and the colônias are small, so willingness to pay is weak. The market size was not checked. Buyers are fragmented, the job is mostly one-off paperwork help, and gov.br integration is hard. That makes it a niche idea with low willingness to pay.

name: AVCB/CLCB expiry tracker and renewal-file service for small premises, sold to small accounting offices, despachantes and multi-site small operators
buyer: Small accounting offices (500+ client portfolios), despachantes, and small multi-site operators (schools, bars, clinics, churches); individual shops have low frequency
trigger: AVCB/CLCB must be renewed on a state-set cycle (1-5 years) under Lei 13.425/2017 and state decrees; MG Emenda DAT 1/2026 blocks AVCB until notified items are fixed; Campinas LC 606/2026 changes enforcement and creates a provisional alvará that needs a Bombeiros deadline document.
duty: Real and in force, but set state by state. In SP, Decreto 69.118 of 9 Dec 2024 is the state fire-safety regulation (made under LC 1.257/2015). A 2026 AVCB issued through Via Fácil Bombeiros was valid to 2029, about 3 years, and the certificate states that the owner or user of the building must renew it. In MG, owners renew AVCB/CLCB on INFOSCIP through a technical professional (RT) with an inspection report, and the state service is free. Penalties: in SP, Lello (2019) cited fines of up to R$265k plus closure for condominiums, which is old and unverified against the 2024 decree. Campinas LC 606/2026 softened enforcement: unpaid fines were forgiven, businesses are first ordered to stop operating, a fine follows only if they ignore the order, and a provisional alvará is available while regularization is under way. Lei 13.425/2017 is cited in the claim; I did not re-check it. Frequency per premises is low, every 1 to 5 years.
market: Not reached: I found no register count of AVCB/CLCB holders or renewals. As a proxy, a 2019 EPTV/LAI survey found only 431 of 5,197 state schools in order on fire certification. Accounting offices and despachantes number in the tens of thousands nationally, but this was not verified this session.
competitor: I found no dedicated Brazilian AVCB/alvará expiry tracker. The core job (expiry alerts) is a thin feature already covered by: (1) spreadsheets; (2) at least one accounting system in the Contábeis thread (31 Jul 2026), named not by the forum but by a Contador who says it sends expiry notices with a set lead time; (3) managed regularization services that list AVCB/CLCB validity control and alvará renewal for drugstore, retail and restaurant chains (an OHub listing, "Gestão de Regularidade Patrimonial"), plus Licentec and many AVCB consultancies; (4) TOTVS/PC Sistemas, which has a module for documents and alvarás. Whether Acessórias or Domínio track expiry natively is unverified: no official docs were found, and the analyst in the thread still keeps a separate spreadsheet.
reason: The duty is real, but renewal comes only every 1 to 5 years and enforcement is uneven (Campinas just forgave fines and added a grace path). Willingness to pay looks weak. In the only demand evidence, a July 2026 forum thread, one accountant refuses the work as outside accounting, another says clients avoid renewing because of cost, and a third says his accounting system already alerts on expiry. Expiry tracking is a commodity feature that spreadsheets, accounting suites and regularization consultancies already cover. The real work (inspection reports, the RT's technical responsibility document, and filing on INFOSCIP or Via Fácil) needs a licensed engineer, which a solo founder can't easily build into an MVP. Each state has its own portal, so distribution is fragmented.

name: Food-service Manual de Boas Práticas, POP and temperature-log app for small lanchonetes, bars, bakeries and home food sellers
buyer: Owner-run restaurants, lanchonetes, bars, bakeries and cottage-food sellers needing documents for the municipal/state vigilância sanitária; also nutritionist/RT consultants who serve many of them
trigger: RDC 216/2004 requires MBP and POPs plus dated, signed records (pest control, temperature, water tank, handler health); state add-ons (SP Portaria CVS 5/2013, RS Portaria SES 799/2023); infractions under Lei 6.437/1977; alvará sanitário renewal depends on the municipality.
duty: Confirmed. ANVISA RDC 216/2004 (Regulamento Técnico de Boas Práticas para Serviços de Alimentação, amended by RDC 52/2014) is cited as the current rule. It requires an MBP covering hygiene, water, pest control, handler health and training, waste and quality, plus POPs and records. States and municipalities can add their own rules. It applies to restaurants, lanchonetes, bakeries, bars, confectioners and cantinas. The records are kept continuously, often daily (temperature logs). Non-compliance can lead to loss of the alvará or licença sanitária (academic source). I did not open or check the Lei 6.437/1977 penalty amounts or the state add-ons named in the claim (SP CVS 5/2013, RS Portaria 799/2023). Search summaries mention an ANVISA regulatory impact review of RDC 216, with consultations of the sector planned from October 2025. That came from an FNDE PDF I could not open, and I could not confirm whether a new rule has been published.
market: Abrasel, via Mercado&Consumo in January 2025, estimated about 1.35 million foodservice companies excluding MEIs (Nov 2024), plus about 660 thousand MEI CNPJs in the sector. Most are small and subject to RDC 216. The reachable buyers are mostly formal micro and small outlets, plus nutritionist RT consultants; I did not find a count of the consultants.
competitor:
There is no exact Brazilian SaaS match, but these partly cover the job:
- Boaconta (boaconta.com.br): a 122-file kit pre-filled with the business's details (1 MBP, 28 POPs, 28 Excel control logs including temperature). It is a document product, not an app, and the price was not shown.
- Padroniza Segurança de Alimentos: a consultancy that writes MBPs and POPs.
- SafetyCulture: community templates for RDC 216 audits and temperature logs in Portuguese.
- InovaFood: a free iOS app for food services covering checklists, action plans and an occurrence log, with only 3 ratings.
- GoCanvas and Miratag: generic temperature-log templates.
- Saipos (restaurant ERP): content only.
I did not check Checklist Fácil by name; the search returned nothing on it.
killer: No single killer. Weaker demand: low-risk lanchonetes and MEIs are exempt from licença sanitária in several jurisdictions (Fortaleza Decreto 15.114/2021; SC Resolução Normativa 003/DIVS/SUV/SES; Campos RJ). Porto Alegre's inspections are reportedly complaint-driven (unconfirmed). Generic checklist apps and template kits cover much of the job.
reason: The duty is real. Brazil's ANVISA rule RDC 216/2004, amended by RDC 52/2014, is still the base rule and requires a Manual de Boas Práticas, POPs and records. No single Brazilian subscription app for small food outlets turned up, but the core job is already partly covered by others. Boaconta sells a 122-file Word/Excel kit with 28 POPs and 28 logs, consultancies such as Padroniza write the documents, SafetyCulture has community Portuguese RDC 216 checklists, and the InovaFood app is free. Two risks hurt the case. Small owners tend to buy the documents once and keep paper logs. ANVISA's review of RDC 216 means the content will need rework. The more promising buyer is nutritionist consultants who run many clients.
challenge_reason:
I found nothing that kills the idea outright. No Brazilian SaaS turned up that handles MBP, POPs and temperature logs for small food-service businesses. What I did find:
- Generic checklist apps (SafetyCulture with Portuguese templates, Miratag).
- Kits of document templates (Boaconta).
- Consultancies, plus free Sebrae/Abrasel training.

I could not check Checklist Fácil, a Brazilian checklist SaaS, because the search didn't surface it and its site returned empty. Pressure on owners looks weak. Several municipalities and states treat lanchonetes and other low-risk food activities as exempt from the licença sanitária (Fortaleza decree; SC, where low-risk is exempt and medium-risk uses self-declaration; in Campos, MEIs are exempt). Porto Alegre reportedly inspects mainly after complaints, but that comes from a search summary (fetch failed). The duty still applies, but enforcement and the push to renew are weak, so willingness to pay is doubtful. Nutritionist consultants (RTs) are the more plausible buyer.

name: Investment-gold dealer compliance pack (permit, purchase book, daily totals, quarterly SZTFH report)
buyer: Jewellers, coin and bullion shops, and gold buyers that hold or want an SZTFH investment-gold permit
trigger: 2/2026 (II.3.) SZTFH decree under the Trade Act (CLXIV of 2005) since 1 Sept 2025: 7-year permit, a separate purchase record kept as daily totals, a quarterly report to SZTFH by the 20th of the month after the quarter (quantity bought and sold, revenue), a supervisory fee (3/2026 SZTFH) and fines of 500k to 100M HUF. Press says every dealer needed the permit by 31 March 2026.
duty: Investment-gold dealing needs an SZTFH permit (7 years). Licensees keep a stock and turnover register with daily totals and file a quarterly report by the 20th. They also pay an annual supervisory fee and declare revenue by 15 July.
market: Not found in any register. HUF 150M capital, supervisory board and a HUF 2M minimum annual fee imply a few dozen firms at most. The full permit-holder list was not found.
competitor: None found; only permit holders such as Conclude. No dedicated record or report software seen.
reason: The duty is real, but the buyer pool is far too small for a solo founder. Decree 2/2026 (II.3.) SZTFH, in force 8 Feb 2026, sets a 7-year permit, a separate stock and turnover register with daily totals (s.13), and a quarterly report by the 20th of the following month (s.14). The decree text has no penalty provisions, so the claimed 500k-100M HUF fines are unverified. Permit conditions are heavy: HUF 150M minimum capital (s.4), a supervisory board and qualified staff. Decree 3/2026 sets a supervisory fee of 1 per mille of revenue, minimum HUF 2M and maximum HUF 15M a year. Only large, financial-style firms such as Conclude can qualify, so likely a few dozen buyers at most. No competing software found, and the decree sets no electronic reporting system. Ordinary jewellers are excluded, so there is little demand.

name: Vehicle dismantler per-part register and OKIR waste data
buyer: Licensed vehicle dismantlers and scrapyards that sell used parts
trigger: Per-part register of every dismantled part for sale (source vehicle ID, dismantling-receipt number issued through the transport authority's system, fitness guarantee, date sold), plus annual OKIR waste data by 1 March under 309/2014 Korm. rendelet. The Somogy county waste authority issued fines for missing data (2026 decisions seen).
duty: 64/2009 KHEM receipt and colour marking confirmed; per-part register unconfirmed; 309/2014 OKIR waste data not re-checked
market: Not found; licensed dismantler count unknown (likely several hundred); 88 sites inspected in summer checks
competitor: None found for dismantlers; parts-listing and workshop tools not checked; the transport authority's receipt system is free
reason: The bontási átvételi igazolás duty is real. It is issued through the transport authority's IT system, and the dismantler needs a contract with the authority (64/2009 KHEM, §§2-5). The blue-part colour marking and the invoice statement are in §6 of the same decree. The per-part register rests only on a January 2015 article; the njt text I fetched has no per-part register clause, and I could not confirm the current text. The annual OKIR waste-data duty under 309/2014 and the Somogy fines were not re-checked. The number of licensed dismantlers was not found; about 120-130k scrap cars a year, under half going through registered yards. No dismantler-specific Hungarian software turned up, but only two Hungarian-language software searches were run. The market is small and the receipt step is handled in the authority's system, so the willingness to pay is doubtful.

name: Monthly antibiotic-use report assistant for food-animal vets
buyer: Practising vets who treat food-producing animals with a holding code
trigger: Since 28 Jan 2022 vets must report antibiotics actually administered, per holding and species, through Nébih ÜPR by the 15th of every month (128/2009 FVM decree and EU rules). Zero returns are allowed; delegates must be linked to holdings. From 1 Jan 2024 only vets with an authority licence may prescribe antibiotics for food animals.
duty: Monthly antibiotic-use report per holding and species via Nébih ÜPR by the 15th (128/2009 FVM decree; EU 2019/6 and 2021/578); in force since 28 Jan 2022; Nébih audits and opens proceedings for omission
market: About 2,900 practising vets (MÁOK, Jan 2024); food-animal or mixed vets are likely a few hundred
competitor: None found: free Nébih ÜPR web form (upr.nebih.gov.hu) with delegate access is the baseline
reason: Duty is real: since 28 Jan 2022 vets must report antibiotics actually administered, per holding and species, via Nébih ÜPR by the 15th monthly (128/2009 FVM decree plus EU 2019/6 and 2021/578); zero returns allowed; delegates linked to holdings; Nébih audits and has opened proceedings for deliberate omission. No named vet practice package with ÜPR export found, and the free ÜPR web form is the baseline. A Nébih machine interface was announced, but it was framed for farm-side software and the date is unclear. The market is tiny: about 2,900 practising vets, roughly 90% of those outside Budapest/Pest in small-animal practice, so food-animal vets are likely a few hundred. The workflow is a simple form, willingness to pay is low, and the state could ship its own API. Unchecked: which practice software vets use, exact penalty amounts, and ÜPR bulk upload.

name: Annual report filing assistant for small associations and foundations
buyer: Volunteer-run associations, sports clubs and foundations (tens of thousands exist; exact count not confirmed)
trigger: Civil Act (2011 CLXXV): annual report, plus public-benefit annex where applicable, approved by the members and filed electronically with the court (OBH) by the last day of the 5th month after year end, i.e. 31 May; also publication on the body's own site; court fines if not made good within a year. Simplified reports exist for small bodies.
duty: Civil Act 2011 CLXXV: annual report filed with OBH by 31 May, fine 10-900k HUF if not made good within a year
market: About 54,483 associations and foundations in 2024 (about 62,100 nonprofits in total)
competitor: Forintsoft Nonprofit kettős könyvelés; CivilTech free software; free OBH iFORM forms; civil-sector accountants
reason: Duty is real and in force: civil bodies must file their annual report with OBH by 31 May each year. A fine of 10-900k HUF is possible if it isn't made good within a year. Since 1 Jan 2026 filing is only possible through free official iFORM forms on magyarorszag.hu (SZÜF); the old ÁNYK route is gone. That is a real pain point, but the state form is free and the filing step is covered. Competition: Forintsoft nonprofit double-entry package, accountants who serve civil bodies, and the free CivilTech software programme. Market is large (about 54,500 associations and foundations, KSH/NIOK 2024), but volunteer treasurers pay little, buyers are scattered, and filing happens once a year. Possible niche: iFORM guidance plus a done-for-you service. Searched in Hungarian only; no direct iFORM-assistant product found.

name: Smart-tachograph (G2V2) compliance for small international van carriers
buyer: Small hauliers running 2.5-3.5 t vans in international transport
trigger: From 1 July 2026 vans of 2.5-3.5 t in international road haulage need a G2V2 smart tachograph and fall under driving-time rules (Reg. 561/2006); no general transition period; fines set by the country of inspection. A survey of 116 customers of one provider found over a third not converted.
duty: EU Reg. 561/2006 and 165/2014, amended by Mobility Package Reg. 2020/1054, directly applicable in Hungary: from 1 July 2026, vans over 2.5 t up to 3.5 t in paid international transport or cabotage must have a G2V2 smart tachograph, follow driving and rest time rules, and do the usual periodic data downloads and archiving (driver card and vehicle unit). Exemptions exist under Art. 3(aa)/(ha). Since 21 May 2022 the same vans need a Community licence under amended Hungarian Govt Decree 261/2011. Fines depend on the country of inspection; the Hungarian fine schedule was not checked (not_reached).
market: Not reached: no Hungarian count of vans of 2.5-3.5 t with a Community licence was found. The likely group is small international van hauliers holding a Community licence (licensing data held by the transport authority), but the number was not checked.
competitor: Ecofleet (Hungarian price list, 1,450 Ft/month per vehicle and per driver card for tachograph analysis); Webfleet Tacho Manager and TachoShare (Hungarian-language datasheets, remote download plus infringement alerts); Jaltest scheduled remote download; Michelin Connected Fleet tacho archive; DAF Connect and other vehicle-maker remote download. All do the core job, which is download, archive and infringement reporting.
reason: The duty is real. EU Regulations 561/2006 and 165/2014, as amended by 2020/1054, apply directly in Hungary. Since 1 July 2026, vans of 2.5-3.5 t doing paid international haulage or cabotage need a G2V2 tachograph, must follow driving-time rules, and must download and keep the data. There is no transition period, though some exemptions apply. The core job of downloading, archiving and analysing infringements is already sold in Hungary. Ecofleet charges 1,450 Ft per vehicle per month and the same per driver card (price list from 15 March 2026). Webfleet sells Tacho Manager and TachoShare with Hungarian datasheets, and Jaltest, Michelin and the vehicle makers' telematics cover the rest. With prices that low and incumbents in place, a solo founder has little room. Not reached: the Hungarian fine schedule and the number of affected Hungarian vans or Community-licence holders.

name: Boiler, pressure-vessel and lift inspection due-date tracker
buyer: Small workshops, bakeries, laundries and condominiums that own pressure vessels, boilers, lifts or cranes
trigger: Periodic inspection on the dates recorded on the BNY sheet (2/2016 NGM, 213/2019 Korm.), 60-day authority procedure; lifts and cranes under the EBSZ with records kept to scrapping.
reason: The duty is real: periodic inspection of pressure equipment follows the dates on the BNY sheet, with a 60-day authority procedure (kormanyhivatalok.hu info sheet 37). Lifts fall under 146/2014 Korm. (inspections roughly every six or twelve months). Cranes fall under the EBSZ, 47/1999 GM. The claim's legal citations are partly wrong or unverified: 2/2016 NGM and 213/2019 Korm. were not confirmed, and the pressure-equipment rules now seem to sit in 11/2022 SZTFH, which has several versions in force. I found no Hungarian tracker, but only 3 searches ran, so that is weak evidence. Lift maintenance firms and inspection bodies (TÜV SÜD) already schedule inspections, and generic maintenance software covers reminders. The buyer group is fragmented and its size is unquantified. Willingness to pay is low, because incumbent service providers bundle the reminder. Fines were not found.

name: Hunting-rights holder annual game report and plan upkeep
buyer: Hunting societies and landholders who hold hunting rights
trigger: Annual OSAP 1261 game-management report (period 1 March to end February) and the 1262 population estimate to the county hunting authority; management plans reviewed every 7 years; the lessee is responsible for carrying out the plan.
duty: Annual OSAP 1261 report and 1262 population estimate; hunting log and bag register (79/2004 FVM as amended by 6/2025 AM, applied from 1 Oct 2025)
market: Not found in a register; my own estimate is roughly 1,000-1,200 hunting-rights holders, unverified
competitor: State agrarstatisztika portal for OSAP 1261/1262; no commercial Hungarian e-log vendor found (Hunterra is foreign and only plans hunts)
reason: Duty is real: the annual OSAP 1261 game-management report (period 1 Mar to 28 Feb) is due from every hunting-rights holder. In the 2023 quality report the deadlines were 20 March to the county authority and 15 April to OVA, and they vary by year. The hunting-log duty also exists, and 6/2025 (IV.10.) AM, applied from 1 Oct 2025, lets it be kept electronically. The filing runs through the state agrarstatisztika portal, so the report itself is a free state tool, and a vendor adds little there. No commercial Hungarian e-log vendor turned up (only the foreign Hunterra hunt-planning app). The market is probably around 1,000-1,200 holders, which is my own estimate with no source found, and it is a niche of hobbyist societies with a low willingness to pay. The e-log requirements and any state e-log could not be checked. Sources: https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2025-6-20-7R ; https://agrarstatisztika.kormany.hu/download/1/44/23000/Minosegjelentes%20OSAP%201261%20adatgyujtes%20OVA-20230829.pdf

name: Condominium representative and annual-accounts registration tracker for professional condo managers (közös képviselő)
buyer: Professional common representatives and property-management firms (small offices managing dozens of condos), and self-managed condos with more than 6 units
trigger: Tht. rules: the representative or committee chair must be entered in the property register, or they may not lawfully handle the condo's affairs. The deadline was extended to 31 Oct 2026, and the sources say the assembly must remove officials who do not apply. Annual accounts must also be registered (Tht. 55/B §(2)) and are published by Lechner. After the deadline some authority and bank-account matters may be blocked (press claim).
duty: Tht. (2003. évi CXXXIII. tv., version in force from 29 Nov 2025): 55/A(2) says the common representative or committee chair may handle the condo's affairs only once the office is registered in the property register. 64/A allows unregistered officers to act only until 31 Oct 2026 (extension by 2025. évi XXIII. tv., in force from 13 May 2025). 49(6)(c) lets the assembly dismiss an officer who does not apply in time. 55/B(2) requires the approved annual accounts to be submitted, and the authority records the filing on the property sheet. No deadline is visible in that text: 31 May appears only in 2019-20 press, so this is unverified. 65(3) leaves sanctions to a government decree, and I found none. Registration is reported as lawyer-only since 15 Jan 2025. Whether the accounts filing is also lawyer-only is unverified. Recurring parts: the annual accounts filing and re-registration whenever an officer changes.
market: I found no register count or statistic. Pénzcentrum says more than one million flat owners are affected, and the duty covers every condo with more than 6 units. The number of professional condo managers and of condos still unregistered: not_reached.
competitor: Law firms sell flat-fee filing (HUF 79k + VAT for the representative entry, 39k for the accounts, 109k for both). The Netház/WHM Cloud condo-management systems (Invert Kft.) pass registration data to a partner lawyer. Novitax társasházkezelő handles condo records. Because registration needs a lawyer, the core filing job is already done by legal services, and software cannot file on its own. I found no software that tracks registration status across many condos or prepares the annual accounts filing. Whether the Lechner portal has a free upload: not_reached.
reason: The duty is real. Tht. 55/A(2) says officers of condos with more than 6 units may act only once registered with the ingatlanügyi hatóság. 64/A sets the deadline at 31 Oct 2026, three weeks away, and 49(6)(c) lets the assembly dismiss an officer who does not apply. The annual accounts filing under 55/B(2) has no deadline in the visible law text. A 31 May date appears only in 2019-20 press, and I found no penalty. Several sources say registration has been lawyer-only since 15 Jan 2025, so law-firm flat fees (HUF 79k/39k/109k), with Netház/WHM Cloud passing data to lawyers, already cover the core job. Left for software: a status tracker plus the annual accounts filing. That is thin, the one-off spike is nearly over, and the size of the market is unknown.

name: Klímagáz database and leak-test due-date and records tool for small HVAC and refrigeration firms and equipment owners
buyer: Small qualified HVAC and refrigeration contractors, plus owners of regulated cooling circuits (shops, restaurants, cold stores, refrigerated trucks)
trigger: Act 2024 LXXXVII, 458/2024 Korm. rendelet (amended 2025). Firms and persons register in the Klímagáz database. Equipment is registered per refrigerant circuit, with data entered within 8 days after the owner's order. Leak-test validity is checked by barcode at roadside and technical inspections. An annual climate-protection supervision fee is due once equipment is entered. Owners of unregistered mobile air-conditioning units must keep documentation for the authority. The 2026 EU F-gas phase-down also affects servicing.
duty:
Real and in force. Act LXXXVII of 2024 on climate gases (consolidated text dated 2026-01-02, in force from 2025-01-01) plus Government Decree 458/2024 (XII.30.). Who must register in the authority's Klímagáz database: firms doing F-gas work, and the owners and operators of equipment that must be leak-tested. Qualified firms must report leak-test results to the authority (§10(5)). The authority states that paper leak-test records are no longer accepted: only electronic protocols made and recorded in the Klímagáz database count, and a job counts as done only once its protocol is entered there. Leak-test validity is checked publicly by the equipment's barcode, including at vehicle technical inspections. Annual supervision fee under §5(9):
- 30 or 60 HUF per tCO2e of charge, with a minimum of 2,000 or 4,000 HUF and a cap of 2,000,000 HUF per installation.
- 40,000 HUF for listed activity categories.
- Paid in arrears in two halves, due 31 March and 30 September.

Fine amounts are set by the decree; I did not check them. Leak-test intervals follow the EU F-gas regulation.
market: Not reached. No public count was found of qualified firms or of registered circuits. Owners of regulated equipment (shops, restaurants, cold stores, refrigerated vehicles) probably number in the tens of thousands, and qualified HVAC firms likely a few thousand, but these figures are unverified.
competitor: The free, mandatory state system already does the core records job. The Klímagáz database (Nemzeti Klímavédelmi Hatóság) is the only place where a valid leak-test protocol can be made. It also holds the registration of each refrigerant circuit, and its public barcode lookup shows real-time leak-test validity. A third-party records tool would therefore only duplicate data entry, and no public API or bulk upload was found. Commercial tools found: no Hungarian F-gas-specific product. Foreign tools exist (Bacharach Parasense, GoCanvas or Jotform forms) and so does generic field-service software. Not verified: whether the database sends expiry reminders to owners or contractors, or offers a "due tests" list. That due-date and reminder layer is the only possible gap left, and it overlaps with generic field-service CRM, which is out of scope.
reason: The duty is real, recurring and enforced: per-circuit registration, electronic leak-test protocols, barcode checks at vehicle inspections and a twice-yearly fee. But the law and the authority's guidance make the free state Klímagáz database the only system where valid records can live, and it already shows validity in real time. With no API, any outside tool means entering everything twice. What is left is reminders of due tests for owners and contractors, plus possibly a fee estimate. That is thin and overlaps with generic field-service CRM. I could not confirm whether the database already sends reminders, or how many firms or circuits there are. Small HVAC firms seem unlikely to pay much for this. Not refuted by a commercial product; the core records job is taken by the state system.
sources: https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2024-87-00-00 ; https://nemzetiklimavedelmihatosag.kormany.hu/doc/MR_szektor_tajekoztato_1129.pdf ; https://nkvh.kormany.hu/download/c/4f/53000/utmutato_a_regisztraciora_kotelezett_berendezesek-felvitelehez_2503.pdf (snippet only; the fetch returned 503) ; https://nkvh.kormany.hu/download/9/64/73000/2025_marcius_1_tol_hatalyba_lepo_hazai_klImagaz_szabalyozas_1001.pdf (snippet only; the fetch returned 503) ; https://nemzetiklimavedelmihatosag.kormany.hu/doc/2025/regisztracio_felhasznaloi_25.pdf ; https://njt.jog.gov.hu/jogszabaly/2024-458-20-22

name: Tourist-tax (idegenforgalmi adó) rate lookup and monthly return for small guesthouses and short-term hosts
buyer: Small guesthouses and private hosts (mostly Airbnb-type)
trigger: Local tax decrees set the rate per municipality (2025 national cap HUF 804.5 per person per night; Eger 750 HUF from 1 Jan 2026). The host collects from guests and returns it monthly, for example by the 15th (Eger). VIZA and NTAK duties are separate and already vendor-served.
reason: The duty is real. Under the Htv. (1990. évi C. törvény), hosts collect idegenforgalmi adó per guest-night and file with the municipal tax authority. Eger sets the rate at 750 HUF from 1 Jan 2026, with return and payment by the 15th of the following month. Since 2023 the PMS software must hold the tax records, and the notary (jegyző) audits from them. Those PMS records already carry the tax data, and the municipal ASP portal handles filing. Government resolution 1420/2025 (XI. 13.) tells NTAK to prepare a pre-filled return draft by 31 Dec 2026, so a free state tool is due within weeks. The buyer pool is small hosts with a low willingness to pay. I found no live product doing municipality-specific returns. I did not check host counts or the 830 HUF 2026 cap, which only a financial portal states.

name: Digital self-check (önellenőrzés) and temperature log pack for micro food shops, butchers and bakeries
buyer: Micro food retailers, bakeries, butchers and kistermelők selling to shops
trigger: 61/2023 (XI.20.) AM amending 28/2017 FM: documented self-check plan, named responsible person, 2-year retention; electronic records must meet Nébih technical conditions; kistermelők must keep traceability/origin and waste records under 60/2023 AM
duty: 28/2017 FM as amended by 61/2023 AM; 852/2004/EK Art. 5; self-check plan, named person, 2-year retention; paper allowed for small and micro firms
market: not_reached (no register count found)
competitor: Foreign only: Xenia, FoodReady, Alcomo HACCP, HACCP Pocket, MyFoodCheck; no Hungarian vendor found
reason: The duty is real. 852/2004/EK Art. 5 requires HACCP-based procedures. The 28/2017 FM decree, amended by 61/2023 AM, requires a documented self-check plan naming the responsible person, with documents kept 2 years on site. Small and micro firms may use paper or electronic plans, so there is no digital mandate for the target group, which weakens willingness to pay. Searches found no Hungarian HACCP or temperature-log product, only foreign apps (Xenia, FoodReady, Alcomo, HACCP Pocket at 9.90 EUR one-off) with no Hungarian interface or Nébih claim. The search tool was weak on Hungarian vendors, and consultant services and free Nébih templates likely compete. Not checked: the Nébih e-record technical conditions (PDF unreadable), the business count, and fine levels. Pain and frequency are modest; sales would need a consultant channel.

name: Driving school instructor logbook for the KOKENY system
buyer: Small driving schools and independent instructors
trigger: Since Sept 2023 lessons must be pre-announced electronically with driver, car, start and end addresses (KAV KOKENY)
duty: Electronic pre-announcement of each driving lesson in KÖKÉNY (KAV), per 2023 reports. Penalty and legal basis not found.
market: Not verified. Roughly a few thousand driving schools and instructors in Hungary (estimate).
competitor: State KÖKÉNY (KAV) is the mandated channel. Anolla and E-Klikk are booking tools with no KÖKÉNY integration.
reason: Duty looks real but only 2023 sources confirm it. Eduline (Sept 2023) says instructors must announce lessons electronically in advance (driver, plate, time, start and end address). Telex says KÖKÉNY use is mandatory. I found no 2026 status, decree citation, penalty or deadline. The state KÖKÉNY system is the mandated channel, and I found no documented API or third-party integration, so an add-on would be a duplicate-entry layer at best. Generic booking tools (Anolla, E-Klikk) don't mention KÖKÉNY. Market is a few thousand schools and instructors (not verified). Buyers are tiny and the state system is free. A closed state system with no API caps the MVP, so the score stays low.

name: Periodic technical-inspection calendar and records for lifts, boilers and other high-hazard equipment
buyer: Condominium associations and building managers with lifts; small firms with boilers or pressure vessels, cranes, escalators or amusement rides; lift maintenance firms
trigger: Decree 173 (10 July 2013), Technical Regulation on inspection of objects of increased technical hazard. Mandatory periodic inspection: lifts, escalators and cranes every 3 years; boilers and pressure vessels every 4 years; quarries, rides and funiculars every 2 years; gas stations, oil depots and ammonia refrigeration annually. Lift safety regulation No. 446, in force 1 Jan 2014, binds every owner or operator. The Technical and Construction Supervision Agency plans the inspections.
duty: The duty is real and in force. Government Decree 173 (10 Jul 2013, in force 1 Jan 2014, amended by Decrees 189 and 383 in 2015) sets the inspection intervals counted from the last inspection: lifts, escalators and cranes every 3 years; boilers and pressure vessels every 4 years; quarries, funiculars, rides and cableways every 2 years; gas-filling stations, oil depots and ammonia refrigeration every year; mines every 6 months. The Agency head approves the inspection plan. Decree 446 (lift safe operation, in force 1 Jan 2014, binds all owners and operators) adds these owner duties: qualified maintenance, emergency release, periodic inspection, registration before commissioning under Decree 317/2012, and technical documentation. It also requires annual static and dynamic tests, and the operator must keep a record of repairs. The Product Safety and Free Movement Code governs enforcement. Under Art. 19, the Agency fines an owner who skips inspection and sets a new deadline; the fine doubles if that deadline is missed, and unpaid or uncorrected fines are tripled. Art. 20(3) and Art. 21 have accredited, insured inspection bodies do the inspections and report to the Agency within 5 working days. Fines for missing periodic inspection: lifts, cranes and escalators GEL 500 (repeat 1,000) under Art. 35; boilers, pressure vessels and rides GEL 750 (repeat 1,500) under Art. 34; quarries and oil depots GEL 2,000 (repeat 4,000) under Art. 33. Fines for nonconformities under Art. 29 (lifts) run from GEL 100 to 2,000. One caveat: the 2015 consolidated text of Decree 173 is paywalled, so I could not confirm whether the intervals changed.
market: Not quantified. I found no count of registered lifts or boilers. Tbilisi has many Soviet-era lifts (mostly MogilevLiftMash), and the city spends about GEL 40M a year co-funding lift replacement for condominium associations. The Agency's register would hold the real number, but I did not reach it. The paying buyers are mainly condominium associations, which are cash-poor, plus a few hundred small firms with boilers, cranes, gas stations or rides.
competitor: I found no Georgian software for owners to track equipment inspections, but the competitor search was thin: 6 searches, mostly about the law. The core job is already covered in another way. Accredited inspection bodies (for example Saqexpert, Tbilisi, listed by UNIDO as accredited for new and periodic lift inspection) and lift maintenance firms already handle the work. Maintenance contracts include monthly checks (for example, the ProCredit Bank tender). These firms are in a natural position to remind clients and keep the records. The Agency keeps the state register of high-hazard objects, and Tbilisi City Hall's lift co-financing program requires a technical inspection and state registration first. I did not search vendor software such as inspection-body or lift-firm CRMs.
reason: The duty is real and enforced: a lift inspection every 3 years, fines of GEL 500 to 1,000 for skipping it, and doubling or tripling on repeat or non-payment. But the pain is low. Inspection is needed only every 2 to 4 years for most objects, and accredited inspection bodies and lift maintenance firms already do the work and can easily handle reminders and records. Condominium associations are cash-poor and lean on City Hall programs, so willingness to pay is low. A calendar MVP would be simple, but it is barely more than a reminder. The better route may be selling software to inspection bodies or lift maintenance firms, but there are few of them. The count of lifts and boilers was not found.

name: Waste records, annual reporting and waste management plan service for small generators
buyer: Small and medium businesses that produce hazardous waste (garages and car repair, printing, clinics, dry cleaners, battery or oil handlers) or more than 2 t a year of non-hazardous waste; waste carriers and collectors
trigger: Waste Management Code and Government Decree 422 on waste records and reporting, amended by Decree 332 (6 Aug 2025, in force 1 Aug 2025). Decree 44 (21 Feb 2025, valid to 1 Jan 2028): waste plan and environmental manager above 200 t non-hazardous or any hazardous waste; records and reports for more than 2 t non-hazardous or any hazardous waste. Producers of 120 kg or less hazardous waste a year are exempt only until 1 Jan 2028, so a cliff is coming. Generators had to register in the waste database by 1 June 2022; reports are filed electronically at waste.mepa.gov.ge.
duty: Real and in force. I opened Government Decree No. 44 (21 Feb 2025), which applies from 1 Jan 2025 and is in force until 1 Jan 2028. It sets the thresholds for a company waste management plan and an environmental manager (Art. 3 and 4): more than 200 t a year of non-hazardous waste, any hazardous waste, or inert waste above 400 t for legal entities and above 1,000 t for individuals. Records and reporting to MEPA (Art. 5) apply to waste generators with more than 2 t a year of non-hazardous waste (municipal waste excluded), any hazardous waste, and operators under Code Art. 24 and 26. Entities in the listed activities that produce 120 kg or less of hazardous waste a year are exempt from all three duties until 2028. Report form and content are set by Decree 422, amended by Decree 332 (6 Aug 2025); I did not open the amendment text. Filing goes through the MEPA electronic WMS (wms.mepa.gov.ge). The plan is agreed with the National Environmental Agency for a fee of 100, 200 or 400 GEL depending on how fast the decision is wanted. Penalties: April 2026 Code amendments set 2,000 GEL for incomplete or incorrect reporting and 10,000 GEL for missing an agreed action-plan deadline (GeorgiaToday, search summary; it is unclear whether the 2,000 GEL applies only to EPR reporting). MEPA counted 240 violations of waste-management-plan requirements in H1 2026, out of 2,664 Waste Management Code violations in total. Not checked: what happens to the exemption after 2028, and the January 2026 amendment to Order 211.
market: Not found. My search for the number of companies registered in the WMS returned no statistics. The only proxy is enforcement: 240 plan-related violations in H1 2026 suggest at least hundreds of obliged firms, probably a few thousand hazardous-waste generators (garages, clinics, printers).
competitor: I found no private software or app in Georgian or English searches. The state WMS is a filing portal, not a tool for preparing records or plans. Plans are written by environmental consultancies; for example, Gama Consulting LLC (შპს „გამა კონსალტინგი“) wrote a plan for a hydropower project that is published on mepa.gov.ge. These firms seem to work on large projects and environmental impact assessments rather than garages or clinics. Not checked: consultant price lists, and whether MEPA offers a free plan template beyond the guidance document (mepa.gov.ge/Ge/Files/Download/45902).
killer: None found. Not settled: whether the WMS portal or MEPA's guidance (mepa.gov.ge/Ge/Files/Download/45902) includes a free plan template or an electronic logbook, because both PDFs were unreadable. Also not settled: whether licensed hazardous-waste collectors include the record-keeping and plan work in their collection service.
reason: The duty is real and current: annual records and reports, a waste plan, and an environmental manager, with fines rising in 2026 and 240 plan violations in H1 2026. I found no software. The state WMS only takes the filing, and the consultants I saw work on large projects.
