But many small producers (120 kg or less of hazardous waste) are exempt until 2028, and the decree itself lapses then, so the obligated small-firm base is uncertain. Reporting happens once a year and the plan is mostly a one-off. Willingness to pay in Georgia is low and fines are moderate. The market size is unknown. This looks more like a service business than scalable SaaS. A modest opportunity, with possible upside if the exemption ends in 2028.
challenge_reason: Georgian and English searches found no software, app or named consultancy that prepares waste records, annual reports or company waste plans for small generators. The only plan writers found were EIA consultancies working on large projects, such as Gama Consulting. The duty is enforced: Georgia Today counted 240 waste-plan violations by companies in the first half of 2026. Fine amounts were not found. Weak points: the buyers (garages, clinics) have little money and are not used to buying software. Licensed hazardous-waste collectors may already do the paperwork as part of their service (not checked). Neither MEPA PDF (the plan guidance and the WMS manual) could be read, so a free template inside WMS was not ruled out. No 2026 extension of the 120 kg exemption past 2028 was found.

name: Currency exchange point quarterly NBG report and compliance pack
buyer: Registered currency exchange point operators (small firms and sole traders)
trigger: National Bank rule on registration and regulation of currency exchange points, replaced by a new rule effective 9 July 2025 (order N167/04). The 2018 rule required a quarterly Excel report within 10 working days, a 10-day notice of data changes, a financial monitoring form, counterfeit-banknote certificates and transaction software. Registration is revoked for missed reports (an NBG revocation on 16 Dec 2025 cited Art. 16).
reason: Duty is real: NBG order N167/04 (9 Jul 2025) replaced the 2018 rule. NBG issues revocations, warnings and fines for missed reports, with Art. 16 as the revocation ground. Search snippets say reports go through the NBG's NBFI remote-supervision portal, due within 15 days after the reporting month. That is a free state channel, and the cadence may now be monthly, not quarterly as claimed. I could not read the 2025 text (docx and PDF fetches were unreadable). No operator count found; the market is likely a few hundred small firms. No dedicated competitor search was run, and exchange POS vendors likely cover the report. The niche is small, with thin willingness to pay and a tiny buyer pool.

name: Grant-consent and reporting compliance tracker for small NGOs and associations
buyer: Small civil-society organisations, associations and media outlets that receive foreign funding
trigger: Law on Grants amended April 2025 and March 2026, partly eased 15 April 2026: prior government consent for foreign grants, Anti-Corruption Bureau oversight, double-amount fines and criminal liability. Foreign-agent registration law of 1 April 2025.
reason: The duty is real. The Law on Grants (2024, amended 2025 and 4 March 2026) requires government consent for grants and has double-amount fines, a 20,000/40,000 GEL fine for entrepreneurs, and criminal liability. But the claim's enforcer is outdated: the Anti-Corruption Bureau was abolished on 2 March 2026 and its functions moved to the State Audit Office. So the grants.acb.gov.ge portal reference is stale. Consent is a per-grant, donor-led filing, not a recurring workflow. Buyers are politically targeted NGOs, so building the product carries legal and safety risk and the law keeps changing. Willingness to pay is weak, since NGOs lose donor funding. I found no private competitor, but I did not run a dedicated competitor search. Roughly 10,000 NGOs are registered (undated). I did not confirm the 15 April 2026 easing.

name: Cattle, sheep and goat holding registration and movement records
buyer: Livestock holders, traders and farmers' groups; municipal and vet bodies
trigger: Government Decree 483 (3 Oct 2019) on animal identification, registration and holding registration, run by the National Food Agency. Annual inspection of at least 3% of registered holdings from 1 Jan 2028. A small-ruminant rule applies separately.
reason: Decree 483 (3 Oct 2019) exists. It sets rules for cattle, small ruminants and pigs and is amended through Decree 629 of 30 Dec 2025. The state-run National Food Agency does the identification and registration from the state budget, so the state, not the farmer, carries most of the work. I could not read holder duties, fines or movement rules, because the annexes and consolidated text are paywalled. I could not confirm the 3% inspection from 2028. I found no private software and no state app, but searches were thin. Market is large in head count (Geostat: about 760k cattle, about 400k sheep and goats) but fragmented smallholders. Willingness to pay is low and the free state system covers registration. Score is low.

name: Business-registry compliance rescue for pre-2022 companies (Law on Entrepreneurs data update)
buyer: LLCs, joint-stock companies, partnerships, co-operatives and foreign branches registered before 1 Jan 2022, often family firms with no lawyer
trigger: Law on Entrepreneurs: update to 1 Apr 2026 deadline passed, non-compliant entities suspended from 1 Apr 2026 (banking, contracting, asset disposal restricted); NAPR says restoration until 1 Apr 2027; registration can be cancelled if a defect is not fixed. One-off deadline with many firms acting at once.
reason: Duty is real: NAPR (June 2026 notice) says entities suspended on 1 Apr 2026 lose representative authority, banking, property disposal and loans, and can restore until 1 Apr 2027. Revera/AmCham describe a later deregistration step; the 1 Jan 2027 and 1 Apr 2027 dates conflict and I could not reconcile them. The Ministry of Justice reported over 350,000 entities updated by March 2026. No count of remaining firms was found. Competition: NAPR offers free filing via my.gov.ge and Public Service Halls, and law firms sell the service. I found no dedicated software, but the search was thin. It is a one-off job with a short life, mostly done-for-you, with no recurring workflow, so the score is low.

name: Foreign-guest registration under the unified registry of foreigners (from 1 Sept 2026) for hosts and guesthouses
buyer: Guesthouses, small hotels, short-term rental hosts and landlords
trigger: Unified registry of foreigners and legal-status monitoring from 1 Sept 2026; any host duty is unconfirmed
reason: The registry is real: Georgia amended the Law on the Legal Status of Aliens and Stateless Persons, and the registry starts 1 Sept 2026 under the Justice Ministry's State Services Development Agency. Eurofast says implementing procedures are still being published. No source I found imposes any duty on hosts, guesthouses or landlords to register or notify foreign guests. The Eurofast article only advises employers of foreigners to audit their paperwork. The registry looks state-side, tracking foreigners' status, so this candidate has no confirmed duty, frequency, penalty or market count. I did not check the 25/06/2026 amendment text on matsne (the first search showed it, doc 1803-Vმს-XIმპ, but I never opened it), and I did not check the Georgian-language product landscape. The Georgian search returned nothing relevant. Treat as unproven and low priority.

name: Excise-stamp write-off and stock records for small alcohol and tobacco producers and importers
buyer: Small alcohol producers (chacha, wine, brandy), importers, wholesalers
trigger: Orders N33 and N34 of 5 Feb 2026 on write-off of excise goods with stamps; stamp face values and tobacco fixed excise changed 1 Jan 2026
reason: Duty is real but narrow. Orders N33/N34 (5 Feb 2026) only change on-site destruction write-off for Georgian-made stamped goods, with a 2% tax-official sample check, plus a 2025 look-back. This is an occasional event, not a recurring workflow. Monthly excise returns (Annex 2 for local, Annex 10 for imports) already run through rs.ge. Buyers are few, and small producers file via rs.ge. I found no private stamp-ledger software, but no demand evidence either. Penalties and market size (excise-stamp payers) were not found. Overlaps K08. Weak solo-founder product.

name: Community aqueduct (acueducto comunitario) SUI / RUPS / subsidio comunitario filing desk
buyer: Juntas administradoras de acueducto, asociaciones de usuarios, cooperativas and JAC that run rural or small urban water systems (organizaciones comunitarias)
trigger: RUPS registration with Superservicios, periodic SUI uploads, CRA tariff studies, and since 2024 reporting of subsidio comunitario (Decreto 1697/2023; Res. SSPD 20241000389885/2024; MVCT Res. 0642/2025 excluded 20 managers for SUI inconsistencies)
duty: The duty is real and in force. Res. SSPD 20241000389885 (25 Jul 2024, in force from publication) requires community water managers (gestores comunitarios de acueducto) that receive the subsidio comunitario (Decreto 1697/2023) to report to the SUI every four months, by the 5th day of the month after each period. Each report has three parts: the online form 'Información Subsidios Comunitarios', a monthly Excel file per subscriber (invoice number, invoice value, subsidy, balance) and one searchable PDF of all invoices. Late reports are flagged to MVCT and administrative action follows. The resolution sets no fines of its own. The real penalty is losing the subsidy: MVCT Res. 0642/2025 refused extensions to managers that uploaded incompletely or late. A current RUPS registration is also a condition. Separately, general SUI reporting (billing, subscribers, stratification) still applies to all providers registered in RUPS. Caveat: the subsidy is temporary. It is tied to art. 274 of Ley 2294/2023 (the PND) and lasts at most 36 months. MVCT Res. 0393/2026 and 0552/2026 show the program is still running in 2026, but how long the subsidy-specific part lasts is uncertain.
market: The Comuniagua presentation (dated 2024) mentions 1,491 community water managers in 2026 serving about 1.4M people in strata 1-2. That looks like a projection or target for subsidy-eligible managers. Portafolio estimates more than 10,000 rural community organizations overall, but many are informal and not in RUPS. A 2012 figure says under 15% reported to the SUI. Res. 0393/2026 lists 53 managers with a current subsidy in the emergency departments alone. No total from the RUPS register was found.
competitor: No commercial product aimed at the subsidio comunitario or SUI filing workflow was found in 5 Spanish-language searches. What exists: Minvivienda's free 'Software Integrin', which produces .csv files for SUI upload (cited in a SINAS technical-assistance record), the SUI web forms themselves, generic local billing or accounting programs (Prosoft at the AQUA 7 aqueduct in Acacías), and university thesis prototypes. Free Minvivienda and Superservicios technical assistance (the Comuniagua route) acts as a substitute. Whether Integrin produces the subsidy Excel and PDF bundle was not checked, because the instructivo PDF could not be read.
killer: Commercial software for rural and community aqueducts already does the SUI reporting. Mi Vereda (mivereda.com) is built for "acueductos rurales" and lists "Generación de reportes SUI Comercial", sold as an annual subscription priced by subscriber count. Sifasp Pro (sifasp.app) produces "Reportes SUI de PQR y facturación ... listos para el validador". Acuasoft (acuasoft.com) handles billing, DIAN e-invoicing and "liquidación de subsidios" for juntas de agua, including systems with fewer than 200 subscribers. Other vendors in this space: Software GBS, SOLINCloud, Yeminus and Prolyam. The only part left uncovered, the subsidio comunitario report, applies to about 350 gestores (Minvivienda), a very small market.
reason: The duty is real, recurs every four months and has a harsh penalty: losing the MVCT subsidy, as Res. 0642/2025 shows. No commercial tool does the subsidy reporting bundle. But the subsidy is temporary (36 months, tied to the 2022-2026 PND), so the core trigger may disappear. The buyers are volunteer-run rural associations with very low budgets and poor connectivity, and they get free state tools (Integrin) and free state assistance. The reachable market is about 1,500 organizations. An MVP is simple (billing data in, SUI Excel and PDF out), and selling through COCSASCOL or departmental water plans (PDA) is possible. Willingness to pay and how long the program lasts are the main weaknesses. Subscriber counts from RUPS and Integrin's subsidy coverage were not checked.
challenge_reason: The claim that no commercial product exists is wrong. Mi Vereda, Sifasp Pro and Acuasoft already target small and rural aqueducts with billing plus SUI commercial-report generation and subsidy liquidation. None of the vendor pages I opened mentions the subsidio comunitario matrix, the RUPS process or CRA tariff studies, so that gap is real. But Minvivienda puts subsidy recipients at about 350 gestores, and resolutions show cohorts of 165 to 224. Free Comuniagua technical help covers them, and the billing vendors can easily add the export. Buyers are cash-poor organisations whose money comes from tariffs. A standalone filing desk would be a feature for incumbents, not a business. Not verified: whether Integrin covers the subsidy upload, and the RUPS-admitted count.

name: Gold-buyer (RUCOM comercializador) back-office for the Plataforma de Trazabilidad de Minerales
buyer: RUCOM-registered comercializadores and casas de compra de oro that buy from small miners and barequeros
trigger: Res. ANM 759/2024 and Res. 1549/2025: every purchase/sale must go through the PTM via an authorised operator (OTTM); small mining stage from 2026-10-01 per Circular VSC 000009, full roll-out 2026-11-19 per Blu Radio; fines up to 1,000 smmlv. Also daily pre-purchase listing for subsistence miners (Res. 40103/2017 volume caps)
duty: Res. ANM 759 of 28 Oct 2024 created the PTM. Comercializadores, plantas de beneficio and consumers registered in RUCOM must record purchase and sale transactions through an authorised OTTM, and comercializadores and plantas de beneficio pay the PTM's operating costs. Res. ANM 1549/2025 phases the start: big mining and PIN titles from 1 Jan 2026, medium mining from 1 Apr 2026, and small mining, ARE, legalisations and subcontracts from 1 Oct 2026. Press reports (Blu Radio, Portafolio, Publimetro) say a 6-month transition began 19 May 2026, with mandatory nationwide use from 19 Nov 2026. These are probably the same scheme described two ways, but I did not reconcile them. Penalty: up to 1,000 smmlv per case for buying without proof of lawful origin or without using the traceability system (secondary source, abceconomia). RUCOM registration has been mandatory since 2015 (Decreto 276/2015), with sanctions and seizures for trading without it. Frequency: every transaction.
market: Not found. No current count of RUCOM-certified gold comercializadores turned up in two searches. ANM publishes the RUCOM lists, but I did not reach them. Casas de compra that buy only used gold are exempt. The market is probably a few thousand registered traders at most (unverified estimate). An El Colombiano piece reports that 35 tech firms grouped into 10 OTTM bids competed for this market.
competitor: Six OTTMs habilitated by ANM in Dec 2025: Cuántico Corporation S.A.S. (MinTrace), Grupo R&M Col S.A.S., Intellygence S.A.S., LN20 S.A.S., Lord Golden Docs S.A.S. and Sistemas Informáticos y Servicios Integrados S.A.S. MinTrace, as described by Portafolio, registers and manages purchase, processing, sale and export operations. It centralises transaction records, validates documents, holds proof of mineral origin, automates regulatory reports, and integrates with banks, accounting, document management and ANM services. It also runs a "Plan Pionero" onboarding programme. The state RUCOM/AnnA Minería platform covers registration and subsistence-miner lists. I found no public OTTM pricing, and no proof either way on whether the OTTMs handle daily subsistence-miner volume caps.
reason: The duty is real. Res. ANM 759/2024, changed by Res. 1549/2025, requires RUCOM comercializadores to record every purchase in the PTM through an OTTM. Purchases from small-mining titles start 1 Oct 2026, and national mandatory use starts 19 Nov 2026 per Portafolio and Blu Radio. Fines reach 1,000 smmlv. But the core job is already done. ANM habilitated six private OTTMs in Dec 2025: Cuantico (MinTrace), Grupo R&M Col, Intellygence, LN20, Lord Golden Docs and SIIS. MinTrace records purchases and sales, checks documents and origin support, automates regulatory reports and connects to accounting, ERP and banks. A founder could only add a thin layer on top of six vendors already competing for the same buyers, or else go through OTTM habilitation. Buyer count and OTTM pricing were not found.

name: Small transport-company reporting desk: Supertransporte annual subjective information (VIGIA) plus PESV follow-up
buyer: Small taxi, colectivo, special-transport and cargo companies (and fleets above 10 vehicles) supervised by Supertransporte
trigger: Annual subjective-information report by NIT-digit calendar (Circular Unica Titulo IV; Res. 13100/2025 sets supervised subjects); May 2026 sanction actions for omitted 2022-2024 reports; PESV follow-up in the SINST-VIGIA 2 PESV module (Res. 20223040040595/2022); Circular 34/2026 for non-transport fleets (Mintrabajo form, deadline in January)
duty: Confirmed in force. (1) Annual subjective report: Title IV of the Circular Única de Infraestructura y Transporte requires supervised parties (road passenger, cargo, special, taxi, mixed and mass-transit companies, among others) to file each year through VIGIA. Filing dates follow an annual calendar by the last digits of the NIT. The content is the financial statements with notes, the revisor fiscal's opinion, the management report, the litigation list, the income tax return, the shareholding and the meeting minutes. Penalty: Supertransporte administrative sanctions (amounts not found). I could not find the 2026 calendar resolution. The May 2026 sanction notification and Res. 13100/2025 are scanned PDFs that I could not read, so the 2026 supervised subsectors are unverified. (2) PESV: Res. 20223040040595/2022 (MinTransporte). Reporting goes through the SINST-VIGIA 2 PESV module, and a technical annex cites Res. 1455/2025. Annual frequency, but the deadline is conflicting: implementandosgi says 31 January, while a search summary of Supertransporte documents says the tenth business day of August. Sanctions are mentioned but not quantified.
market: Not quantified. No official count of supervised transport companies was found. One undated Supertransporte-related source mentions 527 licensed intermunicipal passenger companies. PESV applies to organisations with more than 10 vehicles, a much larger group that includes firms outside transport (one thesis claims a lower threshold of 2 drivers). The supervised group across taxi, special, cargo and other subsectors is probably several thousand firms, but that is unverified.
competitor: The free state portal (VIGIA / SINST-VIGIA 2) does the filing. It also offers web-service integration through a published data dictionary, which allows third-party tools. The content of the subjective report is prepared by the company's accountant or revisor fiscal, which is effectively the existing service. For PESV, I found consultancies and paid template courses (e.g. Atcal's 'plantillas documentales' sold via implementandosgi). Two searches named no commercial PESV SaaS, but that is not proof none exists, and I believe several do. Not refuted by a named product.
reason: Both duties are real. Under Title IV of the Circular Única, supervised road transport companies (taxi, special, cargo, passenger) file an annual subjective report in VIGIA, with dates set by NIT digits. The PESV methodology (Res. 20223040040595/2022) requires reporting in the free SINST-VIGIA 2 PESV module. But the subjective report is mostly financial statements, the revisor fiscal's opinion, minutes and the tax return, all prepared by accountants. Uploading them to a free state portal adds little that software could do. My searches named no PESV SaaS vendor, only consultants and template courses, so I can't say the core job is uncovered. Sources disagree on the PESV deadline. No count of supervised firms was found. The opportunity looks weak.

name: Driving-school (CEA) class, hours and certificate back-office for RUNT / SICOV / Supertransporte audits
buyer: Centros de Ensenanza Automovilistica (small independent driving schools)
trigger: Real-time registration of students, hours and exams in RUNT/SICOV (Ley 1005/2006 art. 10, Res. 14646/2021, Res. 20223040045295/2022); RUNTPRO migration 2024; Supertransporte: 315 active investigations (Mar 2025), 23 CEA suspended for logging dead instructors; Ley 2283/2023 allows virtual theory; bill to modernise academies filed Aug 2026
duty: Confirmed. Ley 2283/2023 (amends Código Nacional de Tránsito for Organismos de Apoyo al Tránsito incl. CEA) and Supertransporte Res. 5790/2016 (SICOV) require CEA to report classes, hours and exams to RUNT online and in real time. Attendance is checked biometrically at the start and end of every class, with random checks against the national ID registry (RNEC, per Res. 355/2023). Theory has to be finished and its exam passed before practical training can start. Res. 2877 of 1 Apr 2026 rebuilt SICOV for CEA/CIA/OT (new technical annex, facial recognition, a 6+3 month transition), and Res. 8863 of 16 Jul 2026 changed those transition dates. Penalties are suspensions and fines: 315 investigations active in Mar 2025, 26 CEA suspended, 17 sanctioned for expired registrations. Frequency: continuous, every class.
market: 742 CEA habilitados per the 2018 SICOV launch communiqué (cited via Xataka and other results). I found no current total. Supertransporte publishes a dashboard of habilitated CEA (Ficha Tablero CEA 2025), but its document gives no total. Estimate: roughly 700-1,000 CEA, many of them small, with demand rising from A2 motorcycle licences.
competitor: Not resolved. The mandatory layer is the homologated SICOV operators. The market for them is concentrated (La Silla Vacía: only a handful were authorised in 2013-2016), CEA can switch between them (Circular Externa 20265330000034, Feb 2026), and since Aug 2026 they must register in SINST VIGIA 2. I could not find their names or whether they bundle scheduling, billing or back-office modules. The search for "Olimpia IT" did not confirm a CEA product. The only commercial driving-school software found is foreign and generic (Total Driving School Management, Drive Scout, Colibri) with no RUNT/SICOV integration. The two key PDFs (the Feb 2026 circular and the Apr 2026 annex) came back as unreadable binary. not_reached: the operator list and their feature sets.
killer: Partial, not confirmed: the mandatory SICOV operator (for CEA, apparently the "Consorcio Sistema Integrado de Gestión y Seguridad para CEAs y CIAs") already supplies the management software, biometrics and real-time class logging. Scheduling through the SICOV app was reported in 2018. RUNTPRO is the free state portal for registering hours and certificates.
reason: The duty is real and in force. CEA have to report classes, hours and exams to RUNT/SICOV online and in real time, with biometric check-in by student and instructor. Supertransporte enforces this hard: 315 open investigations, suspensions and sanctions. SICOV itself was redesigned by Res. 2877 of 1 Apr 2026 (facial recognition, analytics), and Res. 8863 of Jul 2026 changed the transition dates. But the mandatory capture layer is run by a small, concentrated group of homologated SICOV operators. I could not get a list of them or find out whether they already bundle management features. No local CEA back-office product came up, only foreign generic driving-school tools. The market is about 742 CEA (2018 figure). The buyer pool is small, integration depends on operators who control access, and the rules keep shifting.
challenge_reason: I found no product that kills it. I also found no Colombian software for running a CEA back office, only foreign generic tools like Colibri, Anolla and Total Driving School Management. The weak point is that the core compliance job looks taken. The homologated SICOV operator supplies the "software de gestión", the biometric devices and the real-time class log, and a 2018 Xataka article says students sign up and book classes on the SICOV platform or its app. RUNTPRO is the free state portal. What is left is reconciling SICOV with RUNT, plus general scheduling and billing, and that needs RUNT developer accreditation (Res. 792/2013) and SICOV access that may be closed. The market is about 1,000 CEA, my own estimate from 21,305 CEA vehicles. Not reached: the 2026 SICOV annex text (unreadable PDF) and the names of the operators.
challenge_sources: https://www.xataka.com.co/legislacion-y-derechos/todo-lo-que-debes-saber-sobre-sicov-el-nuevo-sistema-para-expedir-la-licencia-de-conduccion-en-colombia ; https://www.supertransporte.gov.co/documentos/2024/Mayo/Comunicaciones_27/Cartilla_para_Cea_y_aspirantes.pdf ; https://runt.gov.co/sites/default/files/Comunicado%20078%20de%202020.pdf ; https://www.runt.gov.co/sites/default/files/Comunicado%20031%20de%202024.pdf ; https://sidn.ramajudicial.gov.co/SIDN/PUBLICACIONES PERIODICAS/TEXTO COMPLETO Y TABLAS DE CONTENIDO/GACETA DEL CONGRESO/GACETA DEL CONGRESO 2024/GC 0229 DE 2024.PDF ; https://ambitojuridico.com/sites/default/files/BancoMedios/Archivos/comunicadoporinconsistenciasdealgunosceaentransicionalsistemadecontrolvigilanciausuariostendranrepetir-18.pdf ; https://www.supertransporte.gov.co/documentos/2026/Abril/Juridica_07/ANEXO_TECNICO_SICOV_CEA_CIA_OT.pdf ; https://www.appvizer.es/servicios/autoescuela ; https://anolla.com/es/software-para-instructores-de-conduccion

name: SISMED quarterly reporting workbench for independent drugstores (Circular 021/2026: CUFE per line, minimum dispensing unit, PISIS)
buyer: Independent drugstores (droguerías) and small pharmacy chains, plus small distributors, if they fall in Rol 2 (quarterly reporters)
trigger: CNPMDM Circular Externa 021 of 9 Jun 2026 (Diario Oficial 53.517) replaces Circulars 06/2018 and 17/2023. Rol 2 reports quarterly (Q3 window 1-31 Oct; Q4 window 1 Jan-15 Feb), only via PISIS, valid only when the second notification shows 100% loaded; invoices kept 3 years; SIC sanctions (Ley 1438/2011 art. 132). Draft circular (consultation Sep 2026) would extend the trial to 31 Dec 2026 and start mandatory use in Jan 2027.
reason: Duty is real: Circular 021/2026 (9 Jun 2026) sets quarterly Rol 2 reporting via PISIS (Q3 window 1-31 Oct), with CUFE per invoice line, minimum dispensing unit, 3-year invoice retention, and SIC sanctions (Ley 1438 art. 132). Not confirmed: that droguerías are Rol 2. The article defines Rol 2 only as "everyone else" and says sellers direct to the consumer need not report purchases, so retail drugstores may be only partly covered. The transition and trial period muddy the start date. Competition: SYAC's July 2026 bulletin shows POS vendors adding "Generar circular 021 2026", so the core job is likely built into the POS. Market: about 14,208 droguerías in 2003, and Coopidrogas alone has 10,007 affiliates. Weak standalone case.

name: Supervigilancia annual financial-report and SARLAFT compliance desk for small security firms
buyer: Small private-security, surveillance, advisory, training-school and armoured-vehicle firms supervised by Supervigilancia
trigger: Annual financial statements (plus REGADS, RIFINC for advisers) filed through the Supervigilancia web application each April (Res. 07657/2025: 1-30 Apr 2025; Decreto-Ley 356/1994 art. 105); SARLAFT 2.0 and transparency programme. April 2026: 240 sanction resolutions, over COP 9,000 million, for not filing 2023 statements; 30 April set to regularise; more sanctions announced.
duty: Annual financial statements filed through the Supervigilancia application each April (Decreto-Ley 356/1994 art. 105). SARLAFT 2.0 mandatory (Circular 245/275 of 2024). Sanctions are fines, as in the 240 resolutions of April 2026.
market: About 1,500 registered firms (Superintendent interview, Sept 2025), including about 438 in-house (autoprotection) schemes.
competitor: No third-party software found. The agency's own filing application exists. KPMG PTEE/SARLAFT consulting brochure for the security sector.
reason: The duty is real. Supervigilancia sanctioned 240 supervised firms (over COP 9,000M) for not filing 2023 financial statements (Asuntos Legales, April 2026). SARLAFT 2.0 is mandatory under Circular 245/275 of 2024. No third-party software for this was found, but I only ran 3 searches and did not open the sources. The market is small: about 1,500 registered firms, of which about 438 are in-house (autoprotection), so roughly 1,000 paying buyers. Filing is a once-a-year upload to the agency's own application, probably done by the accountant, so the pain and willingness to pay look low. SARLAFT and PTEE consulting from firms such as KPMG competes for the same budget. The 2026 window and the 2025 statements deadline were not checked.

name: LOFL / remisión de empresa forestal desk for sawmills, timber yards and wood traders
buyer: Sawmills (aserraderos), timber depots, wood traders and small wood-processing firms (carpentry, pallets) that hold or must open a Libro de Operaciones Forestales
trigger: Res. 1971/2019 (LOFL mandatory, registered only in the VITAL portal), Decreto 1076/2015 art. 2.2.1.1.11.1; REF transport remissions backed by LOFL inventory; SUNL (Res. 1909/2017); CAR follow-up visits; Circular 21022024E2019085 reiterated the duty; EPA Cartagena auto 000295 of 2026 requires registration from a trader. Offline fallback: written filing with form FT.0340.67.
reason: Duty is real. Res. 1971/2019 (changed by Res. 0200/2020) makes the LOFL mandatory, registered only in the state VITAL portal. It applies to firms listed in Decreto 1076/2015 art. 2.2.1.1.11.1. The state portal does the core job for free, and VITAL has a user manual (M-M-INA-01). I found no third-party software. A search snippet says CVC exempts secondary-transformation and commercialization firms from the online LOFL, but I could not read the PDF to confirm that; EPA Cartagena still requires a trader to register. So the buyer scope is unclear. Market size, penalties and enforcement frequency were not found. Willingness to pay is low, since a back-office would only sit on top of a free state tool. Fragmented regional authorities add to the difficulty.

name: Hass avocado producer and exporter ICA registry and quarterly phytosanitary report back-office
buyer: Hass avocado growers (lugares de producción), packers and small exporters registered with ICA; assistants técnicos who sign the reports
trigger: ICA Res. 824/2022 (mod. Res. 12482/2023 and 8996/2024): production-place, packer and exporter registration (2/5/10-year validity by crop cycle), quarterly informe fitosanitario (num. 13.1.6), SimplifICA GPX polygons matching registered area, SISPAP supplier letters, SISFITO HASS buffer-area surveys uploaded as PDF (circular 16 Jun 2026), lot data for Cuba circular of 8 May 2026 (ICA code, harvest date, volume, crates); ICA fined exporters and suspended a registration.
duty: I confirmed the duty in the compiled text of ICA Res. 824/2022, which is in force as modified (Res. 12482/2023 changed art. 22, then Res. 8996/2024 repealed that change and rewrote art. 22 par. 3). Registration validity: production places 2, 5 or 10 years by crop cycle (Hass is long-cycle, so 10); packers and exporters 10 years. Num. 13.1.6: the holder must report the informe fitosanitario, phenological stage, production volumes and monitoring of officially controlled pests in the first week of February, May, August and November (quarterly). Num. 13.2.6: the asistente técnico backs this with the quarterly report. Changes must be filed online within 10 working days (art. 11). Records move to the SimplifICA fresh-vegetables module. Penalties: fines under Ley 1955/2019 arts. 156-157 (art. 21), temporary inactivation (art. 18) and loss of registration (art. 12). In June 2022 ICA fined two Hass exporters COP 25.4M and 38.0M and suspended one exporter's registration. Res. 1507/2016 pest monitoring also feeds the quarterly report. I did not check the June 2026 SISFITO buffer circular or the May 2026 Cuba circular myself: one search snippet named the June 2026 circular, and I did not open either.
market: There is no official national count dated 2025. Partial figures: about 24,424 ha registered with ICA for export (article, year unclear); an older Agronegocios figure of 1,800 registered Hass farms on 12,200 ha; Portafolio quoting ICA on about 4,500 farms certified for export in Antioquia (2024), 2,049 of them Hass only; ICA monitors 600 Hass farms monthly for the US. The national total is probably several thousand registered production places, plus a few hundred packers and exporters and the agronomists who serve them. Hass exports in 2025 were USD 375M and 201,479 t (DIAN/Analdex).
competitor: I found no private software that prepares the 824 quarterly report, GPX polygons or SISPAP and SISFITO HASS submissions. The only software found was an academic web app from Universidad de Manizales (2024) for one farm. The state portals SimplifICA, SISPAP and SISFITO HASS are where data is filed, and ICA is pushing digital filing. They take the submission but do not seem to do the preparation (field monitoring records, consolidating data from many farms, formatting). I did not check generic farm-management or GlobalG.A.P. tools for ICA templates. Gobernación de Antioquia programmes (Agro Antioquia Exporta) and Corpohass give free help with registration, which competes with a done-for-you service.
killer: None found. Partial headwinds: official monthly surveillance is done by ICA, Corpohass and Asohofrucol under a funded agreement (3,444 monitoring visits a month over 15,000 ha), and the Antioquia government gives free registration help (Agro Antioquia Exporta). The 2022 ICA circular's quarterly report format is an Excel annex (the PDF is a scan and could not be read).
reason: The duty is real, recurring every quarter, and enforced with fines and suspensions. A registration being inactivated blocks export, so the pain is high. I found no product that does the job. The best buyers are asistentes técnicos and exporters who look after many supplier farms: they could pay for one tool covering many farms, and they can be reached through Corpohass and the mesas fitosanitarias. Risks: the ICA portals keep changing and absorb some of the work; free government and gremio support; small growers will not pay much; the national count is unclear; the formats come from the ICA manual and may change. A simple MVP is possible (monitoring app plus quarterly report and GPX export), but distribution is niche and B2B.
challenge_reason: I found no software, Corpohass tool, consultancy product or ICA feature that prepares the 824/2022 quarterly informe fitosanitario, GPX polygons or SISFITO HASS uploads. SimplifICA, SISPAP and SISFITO HASS only receive filings. A 2022 ICA circular sets an Excel annex as the report format. The market is real: about 24,400 ha are registered with ICA for export, and an ICA official cited 4,500 certified export predios in Antioquia (likely all crops). Fines and registration inactivation are enforced. Three things limit it. ICA, Corpohass and Asohofrucol run the monthly official surveillance under a funded agreement. Departments give free help with registration. The real buyer is the agronomist acting as technical assistant, and whether they will pay is unproven. Generic farm-management tools taught under a Tolima programme were not checked for ICA templates.

name: RNT renewal and quarterly Fontur contribution reminder-and-filing service for small lodging providers and short-term rentals
buyer: Small hotels, hostels, fincas and apartments with an RNT; each establishment files separately
trigger: Annual RNT renewal 1 Jan-31 Mar (automatic suspension from midnight 1 Apr, MinCIT notice 11 Feb 2026; Fontur arrears and commercial-registry renewal must be current); Fontur contribution 2.5 per mil of operating income, quarterly, Manual v2 in force 2 Jan 2026 (Decreto 1338/2021; Ley 2068/2020 art. 34); reactivation fine to Fontur 106.11 UVB (2025).
duty: Confirmed and in force. The RNT must be renewed every year between 1 Jan and 31 Mar (Decreto 1836/2021). If it is not, the registration is suspended automatically from midnight 1 Apr (MinCIT notice, 11 Feb 2026), and the provider cannot operate while suspended. Cámara de Comercio de Cartagena says reactivation requires paying 1 SMMLV to FONTUR. The claim's figure of 106.11 UVB was not verified. The renewal itself is free and done online through Confecámaras. The Fontur parafiscal contribution is 2.5 per mil of operating income, assessed quarterly over past periods (Decreto 1338/2021, art. 2.2.4.2.1.7 of Decreto 1074/2015). It must be filed and paid within the first 20 days of the month after the quarter; the 2022 Fontur ABC says 20 business days, so the exact wording is unclear. Late payment brings default interest and Estatuto Tributario penalties. Fontur Manual v2 (M-GCP-01) lists 2 Jan 2026 as its effective date. Not verified: any current size threshold or exemption for small providers. A 2019 Fiducoldex letter mentioned a 50 SMMLV sales threshold (outdated), and a 2025 Fontur notice titled 'finalización exención' could not be opened (HTTP 503). A MinCIT draft decree to reform the RNT (Dec 2025 / Jul 2026) may change these rules; its status was not confirmed.
market: La República (about 2024) reports 54,916 RNT registrations for vivienda turística, which it says is 57% of all tourism providers. That implies roughly 96k RNT holders in total, of which hotels are about 19% (around 18k). MinCIT reported about 62k registered providers in June 2022. Many are not current: a 2024 Riohacha study found only 43.6% of tourism firms had a renewed RNT. No official 2025 national figure was found.
competitor: Searches in Spanish found no Colombian software or service that automates RNT renewal reminders or Fontur filing. Free official channels already cover most of the job: the Confecámaras online RNT renewal (with manuals and videos), Fontur's own liquidation and payment platform (register each establishment once, then file and pay quarterly), and yearly campaigns by MinCIT and the chambers of commerce. Accountants likely handle Fontur filings for firms (not checked). Chekin and Stays cover only TRA/SIRE (K10). The gap is reminders, bundling with other tasks and filing on the client's behalf, not a missing tool.
killer: None found. The closest threats are the free tools that already do the job (Confecámaras RNT renewal and Fontur's liquidation and payment platform) and the very small levy, which limits willingness to pay.
reason: The duty is real, recurs every year and every quarter, and the suspension penalty has teeth. But the pain is low. The RNT renewal is free, online and a few minutes of form-filling. The Fontur contribution is tiny for small lodgings: 2.5 per mil of COP 60M a year is about COP 150k. A free Fontur portal already handles filing, and the state and the chambers of commerce send renewal reminders. Willingness to pay a separate tool will be weak. It works better as an add-on to a TRA/SIRE or vacation-rental compliance tool (K10 buyers) or as a cheap done-for-you service for Airbnb hosts. Distribution through host communities is possible. The market is large (about 55k vivienda turística RNTs). Unverified: whether a small-provider threshold or exemption applies, and the status of the RNT reform decree.
challenge_reason: Survives, but it is weak. Six Spanish searches found no software, PMS module, association tool or paid service that automates RNT renewal or Fontur filing, so nothing kills it outright. No small-firm exemption exists. Only PDET municipalities are exempt, and the 2023-24 RNT-based exemption ended in Q1 2025. Still, the free official tools do the core job: Confecámaras/RUES renewal, which is itself free, Fontur's own filing platform, and reminder campaigns from MinCIT and the chambers. The levy is tiny at 2.5 per mil, roughly COP 100k a year for a typical short-term rental, so willingness to pay is low. The market is large: about 55k vivienda-turística RNTs (La República, date of count unclear). A draft decree requiring one RNT per unit may help, but is not issued and would start 2028.

name: Private school and nursery tuition-regime and EVI reporting service
buyer: Private schools and jardines infantiles (Ley 115/1994 art. 202 regimes), thousands of small establishments
trigger: Annual EVI application (form 1 caracterización, form 2 financial report, autoevaluación) decides libertad regulada / vigilada / controlada; MinEducación Res. 019805/2025 (2026 increases 5.26-9.1%), Res. 020309 of 31 Jul 2026 (2027 parameters, not opened); secretariats issue per-school resolutions; Circular 002 of 8 Jan 2026.
duty: Ley 115/1994 art. 202 and Ley 715/2001 art. 5.12. MinEducación Res. 020309 of 31 Jul 2026 (in force from 1 Aug 2026, Diario Oficial 53.571; corrected by Res. 021581 of 6 Aug 2026) sets the 2027 tuition parameters. Maximum increases range from about 9.9% to 11.24% depending on regime (my sum of the IPC 6.14%, inclusion, teacher and permanence components). Every private preschool, básica, media and adult-education establishment must file an annual autoevaluación (Form 1A/1B/1C) and a financial and tariff report (Form 2) in EVI, using Guía 4 v11. Any establishment running more than one jornada files one form per jornada. The board (consejo directivo) must approve the self-assessment, cost study and tariffs over at least 2 sessions at least 3 days apart. The filing is due at least 60 days before enrolment. Penalty: a late report means classification in régimen controlado (art. 17 par. 1), plus a possible sanction procedure by the secretariat. Schools in controlado must file improvement plans. The 3.2% teacher-recognition component needs a contador or revisor fiscal certification through EVI. Secretariats issue a tariff resolution for each school (e.g. Magdalena Circular 33 of 3 Sep 2026 for 2027).
market: No current national total was found. Bogotá alone had 1,457 private schools in 2024 and 1,317 in 2025 (Portafolio, citing Sineb). Closures are significant nationally: about 1,943 private schools have closed since 2020 (La República) and 769 in 18 months (Portafolio/DUE), which points to a shrinking but still multi-thousand base (likely several thousand private schools and jardines nationally; not confirmed). The Javeriana LEE report and DANE C600 hold exact figures but were not opened.
competitor: The free MinEducación EVI application, with a help desk and online help, is the mandatory filing channel, so it is not a helper. There is also free ministry training ("Colegios de Avanzada", R.Ed. Privada). Searches found no commercial EVI pre-check, cost-study software or named consultancy. The search that named the school ERPs Phidias, Cibercolegios and Gnosoft returned no pages for them, so whether they have EVI or cost-study modules is unverified. Conaced, the private-school association, is active on EVI v11 problems and may advise its members (not confirmed). Accountants and revisores fiscales do part of the work.
reason: The duty is real and in force. Res. 020309 of 31 Jul 2026, corrected by Res. 021581, sets the 2027 regimes. EVI under Guía 4 v11 is mandatory. The board must approve over two sessions. The filing is due at least 60 days before enrolment. A late filing means automatic régimen controlado, which caps the increase about 1 point lower. A sanction procedure can follow. Pain is high: Conaced says v11 pushed about 80% of Bogotá self-assessed schools to controlado. No commercial EVI or cost-study tool or consultancy turned up, but school ERPs (Phidias, Cibercolegios, Gnosoft) returned no results, so that is not proven. Weaknesses: the filing is annual, EVI is free, and accountants or rectors do the work. A pre-check simulator for the regime score is a plausible MVP. Distribution through Conaced and the secretariats is possible.
challenge_reason: Nothing found kills it. Seven searches in Spanish turned up no commercial EVI helper, Excel simulator, cost-study tool or named consultancy; only ministry and secretaría documents came up. Phidias has treasury and administration modules, but no EVI module showed up. There is real pain: Conaced reported that about 80% of Bogotá schools that self-assessed under Guía 4 v11 dropped to régimen controlado, which suggests demand for a pre-check. Weaknesses: the free MEN EVI app is the required channel and has a help desk; the filing happens once a year; accountants already certify the financials; and the market is about 9,600 private schools (my estimate from the 2024 MEN bulletin), with many closing. Phidias and Gnosoft were not checked in depth, so either may have a module.

name: Habilitación and self-evaluation tracker for small IPS, consultorios, dental offices and labs (migration from Res. 3100/2019 to Res. 1732/2026)
buyer: Independent professionals, consultorios, small dental practices, small labs and small IPS (thousands), plus consultants who serve them
trigger: Res. 3100/2019 art. 5: annual self-evaluation and REPS declaration before renewal, and in year 4 of registration. Res. 1732 of 5 Aug 2026 gives existing providers 12 months to move to the new manual (Tomos I and II); failure to self-evaluate means inactivation of the service. Draft transitory resolution may add up to 6 months in earthquake-hit departments.
duty: Res. 3100/2019 art. 5, as modified by Res. 465/2025, remains in force. IPS, independent professionals, special patient transport and entities whose main business is not health must self-evaluate and declare in REPS before initial registration, before each annual renewal and in year 4 of registration. Per Cerlatam's summary of a draft rule, missing the self-evaluation can lead to inactivation; I did not confirm the penalty wording in the in-force text. Res. 1732/2026 (the new manual with a 12-month migration) was revoked by Res. 2080 of 8 Sep 2026 and never took effect because it was not published in the Diario Oficial. The draft transitory resolution on arts. 5 and 17 of Res. 3100 (the possible earthquake-zone extension) returned 404 on minsalud.gov.co, so whether it was issued is not_reached.
market: No national REPS total found. Bogotá in 2011 had 1,790 providers, of which 1,327 were independent professionals and 418 were IPS. A Bogotá notice cites more than 4,000 providers but has no visible date. UNIPS reports that 332 IPS closed in H1 2025, a sign of a financially stressed sector. Nationally the count is plausibly in the tens of thousands, mostly independent professionals, but this is unverified.
competitor: No dedicated commercial habilitación self-evaluation tracker found. The only results were a Medesk marketing guide, university web-app prototypes (UdeA 2025, UNAB 2023), the official REPS app (prestadores.minsalud.gov.co, a declaration form only) and secretaría guides. Colombian quality-management suites (Almera, Daruma, ISOlución and similar) were searched by name, but no habilitación-module evidence came back, so they are unverified, not ruled out. Consultants and course providers such as Polisura sell training and services.
reason: The migration trigger is refuted. Res. 2080 of 8 Sep 2026 revoked Res. 1732/2026 in full, including Tomos I and II. Imprenta Nacional certified on 3 Sep 2026 that 1732 was never published in the Diario Oficial, so it never took effect, and its 12-month transition is gone. Res. 3100/2019 still applies with its amendments up to Res. 465/2025. Under it, providers must still self-evaluate before the annual renewal and in year 4, then declare in REPS. That duty is real, but it is the long-running status quo with no deadline driving demand. No dedicated product was found, only Medesk content and university prototypes. Payers are thin and the rules are unstable. A tracker built only on Res. 3100 would be a weak, separate candidate.

name: Taxi company and owner back-office for Decreto 1001/2026 (tarjeta de operación on 2-year cycle, vinculación contracts, free monthly statement, desvinculación clock)
buyer: Taxi companies and cooperatives (many small ones), and their owner-affiliates
trigger: Decreto 1001 of 6 Aug 2026: free monthly statement of charges/payments per owner; vinculación contracts max 2 years; answer a change-of-company request in 15 business days; no fees for desvinculación, tarjeta or PUVO; tarjeta of 2 years; replacement window 5 years; theft paperwork within 6 months. Tarjeta issuance runs on HQ RUNT.
duty: Decreto 1001 de 2026 (signed 6 Aug 2026, amends Decreto 1079 de 2015), reported by Infobae, Noticias RCN, Blu Radio, El Espectador and Vanguardia, citing MinTransporte. Taxi companies must give each owner a free monthly statement of charges and payments by concept, keep vinculación contracts to 2 years or less, and answer change-of-company requests within 15 business days. They may not charge for desvinculación, the tarjeta de operación or PUVO. The tarjeta now lasts 2 years instead of 1, the replacement window is 5 years, and theft documents are due within 6 months. Not reached: the official Diario Oficial text, effective date, transition and the penalty for each breach. Earlier Decreto 1079 rules still apply: companies process tarjetas for owners free of charge, must file renewal at least 1 month before expiry, and return expired tarjetas within 10 days. Bogotá adds SIRC driver reporting.
market: I found no national count of taxi companies. MinTransporte counted about 252,819 taxis, apparently 2023 data (Portafolio). Bogotá has 52 to 77 habilitated companies depending on the article's date (El Tiempo). Barranquilla has 17 companies with 14,363 taxis (Portafolio). Nationally there are probably several hundred companies and cooperatives, plus tens of thousands of owner-affiliates. New taxi sales fell to 4,693 in 2025 (ANDI via Noticias RCN), so the sector is shrinking.
competitor: No Colombian product found for the owner-statement, vinculación and tarjeta-tracking job. TaxiCloud (dispatch, from USD 99 a month, operates in Colombia) only does dispatch and AI or WhatsApp booking. YourTaxi (UFPS Cúcuta) is an academic project. CityTaxi and Digi+ are dispatch or fleet-monitoring apps. Generic fleet ERPs are Spanish. There is no free state tool for owner statements; tarjetas run through local authorities and RUNT. Regional transport-accounting vendors were not checked in depth, so small local tools may exist.
killer: None found. The weak points are a small, concentrated buyer pool, revenue lost to the fee bans, and the chance that companies' existing accounting software already produces the monthly statement (not verified).
reason: Several outlets say Decreto 1001 of 6 Aug 2026 (it amends Decreto 1079/2015) makes taxi companies send owners a free monthly statement, caps vinculación contracts at 2 years, sets a 15-business-day reply on change-of-company requests, bans some fees and stretches the tarjeta to 2 years. I didn't reach the official text, effective date, transition or penalties. I found no Colombian product doing this; TaxiCloud only dispatches and YourTaxi is academic. Pain is moderate. The monthly statement is a real recurring job, but the tarjeta is now needed half as often, and the fee bans cut company revenue, so firms may pay less. There may be about 250k taxis, but I found no national company count. Mostly a statement and contract-tracking tool.
challenge_reason: I found no product, state tool or exemption that kills this. Spanish-language searches turned up only dispatch apps (TaxiCloud, Digi+, the Bogotá apps), ControlT (logistics), the academic YourTaxi project, and city registries. Bogotá's SDM web tool, which companies use to upload vehicles, owners and tarjetas de control, does not produce owner statements. Two things weaken the idea. The market is small and concentrated: about 57 companies in Bogotá (2018) and 17 in Barranquilla with about 14,363 taxis, so maybe a few hundred buyers nationally. The decree also bans fees for desvinculación, tarjeta and PUVO, which cuts company revenue. The monthly statement is close to what ordinary accounting already produces (not verified). Effective date and transition are still not found; El Espectador gives neither.

name: Ley Kiara (Ley 2480/2025) pet-service registry and compliance kit
buyer: Veterinary clinics, dog daycares/hotels, grooming and spa shops, trainers, dog walkers (up to 8 dogs per walker)
trigger: Ley 2480 of 16 July 2025: Chamber of Commerce registration (except natural-person walkers), registration on MinAmbiente platform with municipal verification, CCTV required, no overnight stay in grooming, fines 5-20 smmlv. Press says obligatory from January 2027; regulatory decree not found.
duty: Ley 2480 of 16 July 2025 (in force on publication) covers daycares, hotels, training centres, grooming and spa, dog walkers, pet transport and vet clinics that offer these services (Art. 2, Art. 20). Chamber of Commerce registration is required except for natural-person walkers (Art. 4). Providers must register on a platform run by MinAmbiente, which the public can search (Art. 5). Daycares and hotels have 22 requirements (Art. 7), including a behavioural exam on file, health certificates valid for up to 6 months, a per-animal file with vaccination and deworming records, and CCTV. Grooming requires recorded CCTV and no overnight stays (Art. 8). Walkers are limited to 8 dogs (Art. 9). A contract is required (Art. 11), and so is an urgent search plan for lost or escaped animals (Art. 16). Municipalities verify compliance (Art. 12). Sanctions are a warning, suspension, closure, removal from the registry, or a fine of 5 to 20 SMMLV (Art. 13). The technical regulation is due within 18 months, about January 2027 (Art. 4), and existing providers have 2 years to comply, until July 2027 (Art. 21). The law sets no periodic filing frequency. Searches found no regulatory decree, draft for consultation, or live platform as of October 2026.
market: I found no national count of covered providers. Bogotá had 308 establishments under CIIU 9609 (animal care) in 2019. The Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá puts the whole pet sector at about 34,000 linked firms (2026), but that includes trade and food. The national target group is probably a few thousand to low tens of thousands, many of them informal walkers. This is an estimate, not a register figure.
competitor: I found no dedicated Ley Kiara compliance product in Colombia. Generic international pet daycare and grooming software already covers booking, pet profiles and vaccination tracking: Anolla (Spanish, has a vaccination control module), Gingr, DaySmart Pet, Revelation Pets, Groomsoft/Pawfinity, EasyWeek and Koalendar. The state's MinAmbiente platform will handle the registration itself once it exists (not yet found). Colombian vet practice software was not checked individually.
killer: No single killer. Partial overlap comes from generic vet and daycare software: Okvet (described as free), Recorvet (Colombian, with a daycare module) and Anolla. The future MinAmbiente state platform will do the registration itself. Registration happens once, with no renewal in the law. The regulation is still not issued, and the transition runs to about July 2027.
reason: Ley 2480/2025 is in force. The MinAmbiente technical regulation is due by about January 2027 (Art. 4) and existing providers must comply by July 2027 (Art. 21), so many small firms must act around the same deadline. The platform registration itself looks one-off. The recurring work is the per-animal file required by the law: behavioural exam, vaccination evidence, health certificates valid for at most 6 months, contracts, an urgent search plan for escapes (PBU), and CCTV. Fines are 5 to 20 SMMLV, plus closure or removal from the registry. I found no Colombia-specific Ley Kiara tool. Generic pet booking software (Anolla, Gingr, DaySmart, Groomsoft) partly covers records. The decree and the platform could not be found, so the content is uncertain. Buyers are fragmented, have little money and are not counted.
challenge_reason: Nothing kills it outright, but it is weaker than claimed. The law text requires a single registration on the MinAmbiente platform, with no renewal period in the text. I found no sign the platform or the technical regulation exists yet; the regulation is due within 18 months (about January 2027). Existing providers have two years to comply, to about July 2027 (Art. 21). The recurring duties are per-animal files with vaccination records, contracts, behavioral exams, CCTV and annual staff training. Generic vet and daycare software already covers much of this: Okvet (described as free), Recorvet (Colombian, has a daycare module) and Anolla. Municipalities enforce and must correct before sanctioning, so enforcement looks soft. The best fit is a registration-prep and checklist kit, which is thin and mostly one-off.

name: Annual lift (transporte vertical) certificate and maintenance tracker for building administrators
buyer: Propiedad horizontal administrators and building owners in Bogota, Cali, Bucaramanga and other cities
trigger: Municipal acuerdos: Bogota Acuerdo 470/2011 + Decreto 663/2011 (IDIGER verifies, local mayor fines/seals), Cali Acuerdo 450/2018, Bucaramanga Acuerdo 48/2018; annual revision by ONAC-accredited body, certificate displayed, NTC 5926-1 and separate maintenance schedule.
duty: Real and in force. Bogotá Acuerdo 470/2011, implemented by Decreto 663/2011, requires owners and administrators of lifts, escalators, platforms and electric doors to have a general revision at least once a year. The revision must be done by a body accredited by ONAC (Colombia's national accreditation body) against the relevant NTC standard, such as NTC 5926-1, and the certificate must be displayed next to the equipment. The certificate does not replace preventive maintenance. IDIGER (Bogotá's risk-management agency) checks the certificate, the annual preventive-maintenance schedule, the maintenance reports and the repair procedure, and can make surprise visits. When a building fails, IDIGER notifies the local mayor's office, which can seal the equipment or fine the owner under Acuerdo 79/2003. Owners must also register their systems and upload certificates on sire.gov.co/stv. Cali Acuerdo 0450/2018 and Decreto 0137/2019 set the same annual ONAC-accredited revision and displayed certificate, verified by the Secretaría de Gestión del Riesgo. I only found Cali's rules in 2019 press coverage and did not confirm they are unchanged. Bucaramanga Acuerdo 48/2018 was not checked (not_reached). Frequency: an annual certificate plus ongoing, usually monthly, maintenance.
market: IDIGER verified 6,893 systems at 1,953 buildings between 1 Jan and 9 Sep 2024, including 4,349 lifts. The total number of registered lifts in Bogotá was not found. The open dataset "Sistema de Transporte Vertical 2016 al 30-06-2025" was not downloaded. A rough estimate is a few thousand to around ten thousand lift-equipped buildings in Bogotá, plus Cali, Medellín and Bucaramanga. Many of these are run by professional administrators who manage several buildings each. Lift maintenance costs about COP 0.5 to 1.5 million per month and is the largest PH expense after security (Portafolio).
competitor: I found no software built for PH administrators to track lift certificates and maintenance. The two PH suites I checked do not show this. Propiedata's homepage lists assemblies, admin platform, resident app, virtual intercom and access control, with no maintenance or certificate module. ComunidadFeliz, launched in Colombia in July 2025, only claims to help "coordinate maintenance", with no equipment register or expiry alerts described. Other things partly cover the job. IDIGER's free SIRE STV portal is where certificates get registered and stored in Bogotá. The ONAC-accredited inspection bodies and the lift maintenance contractors already handle the yearly reminder and the monthly service paperwork. Generic maintenance-management (CMMS) tools were not checked. Domus and Admin PH returned no results.
reason: The duty is real, and sealing or fines are a credible threat. But it is one certificate a year per building, and the ONAC inspection body and the lift maintenance contractor already remind the administrator and produce the paperwork. In Bogotá, IDIGER's free SIRE portal already stores certificates. That leaves a thin reminder and document-tracker layer, and any PH suite such as ComunidadFeliz or Propiedata could add it cheaply. Willingness to pay for a standalone tool looks low. The buyers are reachable through the administrator associations and the many administrators managing several buildings, but the tool probably works better as a feature or add-on than as a product. It could also be sold to inspection bodies and maintenance contractors as their client portal, which is a different buyer.

name: Notary SIPLAFT / UIAF compliance back-office (ROS, quarterly RON, annual manual update)
buyer: Colombian notarías (about 900 offices, each an individual notary) and possibly real-estate agents
trigger: Supernotariado Circular 051/2025: ROS immediately and no later than 8 calendar days after the alert; quarterly RON as a flat file (389-position record) via UIAF SIREL, due in the last 15 days of the month after the cut-off (2013 annex, may be outdated); SIPLAFT updated at least annually or when the notary changes (CIR 206/2024); Coordinator SIPLAFT credentials requested by the notary.
reason: The duty is real. Notaries must run SIPLAFT, file ROS and the quarterly RON (389-position flat file via SIREL, due in the last 15 days of the month after quarter end), and file negative reports. Circulars 051/2025 and 206/2024 add handover and annual-update rules. About 920 notarías exist (SNR figures for 2024-25). I found no dedicated notary SIPLAFT product, but searches were thin. The 2013 annex was the only one found. The market is small: about 920 buyers, each a regulated notary with an existing SIN system and in-house compliance staff. The RON file is likely generated by notarial software already, and ROS is manual in SIREL. Real-estate agents were not checked. The score is low because of the small market, probable incumbent coverage and unverified willingness to pay.

name: Smart-tachograph compliance and archiving kit for small van operators (2.5 to 3.5 t, cross-border)
buyer: Austrian sole-trader and micro Kleintransporteure and courier or craft-delivery firms using vans over 2.5 t abroad (WKO Fachgruppe Gueterbefoerderung; counts not verified)
trigger: EU Mobility Package: from 1 Jul 2026 vans and combinations over 2.5 t on cross-border or cabotage trips need a G2V2 smart tachograph, company card, regular downloads (driver card 28 days, vehicle unit 90 days), archiving and documented driver training; domestic use under 3.5 t keeps the Lenkprotokoll. Federal rules (GGBG/EU 561/2006 and 165/2014); WKO leaflets.
duty: Real and in force under EU law that applies directly in Austria (Reg. 165/2014, 561/2006, Mobility Package 2020/1054-1055). Since 1 Jul 2026, vans and combinations over 2.5 t up to 3.5 t used for commercial cross-border transport or cabotage must have a Smart Tacho 2. This covers existing and new vehicles. Purely non-commercial transport is exempt, and the Art. 3 craftsman exemption applies. WKO Wien and WKO OOe (page dated 19.03.2026) tell firms to obtain a company card and arrange download and correct archiving. According to the search summary of WKO NOe, retention is 24 months under § 17b AZG. I did not open that page. The 28-day driver card and 90-day vehicle unit download intervals come only from vendor material (Samsara). Penalties: the search summaries mention fines and possible loss of Zuverlaessigkeit (business reliability). I could not read the exact penalty text, because the WKO PDFs did not parse. I did not check enforcement after 1 Jul 2026 (not_reached).
market: I found no count of cross-border Kleintransporteure with a Gemeinschaftslizenz (the EU community licence, marked "<= 3,5 t" for these firms). WKO 'Verkehrswirtschaft in Zahlen' lists 13,313 active members in the whole Gueterbefoerderungsgewerbe (2024), and most of them are not affected. Only vans used commercially across borders or for cabotage are covered, and craftsman-exempt firms drop out. The affected group is probably a few thousand firms at most; this is unverified.
competitor: The core download-and-archive job is already covered. VDO, now AUMOVIO Trading Austria in Vienna, supplied the slides for the WKO Kleintransporteure webinars and runs the VDO Fleet cloud portal (fleet.vdo.at). Smart Tacho 2 units can download data over Bluetooth through the VDO Fleet app, and the service includes legal archiving. One UK reseller lists auto-download at about GBP 3.50 per vehicle per month; that is not an Austrian price. Other products that do the same job and sell across the EU: Webfleet (remote download plus archive as standard), Frotcom (certified local partners), HUSS Tacho-Fernauslesen, Tachomatik LEA, Descartes/VDO DLK Pro, ZF TX-BOX 2, and Samsara, which markets directly on the 2026 2.5 t rule. Tachograph workshops that fit the units also sell readers and software. I found no Austrian-only micro bundle, but because the rules come from the EU, a German-speaking EU product already does the whole job for an Austrian firm.
reason: The duty is real and recurring: driver card and vehicle unit downloads, plus archiving, probably for 24 months under AZG. It is mandatory, and loss of reliability is at stake. But the core job is already handled by the tachograph makers' own clouds. VDO Fleet, run by AUMOVIO Trading Austria, which presented at the WKO webinars, works through Bluetooth and an app. Webfleet, Frotcom, HUSS, Tachomatik and Samsara also cover it, all sold EU-wide in German at low per-vehicle monthly prices, and fitting workshops bundle them at installation. The buyer pool is small: cross-border van operators only, an unknown share of 13,313 Gueterbefoerderung members, with exemptions. Willingness to pay beyond what the workshop bundles in is low. A founder would need a distinct angle, such as an infringement and training workflow, to stand out.

name: Donor-data transmission and compliance helper for small donation-eligible associations
buyer: Small spendenbeguenstigte Vereine, parishes, foundations, volunteer-run charities that raise donations (count not verified)
trigger: Federal EStG par. 18 and BMF rules: annual donor totals with encrypted vbPK SA sent through FinanzOnline by end of February; Spend 1 approval and Spend 2 for service providers; annual continuation report within 9 months of year-end filed by a tax adviser or auditor since 2025; VerG 2002 accounting statements.
reason: Duty is real: since 2017 donation-eligible bodies must send annual per-donor totals with vbPK SA via FinanzOnline by end of February (BMF). Since 2025, donation status needs an annual report within 9 months, filed by a tax adviser or auditor. Market: about 1,500 listed bodies in 2022 (excluding fire brigades), with roughly 45,000 more able to apply after the 2024 reform; the real count is unconfirmed. Competition: the free FinanzOnline dialog suits small volumes, and the BMF gives the data-stream spec to all developers. I found no named Austrian vendor, but I didn't check CRMs. Willingness to pay is weak: the manual route is free, the adviser step can't be automated, and the buyer is volunteer-run. The niche is narrow and seasonal. Penalty is unclear: a 20% surcharge appears only in fire-brigade guidance.

name: EU AMLR (10 Jul 2027) cash-cap and ID-check pack for jewellers, gold buyers, watch and art dealers
buyer: Small jewellers, gold buyers (Ankauf), watch, antique and art dealers; registered trades under WKO Handel Juwelen, Uhren, Kunst, Antiquitaeten (counts not verified)
trigger: Existing: par. 365m ff GewO (risk assessment, customer due diligence, suspicious-activity reports via goAML, supervision by Gewerbebehoerden). New: Reg. (EU) 2024/1624 applies from 10 Jul 2027 with EUR 10,000 cash cap on all traders and ID checks from EUR 3,000 for occasional cash payments; Austria may set lower limits (unverified).
reason: Duty is real: GewO par. 365m ff obliges jewellers, precious-metal and art dealers to run risk assessments, ID checks, staff training and goAML reports, with fines reported up to EUR 5m (par. 366b, from a secondary calculator site). AMLR 2024/1624 applies directly from 10 Jul 2027 (EUR 3,000 ID threshold, EUR 10,000 cash cap). No Austria-specific tool found, and WKO supplies free leaflets and risk forms. Weak case: tiny, fragmented segment, the trigger is largely a one-off, firm counts are unverified, and the Austrian cash-cap rule is unclear. I did not check whether Austria sets a lower cap. The software would mostly be a purchase log plus ID capture.

name: Annual inspection manager (Pruefbefund register) for small workshops under the Arbeitsmittelverordnung
buyer: Small garages, workshops, retailers and craft firms with vehicle lifts, tail lifts, powered gates, mobile cranes, ladders (employers with staff)
trigger: Federal AM-VO par. 6 ff.: recurring inspection of listed work equipment at least yearly (max 15 months), written Pruefbefund, defects block use; external body at least every 4 years for some equipment.
duty: Confirmed, Austrian federal law in force. AM-VO (BGBl. II 164/2000 as amended, RIS) § 8(1): listed equipment, including Fahrzeughebebühnen, cranes, hoists and powered gates, must have a recurring inspection at least once per calendar year and no more than 15 months apart. § 8(7): equipment unused for more than 15 months must be inspected before its next use. § 11: a written Prüfbefund is required (date, inspector, signature, result, scope) and must be kept until the equipment is retired. The duty correction: the recurring inspection is in § 8, not § 6/§ 7. § 7 covers the acceptance inspection. Recurring inspections may be done by 'sonstige geeignete fachkundige Personen' (WKO Merkblatt). Sanctions fall under the ASchG administrative penalties. I did not open the penalty amounts this session.
market: Bundesinnung Fahrzeugtechnik (WKO statistics, 15.04.2026): 9,811 members and about 26,000 employees. An older WKO page says about 7,220 businesses. This covers vehicle repairers, body shops, tyre specialists and painters. Many are EPU without staff, so they would not carry the employer duty. Other trades with powered gates or tail lifts would widen the market, but I did not quantify them.
competitor: TÜV AUSTRIA 'inspect by tami' portal: manages Prüfobjekte, organises inspection dates and avoids missed deadlines. The basic version is free for TÜV AUSTRIA customers. The page does not mention reminders or Prüfbefund storage. Generic DACH Prüffristen/Arbeitsmittelprüfung software is widely available, with automatic interval reminders and mobile digital test protocols: Softguide lists many vendors, and there is WEKA 'Arbeitsmittel plus'. The DEKRA service portal shows next-due dates per device, but it is German. Inspectors themselves (TÜV, Ziviltechniker, lift service firms) typically schedule the annual visits. I found no Austria-specific AM-VO Prüfbuch app for small workshops, but the core job of tracking deadlines and storing reports is already covered by free inspector portals and existing software.
reason: The duty is real, yearly, and clearly mandatory for vehicle lifts, cranes and gates under AM-VO § 8 and § 11. But the pain is low. A small workshop has a handful of devices, and the inspector (TÜV, a lift service firm, a Ziviltechniker) usually starts the annual visit and issues the Prüfbefund. TÜV AUSTRIA's tami Inspect already tracks deadlines for free for its customers, and many DACH Prüffristen tools do reminders and digital protocols. Willingness to pay for a register of 2-5 devices is minimal. A better angle might be selling to the small inspection firms rather than the workshops, but I did not check that here. Market: about 7,200-9,800 Fahrzeugtechnik members, many without staff.

name: Tageseltern / childminder association billing and care-agreement kit
buyer: Tageselternvereine and individual Tageseltern (Tagesmuetter and Tagesvaeter), plus small private providers
trigger: Landes childcare laws and funding rules: written care agreement per child, BH permit, hours-based Land subsidy claims (NOe online claim form with uploaded agreement; Kaernten quarterly settlement; Tirol Verwendungsnachweis; Steiermark per care hour).
reason: Duty is real but Land-specific. Care agreements, permits and hours-based subsidy claims are set by Land rules (NÖ, Kärnten, Tirol, Salzburg, Steiermark). I did not open the legal texts, so frequency and penalties are unverified. Three German-language searches found no Austrian Tageseltern software, only German Kita tools (winKITA, KAI) and generic English Kita software. The NÖ Trägerförderung PDF lists the data fields passed to the Gemeinde, so a MVP is simple. The market is small and shrinking: about 8,700 children were in Tageseltern care in 2022, down from 11,100 in 2018, and the number of providers is unverified. Most providers are Vereine such as Hilfswerk, Caritas and Volkshilfe, who may use in-house systems (not checked). Nine different Land formats raise the build cost. Buyers are few and probably have little money to spend.

name: Hausapotheke dispensing-record tool for vets (TAMG par. 68, ABO par. 60a)
buyer: Vets running a Hausapotheke
trigger: TAMG par. 68 and ABO par. 60a: dispensing and goods-in records kept 7 years, authority access, electronic interface for reportable data.
duty: TAMG §68 dispensing records, 7-year retention, authority access; no penalty found
market: about 3,100 to 3,175 vets (2017); about 1,400 with a Hausapotheke (older, undated study)
competitor: Vet practice management software; Excel/Word per Tierärztekammer
reason: The duty is real. The USP page says vets with a Hausapotheke must document trade in veterinary medicines, keep records 7 years, delete them within 30 years, and give authorities data in writing on request. I found no penalty on that page. The Tierärztekammer infosheet (2018, not re-checked for currency) says electronic Hausapotheke records have been required since 2019. It also says the ABO does not prescribe a form, so Excel or Word suffices, delivery notes saved on the PC can serve as goods-in records, and "no separate software is needed". USP describes no electronic reporting interface, only written provision on request. Vet practice software already covers this, and I did not name a specific Austrian vendor. Market: about 3,100 to 3,175 vets in 2017. An older, undated study puts about 1,400 with a Hausapotheke. Weak willingness to pay and a free workaround make this a low score.

name: Wahlarzt digitalisation kit: WAHonline fee notes, e-Wahlpartner/e-card, ELGA and e-Impfpass for small elective-doctor practices
buyer: Wahlärzte (private doctors without a full insurer contract) and other elective practices, especially solo practices with under 300 patients a year or with only basic software
trigger: Ärztegesetz 49 Abs 7: electronic fee-note filing (WAHonline) to insurers since 1 Jul 2024; e-card infrastructure, ELGA eBefund/eMedikation and e-Impfpass via e-Wahlpartner since 1 Jan 2026; patients must be told of any exemption; coded diagnosis and service documentation pending (pilot ended 30 Jun 2026, current status unchecked). Federal law, Ärztekammer circulars.
duty: The duty is real, in force and Austrian. Since 1 Jul 2024, Wahlärzte must send paid fee notes electronically to the insurers through WAHonline. Since 1 Jan 2026 they must use the e-card system through e-Wahlpartner to check identity and card validity, and to confirm the patient contact for ELGA eBefund/eMedikation and the eImpfpass. Since 1 Jul 2026 they must code every outpatient contact with at least one ICD-10 diagnosis, plus services. These codes go through e-Wahlpartner each quarter, with deadlines such as 31 Aug for Q2. The pilot ran until 30 Jun 2026. On 11 Dec 2025 the Nationalrat postponed the coding duty and passed an exemption for Wahlärzte with fewer than 300 different patients a year. The same threshold applies to WAHonline and to e-card/ELGA. Legal bases: the Vereinbarungsumsetzungsgesetz 2024 (BGBl. I 191/2023), the Dokumentationsgesetz and the GD-VO (BGBl. II 367/2024). Penalties: a Gesundheit Österreich FAQ (Dec 2025), written for outpatient clinics (Ambulatorien), says breaches can be fined as administrative offences under ÄrzteG §199(3), and may also be disciplinary offences under §136. The FAQ does not say this outright for Wahlärzte. I found no evidence that fines have been imposed since July 2026.
market: I could not find a 2025 count of Wahlärzte. The Ärztekammer statistics for 31 Dec 2025 put total doctors at about 53,353 and report growth among Wahlärzte. A 2020-era report gave 10,578 Wahlärzte. I found no figure for how many are above the 300-patient threshold or lack software with these modules (not reached). Physiotherapists, masseurs and other therapists can also use WAHonline (WKO and Physio Austria material), but I did not check whether it is mandatory for them.
competitor: The core job is already covered. e-Wahlpartner can be used through practice software or through the e-card web interface, which is the state's free route, according to the Ärztekammer Wien. WAHonline modules are offered by practice-software vendors such as Offisy and appointmed (whose help pages describe WAHonline submission). appointmed links to docsy for e-card and ELGA. LATIDO says it covers the mandatory functions in an integrated workflow. Kutschera's ganyMED sells an ICD-10/SNOMED coding module. The ÖGK subsidises the WAHonline software extension with EUR 300 or 500 under certain conditions. Any new product needs a GIN line from one of five network operators, ÖGK approval, and an implementation of the DVSV interface, which is a barrier to entry. The claim targets the smallest practices (under 300 patients a year), but those are exempt from all three duties, so the gap left over is small.
reason: The duties are real, recur every quarter and carry penalties. But the target buyer, small practices with under 300 patients a year, is exempt from all three duties by law since Dec 2025. Practices above the threshold are already served by established vendors (LATIDO, Offisy, appointmed with docsy, ganyMED) with integrated WAHonline, e-Wahlpartner and ICD-10 modules, partly subsidised by the ÖGK. A free e-card web interface also covers e-Wahlpartner. A solo founder would need a GIN connection, ÖGK approval and an implementation of the DVSV e-Wahlpartner interface. Those are heavy barriers for an MVP. A lightweight ICD-10 coding helper or onboarding service is possible, but the margin is thin.

name: Kellerbuch and wine-report pack for small Austrian wine estates and traders
buyer: Winegrowers who bottle or sell wine, wine traders and Sensale (brokers); a large share are small family estates (count unverified)
