trigger: Federal Weingesetz s31: Ein- und Ausgangsbücher (Kellerbuch) kept continuously up to date for inspection by the Bundeskellereiinspektion; no small-firm relief; separate harvest, production and stock reports (Wein-Online) and vineyard register changes via eAMA/INVEKOS GIS.
duty: The duty is real and in force. Under Austrian federal law (§ 31 Weingesetz 2009), anyone who places wine on the market, including winegrowers, wine traders and Sensale (brokers), must keep input and output books, known as the Kellerbuch. The books must be "ständig aktuell" (kept up to date at all times) so the Bundeskellereiinspektion can inspect them, and there is no small-firm exemption. USP, the government business portal, says accounting documents can count as records. It does not say the books must be electronic, and no approval scheme for software was found. Separate reports go through Wein-Online, the ministry's free wine database. The harvest and production report (as of 30 Nov) is due by 15 Dec. The stock report (as of 31 Jul) is due by 15 Aug. Filing electronically is compulsory above 3,000 litres. Smaller producers may still file with the municipality. Wine traders must file the master-data sheet electronically. The penalty for breaking § 31 was not reached; the Weingesetz has a penalties section, but I did not read its wording.
market: No current count was found. A parliamentary answer gives 24,682 businesses with vineyards in 2005, of which 19,834 had under 3 ha. Another answer says 5,193 businesses applied for the state test number in 2010, which is a rough proxy for those that bottle and sell. The 2020 Weingartengrunderhebung (Statistik Austria's vineyard survey) gives 46,165 ha, but the business count was not shown in the page text. A realistic market of businesses that bottle, trade or broker wine is probably about 4,000 to 6,000. That figure is an estimate.
competitor: BOXXER VINO (Medialine) sells a digital Kellerbuch that records inflows and outflows, enrichments, bottlings and weight adjustments. I could not confirm whether it is aimed at Austria or exports to Wein-Online; its page loaded as an unreadable PDF. I found no Austrian Weinbauverband or Landwirtschaftskammer tool and no Austrian approval scheme, and no evidence that any product links the Kellerbuch to Wein-Online. Wein-Online itself is free but only takes the reports; it is not a Kellerbuch. 360Winery is listed on Capterra but is English-only. My vendor search was limited (three searches), so local Austrian vendors I missed may exist. Fraund and mbs were not rechecked.
killer: Small producers are exempt under the Kellerbuchverordnung (BGBl. II 149/2005). Since 2006, a Kleinerzeuger (at most 100,000 l of wine made per year) no longer has to keep running stock accounts. For them the Kellerbuch is essentially a collection of receipts plus a wine-treatment sheet and a list of containers. This contradicts the claim of "no small-firm relief". The reports go through the free state portal Wein-Online, and BOXXER VINO (Medialine) already sells a digital Kellerbuch.
reason: The duty is real and continuous, with no small-firm relief, and I found no Austria-specific tool that combines the Kellerbuch with Wein-Online. But a paper or Excel Kellerbuch seems to be accepted, inspections are occasional, and the yearly reports go through a free state portal. Pain and willingness to pay are therefore moderate. The market is small, about 5,000 bottling estates. Many are part-time and price-sensitive, but they can be reached through the Weinbauverband, the Landwirtschaftskammer and the trade magazine DER WINZER. A minimal product (a Kellerbuch ledger plus pre-filled report figures) is simple to build, but there is no Wein-Online API, so the reports cannot be submitted automatically. German vendors with full winery suites could localise for Austria. The opportunity is real but niche.
challenge_reason: The claim says there is "no small-firm relief". A commentary in the Linde-Verlag LINDA database, citing the Kellerbuchverordnung, says otherwise. Since 2006, winegrowers making at most 100,000 l a year have not had to keep running stock accounts. Their Kellerbuch is a "Sammelmappe": receipts, a wine-treatment sheet and a container list. That covers most Austrian family estates, so the core pain falls away for the very buyers this idea targets. The yearly stock and harvest reports are web forms in Wein-Online, which is free. Larger cellars and traders still need full books, but BOXXER VINO already serves them with a digital Kellerbuch. What is left is small: larger estates, traders and brokers. I found no Wein-Online interface for third-party software, so a niche link to it remains unverified.

name: Grain stock reporting (Getreidemeldung) for small mills and farm-trade firms
buyer: Small mills, grain traders and processors under 500 t a year, plus larger Agrarhandel firms with weekly/monthly reports
trigger: Agrarmarkttransparenzverordnung (BGBl. II 312/2021, EU 2017/1185): weekly report due Tuesday of the following week, monthly report due the 15th of the second following month, annual report by end of February, via eAMA with the AMA Formblatt.
reason: The duty is real. USP lists grain stock reports by firms buying, processing or reselling grain: monthly at 500 t/yr or more, annual below that. Weekly reports are due Tuesday, monthly on the 15th of the second following month, annual by end of February. The reporting happens in a free AMA web form, entered after requesting a PIN. The page names no penalty and no fees. The weekly and price reports apply only to large firms (mills over 10,000 t, first buyers at 2% of a state's volume), which are out of scope. Small firms file a simple form once a month or once a year. No third-party software turned up, but there is little to sell: a tiny, low-pain market with a free state tool. Reporter count not found. The AMA PDF was unreadable, so any file-import option is unchecked.

name: Baurestmassenmeldung and demolition notice helper (Land waste laws)
buyer: Small demolition and building firms and private builders
trigger: Recycling-Baustoffverordnung BGBl. II 181/2015 and Land waste laws (for example OÖ AWG 2009 s21): demolition notice, Rückbaukonzept at 750 t or more, Land-law Baurestmassenmeldung, 7-year record keeping.
reason: Duty is real. Under § 21 Oö. AWG 2009 the Bauherrschaft must report type, quantity and fate of demolition waste to the Bezirksabfallverband after demolition (BAV forms; Linz AG sheet mentions a 100 t threshold). Records are kept 7 years. The Recycling-Baustoffverordnung requires a Rückbaukonzept above 750 t. The duty is one-off per demolition, not recurring, and rules differ by Land. It is paper-form and BAV-based, and I found no software or online portal. The market is small and fragmented, with no register count found. It overlaps K06 (eADok) only on the waste-record side. Low frequency and low willingness to pay keep the score down. Penalties were not verified.

name: ZWR dealer workflow and 2026 Waffengesetz compliance kit for Waffenhändler and Büchsenmacher (Wartefrist tracker, essential-part back-registration, SchKG marking deadline, ammo-buyer entitlement check)
buyer: Licensed Waffenhändler and Büchsenmacher (reglementierte Waffengewerbe); number unverified, likely a few hundred
trigger: Waffengesetz-Novelle 2025 in force 28 Apr 2026 (WaffG §62 Abs 23): all private transfers must run through a dealer who verifies buyer and Wartefrist and does the ZWR entry; 4-week Wartefrist since 1 Nov 2025; essential parts registered via dealers by 28 Apr 2027; SchKG marking by 28 Oct 2026; ammunition entitlement checks. Federal law, BMI ZWR.
duty: WaffG as amended by the 2025 Novelle (BGBl. I 56/2025), fully in force since 28 Apr 2026 (§62 Abs 23). The 4-week Wartefrist for a buyer's first gun in a category has applied since 1 Nov 2025. Private transfers must go through a licensed dealer, who checks ID, entitlement and the Wartefrist and makes the ZWR entry. Ammunition may only be sold to entitled buyers (WBK, Waffenpass, Jagdkarte or a ZWR extract). The SchKG marking deadline is 28 Oct 2026, done by authorised dealers. Dealers must register Kat. C essential parts by 28 Apr 2027. A Waffenbücherverordnung (dealer record books) exists. Penalties: up to EUR 5,000 (EUR 7,000 for repeat offences) for unauthorised possession; dealer-specific sanctions were not checked. This is per-transaction work for dealers, plus one-off deadline waves.
market: About 500 gun dealers, from an undated Austrian Standards business plan that postdates the 2019 Novelle. RUAG Ammotec Austria says it supplies about 200 specialist dealers. Büchsenmacher are mostly micro and small firms, many clustered in Ferlach. I did not get an exact count from GISA or WKO.
competitor: The free official ZWR web application, accessed through USP, is used by hand. The regulation (§10) requires dealers to connect to the ZWR via USP, and I found no public API or batch interface. The WKO ARGE Zivile Sicherheit offers free guides and ZWR training. I found no Austrian Waffenhandel ERP or POS that links to ZWR. German products such as TTE WM-intern serve Germany's NWR and XWaffe, not the Austrian ZWR. Whether Austrian dealers use generic ERPs with weapon modules is unverified.
reason: The duty is real. Since 28 Apr 2026 all private gun sales must go through a dealer, who checks the buyer and the 4-week Wartefrist and makes the ZWR entry. SchKG marking is due by 28 Oct 2026 and essential parts must be registered by 28 Apr 2027. I found no Austrian dealer software. But the WKO guide and the access regulation (§10) describe only manual entry through USP, with no API or batch import, so the core ZWR step cannot be automated. A tool could only track Wartefristen, deadlines and the Waffenbuch alongside ZWR. The market is tiny, about 500 shops, many of them micro-firms. The WKO ARGE already trains dealers and publishes free guides. This suits a niche add-on, not a business you can grow.

name: Almobmann Auftriebsliste collector for sheep and goat Almen (collect lists from sending farms, validate ear tags, submit by 15 Jul)
buyer: Almbewirtschafter and Almobleute of Almen and Gemeinschaftsweiden with sheep or goats; count unverified
trigger: AMA Almauftriebsliste for breeding ewes and goats due 15 Jul 2026 with per-animal ear-tag data, plus 7-day per-animal reports; Almobmann must combine lists from all sending farms. Federal AMA / ÖPUL.
reason: Duty is real (AMA Merkblatt 2026): ear-tag-based Auftriebsliste for ewes/goats by 15.07.2026, 7-day reporting, active Abtrieb report in eAMA, 60-day minimum; filed by Bewirtschafter or Almobmann; late fix only via MFA correction. But AMA's own eAMA already is the filing channel, and no private competitor was found. Market is small: about 8,000+ Almen, mostly mixed cattle/sheep, with few pure sheep/goat Almen (about 115k sheep, 12k goats overall). Annual single-use, volunteer buyers, low willingness to pay, and eAMA free. Weak business. Could not read PDF text; relied on the search summary of it. Exact Alm count and import features unchecked.

name: Electronic plant-protection-product use records for farmers (professional users)
buyer: Farms and growers that use PPPs professionally, mostly small and family farms, via LLKC and agri-input shops
trigger: EU Reg. 1107/2009 art. 67 with Implementing Reg. 2023/564: format and content apply from 1 Jan 2026; VAAD presentation says machine-readable recording is mandatory for professional users from 1 Jan 2027. Records kept 3 years. Current Latvian rule is a registration journal with field-level records.
duty: Confirmed and in force as directly applicable EU law. Under Reg. 1107/2009 art. 67 and Implementing Reg. 2023/564 (applies from 1 Jan 2026), professional users must keep PPP use records electronically in a machine-readable format, create each record without undue delay and transfer paper records within 30 days. Implementing Reg. 2025/2203 (OJ 3 Nov 2025) lets Member States exempt uses before 1 Jan 2027 from the electronic-transfer step, which fits the claim's VAAD 2027 date. Whether Latvia actually used this option is not confirmed: the VAAD PDF could not be read. Neither regulation requires sending records to authorities; records must be kept and shown on inspection. The Latvian national rule (MK Nr. 950) already requires a registration journal kept for 3 years. The penalty amount was not checked.
market: Not reached. No register count of professional PPP users was found. One VAAD document mentions about 2100 professional-user (class 2) certificates, but it is unclear whether that is an annual figure or a total. Latvia has tens of thousands of farms, but the number using class 1/2 PPPs professionally was not verified.
competitor: Free state tool: the VAAD/ZM LIZ farm-management system (liz.vaad.gov.lv). A ZM presentation describes it as covering planning, recording, registers and a warehouse, with records of PPPs, fertilisers and all field activities (GPS). It is aimed squarely at the electronic PPP and fertiliser field-use duty. Private: eAgronom (Estonian, E-Agronom OU, hiring a Latvian marketing specialist, more than 1M ha managed) is active in Latvia, but whether it has a spray log was not confirmed this session. International farm-management systems (xFarm, Cropwise, etc.) were not checked. Two Latvian-language searches for a local private app found nothing.
reason: The duty is real. EU Reg. 2023/564 requires machine-readable PPP use records from 2026, and Member States may defer the transfer step to 2027. But the state already offers LIZ for free, and it is designed for exactly this: field-level electronic records of PPP and fertiliser use, already used by thousands of subsidy claimants. Regional farm-management players such as eAgronom are present in Latvia. There is no reporting step to automate, because records are only kept for inspection, so the willingness to pay is low. The buyers are small, often elderly farmers, reachable through LLKC. A niche of a simpler mobile front end or a done-for-you service for farmers who don't use LIZ might exist, but it is thin. Latvia's use of the 2027 deferral and the Latvian market size were not verified.

name: PPP distributor and licensed sales-point annual data submission
buyer: Small agri-input shops and distributors of plant protection products
trigger: Amendments approved by Cabinet (September): import data submitted electronically and distribution data via machine-readable form or upload to the Crop Monitoring State Information System from 1 Jan 2027.
reason: The duty is real. PPP distributors must report to the state Crop Monitoring information system. Monthly data on class 1-3 sales to professional users and licensed outlets is due, with an annual 1 April report on class 3 sales to non-professionals. Electronic import and distribution submission applies from 1 Jan 2027 (Cabinet amendments to Reg. 949). The state system itself offers a machine-readable form and file upload, so the free state tool covers the core job. Distributors will usually export from their own ERP or stock system. Penalties and the exact file format were not found. The market is niche (probably tens to low hundreds of licensed distributors and outlets; no count found). Many sales-point data requirements are being removed. Thin converter, small market: low score.

name: Septic hauler (asenizators) annual volume reports and municipal register compliance
buyer: Small septic and waste-water hauling firms, plus municipal water utilities that keep the registers
trigger: MK Reg. 384 item 10.3: haulers submit data on volumes collected and discharged to the register keeper by 1 March each year; municipal binding rules renewed in 2025 (Madona 30 Oct 2025, Adazi Reg. 3/2025, Jelgava Dec 2025) with haulers' registration and minimum emptying frequency.
reason: Duty is real. MK Reg. 384 (27 Jun 2017, in force, amended 2019) item 10.3 requires haulers to give the register keeper, by 1 March each year, the volumes collected and discharged. Municipalities register haulers, and the municipality or its water utility keeps the register. Penalties come from municipal binding rules, e.g. Jelgava novads: a warning or a fine of up to 100 units for individuals and 300 for companies. Jelgava already runs a free municipal e-log (dks.jelgava.lv) with GPS. The market is fragmented across about 43 municipalities, each with its own rules. Hauler count was not found. Annual, low-frequency and low-value, so the score is low. Not checked: commercial competitor software.

name: Licensed staffing-agency compliance kit (NVA licence, third-country worker secondment)
buyer: The 395 NVA-licensed placement agencies, mainly small, that second third-country workers to user firms
trigger: NVA licence (MK Reg. 458, fee 500 EUR, 3 years); the new Immigration Law and MK Reg. 564 amendments (in force 10 Jul 2026) widen employer involvement in compliance; permits issued 2025: 22,917.
reason: Licence duty is real (NVA licence, MK Reg. 458, 395 licensed agencies as of Jan 2026 per search summary), and the Reg. 564 amendments took effect 10 Jul 2026. But I found no concrete recurring reporting duty on agencies. The ifinanses article was paywalled and listed no obligations or penalties. Enforcement stories are about leasing of third-country workers. A licence is renewed every 3 years, so the workflow is infrequent. The buyer pool is about 395 firms, which is small. I did not search directly for competing software, and I did not check overlap with K03. The pain is mostly in permit and immigration filings, which the state handles. Score stays low.

name: Veterinary practice medicine-stock and prescription records
buyer: Small veterinary practices
trigger: The regulation on vet practices (likumi.lv/ta/id/333186) requires a stock system covering purchase, use, dispensing, transfers and destruction, with the responsible vet logging batch, expiry and supplier; status in force not confirmed.
reason: The duty is real. Cabinet Regulation No. 337 (7 June 2022) is in force. It requires a traceable stock record covering batch, expiry, supplier, use, dispensing and destruction, kept 5 years. The record is the responsible vet's job, with no fixed filing frequency. But the state's free eVETIS system (PVD) gives each vet a profile for recording all medicine use and auto-fills data from registers. Per a lvportals article on the December 2025 amendments, clinics no longer need a separate register. Clinics can also connect their own software via PVD. That is a free state tool covering the core job, so a paid product has little room. Market size not found. Booking software such as Anolla exists, but it is not compliance software.

name: Building water-system risk assessment (Legionella and lead) for small commercial premises
buyer: Small hotels, care homes and other commercial buildings, and small water suppliers
trigger: Directive 2020/2184 transposition: new Latvian drinking water rules; draft LBN 221-15 amendment for building water-system risk assessment; some transition dates 2026 and 2029.
reason: The duty exists but is much narrower than claimed. MK Regulation 547 (26.09.2023) makes the building internal water-network risk assessment mandatory only for "priority premises": inpatient healthcare institutions and social care institutions with accommodation. Hotels are not covered, and other buildings are voluntary. The deadline is 12 Jan 2029, with review every 6 years and a report to the Health Inspectorate within 3 months. The lead limit drops to 5 µg/l by 2036. Penalties were not found in the text I read. The buyer pool is a few hundred institutions, many of them large or state-run. BIOR offers a free risk-assessment template, and the Health Inspectorate has guidance. I found no Latvian software, but the market is tiny and one-off.

name: Foreigner-declaration and guest-data tool for guest houses, small hotels and short-term rentals
buyer: Guest houses, small hotels, rural tourism farms and private short-term-rental hosts (natural persons included). Count of hosts unverified; the Tourism Law change brings holiday homes and flats in.
trigger: Tourism Law amendments (Saeima 11 Jun 2026; effective 10 Jul or 12 Sep 2026 per different sources) plus MK Reg. 518 of 1 Sep 2026 amending Reg. 226 on the foreigner declaration (in force 12 Sep 2026): providers must have each foreign guest complete and sign the declaration with ID shown, check it against the travel document, keep it 1 year and hand it over to State Police, Border Guard or State Security Service on request. Electronic preparation and remote ID are allowed.
duty: Cabinet Regulation No. 226 (2007), consolidated version of 12.09.2026 as amended by Reg. 518 of 01.09.2026, which follows Tourism Law amendments in force 10.07.2026. Every tourist accommodation provider, legal or natural person and now including short-term rentals, must give each foreign guest the declaration form in Latvian and at least one foreign language. The guest fills it in and signs it in person after showing a travel document. The provider checks it against the document, signs to accept it if it is on paper, keeps it for 1 year, and hands it over immediately when the State Police, Border Guard or State Security Service asks; in emergencies the request can be oral. Electronic preparation is allowed (point 5), and ID can be verified with recognised online means. Points 13 and 15 and Annex 3 were deleted, and there is no routine electronic reporting to the police or any state system. Penalty, per a search summary of the Tourism Law amendment text (Art. 19, not opened directly): a warning or a fine of up to 86 fine units for natural persons and up to 156 for legal persons, with the State Police handling cases. The duty recurs with every foreign guest. Effective dates reconciled: the Tourism Law amendments took effect 10.07.2026 and the regulation amendments 12.09.2026.
market: Not found. The CSP's monthly survey compiled data for 1048 accommodations in October 2025 (a reporting sample, not the full stock). Latvian accommodations had 2.8 million guests in 2025, 59.3% of them foreign (1.7 million). I found no count of short-term-rental or Airbnb hosts, and no host register. The amendments let municipalities set rules for recording accommodations, so local registers may appear.
competitor: No Latvian product or state portal found that produces the declaration. The state offers only Ministry of Economics guidelines and a paper form. The electronic travel declaration at eta.gov.lv is filed by certain third-country travellers before entry, not by hosts, so it does not do this job. A Latvian-language search for PMS software turned up only generic booking software (Anolla) and a local hotel group's own booking system (rixwell.com), with no declaration feature mentioned. Generic online check-in tools (Eurotel, Avirato, Civitfun) exist. Whether Chekin, Mews, Cloudbeds or Clock PMS support the Latvian form was not checked (not_reached). Because nothing is filed with the state, any e-signature check-in tool with a configurable form could meet the duty, so competition risk is high.
killer: None found. The main risks: no state filing is needed, so a paper form or generic e-sign tool is enough; fines only come on inspection; and multi-country check-in tools (Chekin, Check-in Scan) could add a configurable Latvian form.
reason: The duty is real and in force. Regulation 226 has applied to hotels since 2007, so it is not new for them. What changed in 2026: short-term rentals and private hosts are now covered, and providers may prepare the form electronically and verify ID remotely. Penalties are a warning or a fine of up to 86 units for individuals and 156 units for companies. The pain is small: nothing is filed with the state, the provider only keeps each form for a year and hands it over on request, so a paper pad still complies. I found no Latvian tool, but global online check-in and PMS vendors could easily add a Latvian form. That I did not verify. The host count was not found. The best wedge is Airbnb hosts newly covered. Willingness to pay is likely low.
challenge_reason: I found no product that kills it. No Latvian tool or state e-service produces the declaration. Chekin's published list of countries it is legally compliant in (18) leaves out the Baltic states. Check-in Scan covers only Spain, Portugal, Croatia and Italy. The duty is real: Tourism Law Art. 11(7) covers natural persons too, and Art. 19 sets fines of up to 86 fine units (natural persons) or 156 (legal persons), with no exemption for EU guests. But the case stays weak. Nothing has to be filed with the state, so a paper form or any generic e-sign check-in tool meets the duty. Fines only follow an inspection or a request. The market is small: statistics covered about 1,060 to 1,340 registered sites, plus an unknown number of private hosts (2.05M platform-booked nights in 2025). Some Riga hosts already collect passport photos online. Latvian PMS vendors and Mews or Cloudbeds add-ons were not checked.

name: Packaging recyclable/non-recyclable split and quarterly natural resource tax return for small producers and importers
buyer: Small producers and importers who put packaged goods on the market and are not in a producer-responsibility scheme
trigger: Natural Resources Tax Law and MK Reg. 480 (amended 17 Oct 2024): recyclable/non-recyclable split; rates 0.80 and 1.25 EUR/kg since 1 Jul 2024; quarterly return to VID by the 20th of the following month (from a Finance Ministry opinion, not the law).
reason: The duty is real. Under the Natural Resources Tax Law, the first seller of packaged goods in Latvia pays tax on packaging. Quarterly returns go to VID by the 20th of the following month. A VID notice gives rates of 0.80 and 1.25 EUR/kg for the unrecycled quantity from 1 Jul 2024. Penalties are double rate for non-compliance and loss of exemption. However, the exemption route kills much of the market. Firms that contract with a packaging operator (e.g. Zaļā josta) pay no tax, and 300 kg/year of packaging waste forces scheme membership. Only non-members file returns, and no figure exists for how many. I found no dedicated software, but I did not search vendors in depth. The claim's quarterly 20th deadline and Reg. 480 amendment date were not checked against the law text (Section 27 and Annex 7 were not in the fetched part). Market size and 2026 form changes are unverified. This is a low-value niche.

name: Monaco SCP/SCI and small-entity transparency calendar (annual confirmation, responsible person, shareholder register, BO changes)
buyer: Administrators and owners of Monaco civil real-estate companies (SCP/SCI), plus the domiciliation firms, fiduciaries and notaries that run many of them
trigger: Law 1.550 of 10 Aug 2023 + SO 10.117: annual confirmation of activity within the month after the registration anniversary (EUR 25 for a SC, form via Mon Entreprise portal), designation of responsible person for basic and BO information (resident, Monaco account), shareholder register, any change declared within 30 days, 10-year accounting retention. Extra annual duty under Loi 1.381: any entity holding Monaco real-estate rights declares change or no change of beneficial owner to the Direction des Services Fiscaux (window 1 Jul-30 Sep in 2025; form 353-0046_01-2011).
duty: Law 1.550 of 10 Aug 2023, amending Law 797 art. 6-7: annual confirmation within one month after the registration anniversary, fee EUR 25 (SC) or 50 (SA), filed with the RCI. Penalty: formal notice, automatic strike-off after one more month, possible art. 12 administrative fines, double fee to re-register. Also: name a person responsible for basic and BO information within one month of registration, declare BO changes within 30 days, keep records 10 years. Loi 1.381: yearly change/no-change BO declaration to the DSF for entities holding Monaco real-estate rights, filed through an approved agent (KPMG). 2025 window was 1 Jul-30 Sep. A false no-change declaration costs 10% of the property's market value; late payment costs 0.8%/month. 2026 window not verified.
market: Not found: no figure for SCPs on the Registre Spécial (IMSEE search failed). The OECD June 2026 report cites 97.9% legal-person compliance as of Oct 2025 but no count was reached (fetch returned 403). For context, Monaco has about 6,305 employers (IMSEE 2025). Likely a few thousand SCPs, mostly run by a small number of fiduciaries (unverified).
competitor: No SaaS calendar or register tool for Monaco SCPs found in French searches. The work is done as a service by fiduciaries and agents (Valeri Agency, Rosemont, KPMG, CMS, Square Services). Filing goes through the state Mon Entreprise portal and paper forms. For Loi 1.381, an approved agent must file, which pushes the work toward professionals.
reason: The duty is real and in force. Since Law 1.550 (effective 25 Sep 2023), each SCP must file an annual confirmation within a month of its registration anniversary, paying EUR 25 or 50. If it doesn't file, it gets a formal notice, is struck off one month later, may be fined, and pays a double fee to re-register. Loi 1.381 adds a yearly beneficial-owner declaration for entities holding Monaco property (1 Jul-30 Sep in 2025; 2026 dates not checked), and it must go through an approved agent. That means the buyers are mostly a handful of fiduciaries and law firms that already do this work as a paid service. No Monaco-specific SaaS was found. The market is tiny (SCP count not found) and filing frequency is low, so willingness to pay for a tool is doubtful.

name: Volunteer-syndic / small co-ownership accounting and compliance tool for Monaco (Law 1.329 as amended, Bill 1117)
buyer: Syndics of small copropriétés (volunteer syndics and small professional syndics authorised under Law 1.252)
trigger: Law 1.329 of 8 Jan 2007 as amended by Law 1.531 of 29 Jul 2022 (agenda cut-off, works-estimate threshold); Bill 1117 (government filed Oct 2025; CMS May 2026 summary) would require a dedicated bank account in the syndicate's name for all syndics, restructure Article 21 around accounting, archiving and online access to management documents
reason: Law 1.329 of 2007 (amended 2022) is in force. Syndics must keep co-ownership accounts, and professional syndics need Law 1.252 authorisation. Bill 1117 is NOT yet law. CMS (15 May 2026) says it still needs a public-session vote, with proposed entry into force 1 July 2027. Its main change is a dedicated or sub-account bank account for all syndics. That is a bank task, not a software workflow. No Monaco-specific competitor found; only French SaaS (Matera, Simplesyndic at 3 EUR/lot/month), and I did not check their Monaco compatibility. No market count found; the Monaco plan comptable was not checked. The market is tiny and the buyers are mostly professional syndics. Volunteer syndics are hard to reach and pay little. There is no recurring filing to an authority, so the duty is weak.

name: Foreign-contractor site and posting authorisation pack for Monaco works (DDE, Service de l'Emploi, CCPB professional cards)
buyer: French and Italian building SMEs and sole traders working on Monaco sites, and their Monaco principals/site managers
trigger: Foreign companies need a site authorisation (autorisation d'exercer) plus a posting authorisation for work over 48h, then the Caisse des Congés Payés du Bâtiment issues a carte professionnelle du bâtiment per worker; DPAE, minimum wage, working time apply; non-compliance can lead to a ban (CMS, 8 Oct 2025)
duty: DDE site authorisation, Service de l'Emploi posting authorisation, CCPB professional card per worker; per project over 48h; sanctions up to a ban
market: not quantified (no register or statistic found)
competitor: monentreprise.gouv.mc (state portal: site authorisation, posting teleservice); no commercial software found
reason: The duty is real: CMS says foreign firms need a DDE site authorisation (work over 48h), a Service de l'Emploi posting authorisation per employee, and a CCPB professional card. Sanctions are administrative and criminal, up to a ban. The official monentreprise.gouv.mc portal already covers site authorisation and posting, with a teleservice for short postings. No dedicated commercial software turned up, but I ran only two calls. Weak points are that it is episodic per project, not clearly recurring, and the buyers are scattered foreign SMEs. Many use accountants or admin staff. Authorisation lead times are reportedly 4-5 weeks. CCPB fees, the document list and market size were not found.

name: C02 Jeweller AML and hallmark-declaration file (precious-metals dealers)
buyer: Independent jewellers and gold buyers (registered with customs/ADII as covered entities under law 12-18)
trigger: Law 12-18 (dahir 1-21-56, 8 June 2021): client identification above 150,000 MAD (sources disagree on whether this applies to all transactions or only cash), 10-year record keeping, suspicious-transaction reports to ANRF, ADII registration. Plus D19 hallmark declaration now via the customs Badr system since 2023-2024.
duty: Real and in force. Under law 43-05 as amended by law 12-18, precious-metal and stone dealers, including jewellers, are covered entities supervised by ADII (customs). They must run internal controls, identify the client (and record the beneficial owner) for cash operations above 150,000 MAD, and file a suspicious-transaction report with ANRF whenever they doubt where the funds came from or who the client is. Le360 (26 March 2023) and the ADII awareness coverage both say the 150,000 MAD threshold applies to cash operations only, which settles the claim's open question. Clients' ID documents must be kept for 10 years, but this comes from search summaries that were cut off and is not checked against the official text. Dealers had to register with customs offices, including the hallmark (garantie) offices, by 31 Dec 2022 after one extension. Separately, Article 188 of the customs code requires a prior declaration (D19) before gold, silver or platinum pieces are displayed or sold. Since 1 Jan 2024 the D19 is filed electronically in the customs Badr system before the piece goes to the hallmark office. Penalty amounts were not found.
market: No register count found. Le360 says the sector has more than 40,000 direct jobs but gives no source. The federation president (Medias24, July 2025) calls the sector informal since 1990, and federation members put margins at 2-5% under squeezed demand. The number of shops registered with ADII is not public in the sources I reached.
competitor: No Morocco-specific tool for the AML register or for D19 preparation was found in French or Arabic searches. Only generic jewellery stock and till software turned up: JewelMate and Capterra/appvizer listings, plus Sofisoft in Casablanca, a retail software maker with no jewellery compliance module that I could see. The D19 itself is filed in the free state Badr system, so the filing step is already covered by the state. Software could only help prepare it, for example by tracking each piece's weight and purity. I did not check whether ANRF uses goAML or offers a free reporting front end (not reached).
reason: The duty is real, but the paid opportunity is weak. Client identification is only required for cash deals above 150,000 MAD, which is rare for a typical shop, and suspicious-transaction reports are occasional. The recurring D19 filing already runs on the free customs Badr system. Buyers are mostly informal, cash-based, low-margin family shops (2-5% margins, by the federation's account), and the federation says it struggles even to get answers from the authorities. No local competitor was found, but that probably reflects weak demand rather than an open gap. A weight-and-purity stock tool that also fills in D19 data could be sold through the federation, but it would be a jewellery ERP, which comes close to the excluded generic-tool category. Shop counts are unverified.

name: C01 Hearse and funeral-transport operator compliance kit (new 2025/26 arrêtés)
buyer: Funeral-transport and funeral-service firms (one press article cites about 3,000 funeral firms, undated)
trigger: Arrêtés 1250.25 and 1251.25 (May 2025, published BO 12 Feb 2026) replacing the 1970 decree: mandatory refrigeration, biosecurity, exhumation rules, neutral vehicle livery; a complementary arrêté on religious inscriptions is pending. Municipal specifications in Casablanca and Marrakech add contractor rules.
reason: The arrêtés exist. Medias24 and Le Matin report 1250.25 and 1251.25 (May 2025, published in the BO on 12 Feb 2026), replacing the 1970 decree. They require refrigeration, biosecurity and exhumation rules, and restrict vehicle markings. A follow-up arrêté, 442.26 (BO 7486, 26 Feb 2026), restored religious formulas, so the "pending complementary arrêté" is already published. No source shows a register, certificate or periodic filing, and no compliance deadline or penalty turned up. The duty looks like a one-off vehicle and health fit-out, not a recurring workflow software could serve. I found no Moroccan funeral software, but I did only one search for it, and that returned only French and Swiss results. I did not fetch the BO text. Firm count is unverified (the "3,000" is an undated press figure). The buyers are fragmented, informal operators, which makes sales hard.

name: C04 Household-employer (domestic worker) contract and CNSS file service
buyer: Households employing domestic workers
trigger: Law 19-12 (written contract in 3 copies, one deposited with the labour inspectorate), CNSS affiliation file within 1 month, end-of-contract declaration (form 325-1-15); decree 2.18.686.
reason: Duty is real: Law 19.12 (in force 2 Oct 2018) requires a written contract in 3 copies with signatures legalised, one filed with the labour inspectorate. Decree 2.18.686 makes CNSS registration mandatory (since June/July 2020) within one month. Changes must be reported within a month. Enforcement is by complaint or inspection report, then CNSS acts ex officio. I found no penalty detail. No competing software or done-for-you service turned up, and I found no online CNSS service (early reports said the employer must go in person). Compliance is very low: 2,228 declared by Sept 2020, under 5,000 by Nov 2021. That means weak pressure, a one-off event per worker, and low willingness to pay. The household count was not found. No 2025-26 update was found; the 16-18 transition may have ended 2025.

name: C13 Digital tachograph compliance for small hauliers
buyer: Small goods hauliers (over 3.5 t) and coach operators
trigger: Tachograph mandatory for goods vehicles over 3.5 t and passenger vehicles over 9 seats (arrêté 2720-10); driving-time data retention; employer-paid professional driver card training (law 52-05). May 2026 ministry-CDG agreement for a state integrated digital platform including a digital tachograph.
reason: The duty looks real: maroctl.com says the tachograph is mandatory for goods vehicles over 3.5 t and passenger vehicles over 9 seats, under arrêté 2720-10 (BO 5958, July 2011). Another maroctl page cites arrêté 2399-20 for the digital tachograph. I could not read the official texts. I found no Moroccan download interval or penalty. A cabinet CMS page mentions penal sanctions, but I did not open it. The state-CDG platform (14 May 2026 agreement) is a direct risk, with no rollout date found. The Medias24 page returned 403, so its details are secondhand. Only foreign vendors (Geotab, SOLID, VDO) appeared, with no Moroccan product. No market count found. Buyers are fragmented, enforcement is unclear and the state platform is coming, so the score stays low.

name: Auto-entrepreneur / street-vendor quarterly declarations
buyer: Auto-entrepreneurs and street vendors
trigger: Online registration on ae.gov.ma, quarterly declarations; thresholds and rates conflict between low-quality sources (500,000 or 2,000,000 MAD).
reason: The duty is real. Auto-entrepreneurs must file a quarterly turnover declaration, including a nil return, and pay the flat tax (0.5% for commerce, 1% for services) on the state portal ae.gov.ma. Searches suggest ceilings of 500,000 MAD for commerce and 200,000 MAD for services. Reported penalties are a 1,000 MAD fine per missed return and 10% for late payment. These come from secondary guides; I did not open the official portal or the legal text. Refuted as a new product idea because the state portal already does the core job: login, new declaration, automatic tax calculation, online payment. The task also puts this in the known K09 space (rejected), and the claim calls it generic accounting, which is out of scope. The filing is trivial and the buyers have low willingness to pay. The only possible angle is the e-invoicing deadline of 1 Jan 2027, which Inyad says applies to auto-entrepreneurs above 500,000 MAD and still needs an implementing decree. I did not check market size, which the claim puts at about 380,000 registrants.

name: Syndic Accounts Pack: standard chart of accounts, budget and AG annexes for co-ownership syndics (decree 2.23.700)
buyer: Professional syndic firms and owner-run syndic offices managing co-ownerships; budgets over 200,000 MAD must apply the full chart, over 1 million MAD need certified accounts
trigger: Decree 2.23.700 standard chart of accounts and size-tiered annexes for co-ownership syndicates
duty: Decree no. 2.23.700 sets the accounting rules for co-owners' syndicates under law 18-00, art. 24 as amended by 106-12. It is dated 22 Rajab 1446 (about 23 Jan 2025) and was published in BO no. 7391 (1 Chaoual 1446 / 31 Mar 2025). It applies from the start of the financial year after publication, so effectively FY2026 for calendar-year syndicates. Duties: a standard chart of accounts, a standard budget, annual financial statements and annexes for the AG, and 5-year archive retention. Thresholds are tiered. The final Arabic text reportedly uses 200,000 and 500,000 MAD of annual revenue: syndicates at 500,000 MAD or more must prepare annexes 3-10. The 2023 draft and press used 200k/1M MAD, with certification above 1M. The PDF could not be machine-read, so check the exact thresholds and any certification rule. Law 30-24 changed conciliation, AG convening and the notification of minutes, not the accounting thresholds. No specific penalty found (not_reached).
market: Not reached. I found no register count of professional syndics, AMCOP membership or number of syndicates. The AMCOP quoted in the press says syndicates use a mix of software, Excel or handwritten records. Thaïs alone covers about 10,000 co-owners.
competitor: Syndic Connect (Marrakech, web and mobile platform for professional and volunteer syndics, launched 2020). The Thaïs syndic app (online payment of charges, about 70 residences). K Syndic. Kolonell (custom builds at 180k-450k MAD). Copriciel (French, configurable for Morocco). I found no evidence that any of them implements the decree 2.23.700 chart or annexes, so this is unverified, not proven absent. No free state tool was found.
killer: None found. Possible substitutes: accountants using generic Moroccan accounting software or Excel templates, and no visible enforcement. I found no syndic tool that claims to comply with decree 2.23.700, but this is unverified (no vendor demos checked).
reason: The duty is real and in force. Decree 2.23.700 (dated 22 Rajab 1446, about 23 Jan 2025) was published in BO no. 7391 on 31 Mar 2025 and applies from the first financial year after publication. It sets a standard chart of accounts, a budget model, annexes and 5-year archives, with annual accounts for the AG. The claim's thresholds come from the 2023 draft: the final text appears to use 200k and 500k MAD of revenue (annexes 3-10 at 500k MAD or more), so check those. Moroccan syndic software exists (Syndic Connect, Thaïs, K Syndic, Kolonell custom builds), but I found no evidence that any of them produces the decree's statements, which leaves an add-on or white-label gap. Risks: many volunteer syndics run on Excel, buyers are fragmented, and incumbents could add the chart.
challenge_reason: I found no Moroccan syndic software that shows it implements the decree 2.23.700 chart and annexes. Syndic Connect, Thaïs, K Syndic and Kolonell are all general management tools or custom builds, and no free state tool turned up. The duty is real. The decree is dated 23 January 2025 and adala already held a copy in April 2025. It applies from the fiscal year after publication, probably 2026, though I could not verify the Bulletin officiel issue. The claim's thresholds are out of date: the decree text puts unions at 200k-500k MAD on annexes 10-12 and those at 500k MAD or more on annexes 3-10. The 200k/1M figures come from the 2023 draft and the CNC opinion. Enforcement looks weak, many syndics are volunteers, and accountants on generic software can substitute.

name: Radiology and Dental X-ray Authorisation and Radiation-Protection File (AMSSNuR)
buyer: Private radiology cabinets, dental surgeries with X-ray, small clinics and veterinary practices with X-ray equipment
trigger: AMSSNuR authorisation, PCR designation, worker classification and dosimetry for X-ray users under law 142-12
duty: Prior AMSSNuR authorisation is required to use radiology equipment (conventional, interventional, dental) under law 142-12, decree 2.20.131 (in force; category II authorisations and declarations, with a renewal procedure) and decree 2.23.151 on protecting workers and the public (reported in force in AMSSNuR's July-December 2023 review). The D-3 form asks for the authorised physicians, a medical physics lead and the clinic's operating licence number. Validity period, renewal frequency and penalties: unverifiable, because the decree text and the forms returned 403 when fetched. PCR, dosimetry and worker-classification specifics for Morocco: not confirmed.
market: AMSSNuR issued 967 authorisations in 2018, 69% of them medical, per press reports quoting the director (old figure). AMSSNuR has inspected about 344 facilities and activities. I found no current count of private radiology or dental X-ray users. Public-sector figures show 402 radiologists and 458 dentists in public service; private dentists number in the thousands, but I did not verify a figure. The radiologists' federation (FNRIM) says many dentists and other specialists operate X-ray equipment without authorisation, and art. 101 of law 142-12 restricts radiology to radiologists.
competitor: No Moroccan software or done-for-you service found. AMSSNuR provides only downloadable Word forms, with no e-filing for radiology authorisations. Only source imports run online, through PortNet-SIGAM. Medical physics and radiation-protection consultants probably do this work informally, but I did not verify that. Two searches checked for vendors, and neither found one.
reason: The duty is real. AMSSNuR form D-3 covers conventional, interventional and dental radiology (intraoral, panoramic, CBCT). It offers new, modification and renewal applications, and it cites law 142-12, decree 2.20.131 (2021), decree 2.23.151 on worker protection and decree 2-97-132. I found no software or online portal for X-ray authorisation; only PortNet-SIGAM, for source imports, is digital. Frequency is the weak point: these are one-off or renewal filings, and I could not find the validity period. The buyer pool is small: 967 authorisations in 2018, 69% of them medical. The dental side is legally contested, since art. 101 limits radiology to radiologists. Dosimetry providers and PCR duties were not confirmed. It works better as a consultancy service than as SaaS.

name: Cooperative Annual Tele-declaration and Compliance Pack for small cooperatives (ODCO, law 112-12)
buyer: Small agricultural, artisan and women's cooperatives (about 65,000 to 69,000 registered), their presidents and the accountants or federations that serve them
trigger: ODCO tele-declaration from June 2026 and scoring-based controls
duty: Partly confirmed. Law 112-12 (Dahir 1-14-189, in force since 31 Dec 2019 after law 74-16 extended the deadlines) requires an annual ordinary AG no later than six months after year-end, plus bookkeeping. Under art. 72, an auditor is needed when turnover exceeds 10 MDH for two years in a row. ODCO (infomediaire, about 2026) said tele-declaration would be extended to all cooperatives from June 2026, with performance scoring to target inspections. Not reached or unverified: whether it actually launched, the legal basis for making it mandatory, which documents it covers (accounts, AG minutes, activity report), the deadlines, and the fines or dissolution risk. The adala and coops4dev PDFs could not be read: the fetch returned binary content.
market: 65,315 cooperatives with 788,969 members at end of November 2025 (ODCO via infomediaire). 69,193 cooperatives with more than 825,000 members in the central register in mid-June 2026 (Le Matin, July 2026). Most are small agricultural, artisan and women's cooperatives. Many are non-compliant: under half held the required AG by the original deadline.
competitor: No cooperative-specific private software found. Generic Moroccan accounting tools (Sage, KHABIR, CEGID, EBP, per Upsilon Consulting) cover bookkeeping. ODCO runs its own free digital tools (project bank, marketplace, TaaWouNYa Academy, Sijil Coop for setting up cooperatives), so the filing itself will probably sit on a free state portal. The portal's name and features were not found: an Arabic search turned up nothing relevant.
killer: No killer confirmed. The likely threat is ODCO's own free e-filing (Sijil Coop and the planned June 2026 rollout), but I couldn't verify its annual-reporting scope.
reason: Law 112-12 is in force and sets yearly duties: hold an AG within six months of year-end and keep accounts, with an auditor only above 10 MDH turnover. ODCO announced it would extend tele-declaration to all cooperatives from June 2026, with performance scoring for inspections. But no source shows it launched, whether it is binding, which documents it needs or what the penalties are. The ODCO July 2026 piece names only Sijil Coop, which is for setting up cooperatives. No private vendor turned up, but the filing will likely be a free ODCO portal. Buyers are many (69,193) yet poor and rural, so they won't pay much. Federations or accountants are the realistic channel. The real pain is bookkeeping and AG paperwork, not the filing itself.
challenge_reason: I found no product that kills the idea, but the duty is still unclear. The only "télédéclaration" platform I could identify, Sijil Coop, is ODCO's free state portal. Hespress (July 2026) says it handles the creation of cooperatives, not annual reporting. The infomediaire article only says the plan was to roll out e-filing ("généraliser la télédéclaration") from June 2026, alongside a scoring system for controls. I found no proof that it launched, what must be filed, or what the penalties are. Any filing will most likely go through a free ODCO portal. Willingness to pay looks weak: in 2006 only 936 of 6,286 cooperatives reported their results, and most are tiny. That leaves federations or accountants as the realistic buyers. Searches in Arabic and French found no private competitor. The market of 69,193 cooperatives is real, but the pain hasn't been shown.
