name: Licence and compliance tracker for private/small-scale water suppliers (Diploma Ministerial 130/2025)
buyer: Private water suppliers (borehole and small piped network operators, fontanário operators) licensed by AURA
trigger: Private suppliers must hold a water licence (2015 licensing regulation). DM 130/2025 sets technical provisions for private suppliers (Boletim da República I Série suppl. 249, 30 Dec 2025, in force about end of March 2026). DM 131/2025 strategy promotes simplified licensing for small-scale operators under AURA supervision.
duty: Prior water licence is required under the 2015 Regulamento do Licenciamento de Serviços de Abastecimento de Água Potável por Fornecedores Privados (Council of Ministers, 36th ordinary session, 13 Oct 2015). DM 130/2025 (BR I Série suppl. 249, 30 Dec 2025) sets technical provisions and took effect about 90 days after publication (late March 2026); FAOLEX lists it as not repealed. AURA Res. 3/2021 sets tariffs and a minimum consumption of 5 m3/month for private systems. Recurring reporting, water-quality testing frequency and penalties: not verified, because the decree text could not be read (FAOLEX PDF unreadable, LEAP returned 403). A 2024 AIM article shows AURA collects data from providers and wants to improve how it does so, but names no portal or formal reporting duty.
market: AIM, 16 Sep 2024, quoting AURA administrator Julieta Paulo: AURA's database holds about 1,800 water supply providers, of which about 20-25% are licensed (roughly 360-450). The claim's 19% figure is not confirmed; the source says 20-25%.
competitor: Searches found no licence or compliance tracker for private water suppliers in Mozambique and no online AURA reporting portal. Generic utility billing and prepaid-meter platforms exist: CityTaps CTSuite (its listed countries do not include Mozambique), Susteq water ATMs (Mozambique not confirmed), and Triden billing software. Public utilities (FIPAG/ADM) buy their own systems, such as Primavera ERP, through tenders. A USAID URBAN WASH project works with AURA and DNAAS on formalising private providers, a possible free or donor-funded alternative.
reason: The licence duty is real: the 2015 Council of Ministers regulation requires private water suppliers to hold a licence beforehand. DM 130/2025, published 30 Dec 2025, took effect 90 days later and sets technical rules, and AURA sets their tariffs (Res. 3/2021). I could not confirm any recurring duty that software would help with, such as reports, quality-log frequency or penalties: the decree text came back as an unreadable PDF and the LEAP page returned 403. That missing proof is why the verdict is unverifiable. I found no compliance tracker or AURA portal. Generic billing tools such as CityTaps are not confirmed in Mozambique. AIM (Sep 2024) puts the market at about 1,800 providers, only 20-25% licensed. The pain is mostly a one-off licence, buyers are informal and can pay little, so the score is low.
sources: https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/mz/national-legislation/ministerial-decree-no-1302025-approving-technical-provisions (search snippet only, fetch 403); https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/moz212647.pdf (fetched, content unreadable); https://www.portaldogoverno.gov.mz/por/content/download/5161/37039/version/1/file/COMUNICADO+DA+36.%C2%AA+SOCM-2015.pdf (search snippet only); https://aimnews.org/?p=29991 (fetched); https://www.globalwaters.org/resources/assets/small-local-service-provision-water-and-sanitation-services-mozambique-inception (search snippet only); https://www.gsma.com/mobilefordevelopment/programme/digital-utilities/citytaps-delivering-safe-water-to-the-urban-poor-through-prepaid-smart-metering-and-mobile-money/ (search snippet only); https://susteq.nl (search snippet only)

name: Gold and mineral trading licence register and buyer-book tool (Class I and II licence holders)
buyer: Small mineral and gold buyers, jewellers and artisanal-mining traders holding comercialização licences
trigger: Decreto 20/2011 (mineral trading licence classes I and II); Decreto 63/2021 for diamonds, precious metals and gems (replaced Decreto 25/2015). Certificate of origin and packaging needed for export of gold and gems.
reason: Duty partly confirmed: Decreto 63/2021 (Lei 20/2014, art. 87) replaced Decreto 25/2015. It requires a ministerial trading licence for gold, other precious metals and gems, and proof of sale to the Kimberley unit (UGPK) for exports. I could not read the texts, so I could not confirm purchase-register or periodic-return duties, frequency, penalties or the Decreto 20/2011 class details. The in-force date conflicts between FAOLEX (on publication) and LEAP (12 months later). No local competitor or state portal turned up, but only two searches were run. No licence-holder count was found. Holders are probably few, informal and low-paying, and the government is studying a Ghana GoldBod-style model that could replace private buyers. Distribution is weak.

name: Private employment agency licensing and placement-record kit (Decreto 16/2025)
buyer: Licensed private employment and overseas recruitment agencies
trigger: Decreto 16/2025 licensing and operation of private employment agencies; overseas recruitment reserved for licensed agencies; written job offers endorsed by the authority; recruitment fees to candidates illegal. Rules under revision.
reason: The duty looks real but the market is tiny. A Club of Mozambique report says Decreto 16/2025 limits overseas job brokerage to licensed private agencies, and AIM reports only 6 agencies qualify for overseas placement. Licensees must not charge candidates, and overseas offers must be sent to the labour authority. I found no total count of domestic agencies and no periodic reporting duty. I found no competing software, but one search turned up no sign of a market for it either. I could not read the decree text, and sources disagree on earlier instruments (Decreto 36/2016, Decreto 16/2018, Decreto 87/2023). A seller would have a handful to a few dozen buyers, weak willingness to pay and no recurring filing to automate. The value is low.

name: Non-profit beneficial-owner and registry filings kit for associations, religious bodies and foreign NGOs
buyer: Associations, religious confessions, foundations, foreign NGOs registered in Mozambique
trigger: Lei 14/2023 (AML/CFT) and Decreto-Lei 01/2024 (Regulamento de Registo de Entidades Legais) required beneficial-owner declarations to CREL by 27 Feb 2025. A pending non-profit law (draft deposited Oct 2022) and the FATF grey-list exit may add NPO reporting.
reason: The duty is real but one-off. Under Lei 14/2023 the Ministry of Justice required all non-profits (associations, religious confessions, foundations, foreign NPOs) to declare beneficial owners to CREL by 27 Feb 2025. DLA Piper says non-compliance can bring fines and criminal proceedings. A later notice told foreign NGOs to regularise urgently. Declaration goes through the free state portal utente.srn.gov.mz, which competes with any kit. I found no recurring annual duty. I found no evidence the 2022 NPO bill passed. I ran no competitor-software search and have no market count. Weak recurrence, a free state portal and low willingness to pay point to a low score.

name: Licensed foreign-exchange house daily position report generator
buyer: Licensed casas de câmbio and partial-exchange agents
trigger: Aviso 7/GBM/2023: net FX position must not exceed own funds at close of each day, with daily position report to Banco de Moçambique; Aviso 3/GBM/2024 on FX operations and partial FX trading.
reason: Duty is real. Aviso 7/GBM/2023 (11 Dec 2023, Lei 20/2020) art. 9: net FX position at day close must not exceed own funds. Art. 10: a daily position map and a monthly own-funds map go to Banco de Moçambique through its Bank Supervision Application, which is a state portal. Sanctions follow the credit-institutions law. Aviso 3/GBM/2024 requires an IT system to process and record FX operations. I found no vendor product. I did not search for vendors directly, so competition was not checked. The market is tiny: I found no count of houses, and the claim guesses a few dozen. Each house already has to run its own transaction system, which probably covers the report. A solo founder would have few buyers and little willingness to pay. Report format and the portal's input method were not checked.

name: ISPC quarterly return, invoice book and unregistered-supplier withholding kit for micro-traders
buyer: ISPC taxpayers (artisans, small shops, plumbers, carpenters, barbers, mechanics, small farmers and fishers now inside scope) and the bookkeepers who serve them
trigger: Lei 9/2025 (29 Dec 2025), effective 1 Jan 2026: tax period moves from annual to quarterly, every sale or service needs a sequentially numbered invoice in MZN with NUITs, and buyers purchasing from unregistered individuals (up to 2,500,000 MT a year) must issue an invoice on the supplier's behalf and withhold 5%. Turnover ceiling rises to 4,000,000 MT, new progressive rates.
duty: Lei 9/2025 (29 Dec 2025), in force 1 Jan 2026, amends and republishes the ISPC Code (Lei 5/2009). The tax period moves from annual to quarterly, with quarterly payment. Every sale or service needs an invoice or equivalent document: in Portuguese and MZN, dated, sequentially numbered, with the parties' names and NUITs (DLA Piper). Buyers from unregistered individuals (up to 2,500,000 MT a year) must issue the invoice for the supplier and withhold 5% (DLA Piper). RSM says taxpayers must periodically send information to the AT, and filing still applies when tax due is under 500 MT. Ceiling 4,000,000 MT; rates 3/4/5%, 12% and 15% for services, 20% above the ceiling. Not reached: penalties, exact quarterly due dates, whether the implementing regulations PLMJ says were due within 180 days (by June 2026) were published, and whether certified software or electronic reporting is required for ISPC. The RSM and KPMG PDFs could not be read (compressed binary).
market: No register count of ISPC taxpayers found. Signals that the base is growing: the simplified VAT and exemption regimes were abolished, pushing small taxpayers into ISPC or the general regime (EY/PLMJ); scope was widened to small-scale forestry, fishing, livestock, poultry, beekeeping and crafts; and the 2025 budget targeted 200,000 new taxpayers overall (RTP). The exact ISPC population was not reached; the AT's statistical reports would be the source.
competitor: Nothing found that does the ISPC invoice-book, quarterly calculation and 5% withholding job. Certified SAF-T invoicing software (Cegid Vendus and others) serves VAT-regime firms, and Vendus says the monthly invoice-communication duty excludes ISPC taxpayers; that article predates the reform. Per Forbes Africa Lusófona, the state Portal do Contribuinte / e-Tributação was operational for VAT and ISPC payment; no evidence it generates ISPC invoices or withholding documents. Unverified: whether the AT has since released a free ISPC invoicing app.
killer: None found. Possible future threats, unverified: the ISPC regulation (due June 2026, not located) and the AT's e-Factura project, which may be free.
reason: The duty is real and in force from 1 Jan 2026. Lei 9/2025 amends the ISPC Code: tax is now paid quarterly, every sale needs a numbered invoice with the parties' NUITs, and buyers from unregistered individuals must invoice on their behalf and withhold 5%. RSM also notes a periodic information duty. No ISPC-specific invoice-book, quarterly calculator or withholding tool was found. Certified invoicing vendors such as Vendus target VAT firms, and the e-Tributação portal handles ISPC payment only. Not found: the implementing regulations, exact quarterly dates, penalties and the number of ISPC taxpayers. The pain and frequency are real, but micro-traders are often informal and pay little. The 500 MT exemption shrinks the paying base. Best route is through bookkeepers or market associations, or a simple mobile app.
challenge_reason: I found nothing that does the core job: no ISPC-specific invoicing app, no free AT tool, and no regulation that removes the duty. Sources confirm the duty applies since 1 Jan 2026: an invoice for every sale, invoice records sent to the AT, quarterly payment, and 5% withholding with self-billing on purchases from unregistered suppliers. The weaknesses remain. The 180-day regulation (due June 2026) was not found, so I could not confirm the format, deadlines or penalties. The AT's e-Factura project (Cegid mentions it) could become a free state tool. Tax under 500 MT per quarter is exempt from payment, which takes the smallest traders out of the paying base. Micro-traders likely pay little and are largely informal, so selling through bookkeepers is the realistic channel.

name: Simplified licence regularisation and renewal service under Decreto 41/2026
buyer: Small shops, restaurants/catering, dance halls, workshops, salons, small tourism and agro-industry units holding simplified licences
trigger: Decreto 41/2026 (in force 25 Oct 2026): holders of Decreto 39/2017 licences have 12 months to regularise at no cost; licences valid 3 years, renewable 3 years; fines 4 to 10 times the public-sector minimum wage, suspension, closure, cancellation. Decreto 40/2026 prior-notice certificate for low-risk activities. Lei 18/2026 will add a broader commercial-activity regime by 29 Dec 2026.
reason: Duty is real. Decreto 41/2026 (27 July) revokes Decreto 39/2017. It takes effect 25 Oct 2026, so it is not yet in force. Holders of 39/2017 licences must regularise within 12 months at no cost. Fees for issue and renewal are tied to the public-sector minimum wage. Decreto 40/2026 sets a prior-notice certificate issued within 2 hours. Microenterprises are reportedly exempt from fees. The state's free e-BAU platform is the preferred channel, and the BAU says simplified-regime issue time fell from 3 days to 24 hours. That leaves little room for a paid intermediary. The regularisation is one-off and free, and renewal comes only every 3 years. Buyers are informal micro-businesses with low willingness to pay. I did not verify the fine amounts, holder counts or private competitors, and I could not read the official decree text.

name: Savings-and-loan organisation (OPE) and microcredit operator register and returns
buyer: Savings-and-loan organisations, small credit co-operatives and microcredit operators
trigger: Decreto 50/2024 (11 Jul 2024) plus Aviso 8/GBM/2020 limits; registration with Banco de Moçambique; max 200 depositing members for OPEs.
reason: Duty partly real: BdM registration regime for microcredit operators and OPEs exists (Decreto 57/2004, Lei 20/2020, Aviso 8/GBM/2020; OPEs max 200 depositing members). BdM cancelled registrations of operators (2022), so enforcement exists. Could not verify periodic returns, penalties or operator counts; the PDFs were unreadable. A university paper says only microbanks and large co-ops are directly supervised, the rest only monitored, so the filing burden looks thin. Mifos open-source was deployed locally for MFIs and ASCAs (2010-11). Market is small and fragmented, with low willingness to pay. The claim seems to come from a 2024 Decreto 50/2024 reference that I did not verify. Weak opportunity.

name: Dog and cat breeder and seller CVO compliance kit (Decreto 45344-MAG)
buyer: Family breeders (up to 2 breeding females or 6 adults), small, medium and large commercial breeders, and veterinary clinics that sell dogs or cats. Pet shops are effectively cut out unless they qualify.
trigger: Decreto Ejecutivo 45344-MAG, in force June 2026 after a roughly six-month adaptation period. Obligations: CVO from SENASA; per-animal clinical file signed by a vet (age, vaccination and deworming, health, CVO number); records of inventory, buyers, biosecurity and medical history; no sale before 8 weeks; one litter per female per year; housing plans for commercial breeders. SENASA inspectors can suspend and seize.
duty: Real and in force. Decreto Ejecutivo 45344-MAG, the regulation for dog and cat breeding and sales establishments, took effect on 12 June 2026 (Tico Times). Observador reported a six-month adaptation period running from 19 December, which fits a June 2026 deadline. Every breeder (family, small, medium or large commercial) and every establishment selling dogs or cats, including vet clinics, needs a CVO from SENASA. Medium and large breeders need a permanent veterinarian; family and small breeders need a named attending vet. Breeders must keep records of inventory, buyers, biosecurity and medical history, plus an emergency plan. Each animal sold needs a vet-signed clinical file showing age, vaccination and deworming, health status and the breeder's CVO number. Breed clubs must require the CVO from members and report their member list to SENASA every year. The law sets no fixed fine amounts. SENASA can inspect at any time, order corrections, suspend operations and seize animals, with care costs charged to the owner, and the law refers to administrative, civil or penal sanctions under existing legislation. Recurrence is event-driven (each litter and each sale) plus the yearly club report. How often the CVO must be renewed was not found. The official MAG PDF returned 404 when I tried to open it, so these details come from press coverage.
market: Very small. A 2017-2018 UNED study found 111 dog-breeding operations nationwide, only 26% of them registered with SENASA. Observador reported only about 20 SENASA-registered centres (35 at the peak). The minister admits there is no complete national register. Many informal family breeders now technically need a CVO, but they are hard to reach and unlikely to pay. There are about 1.7M dogs and 775k cats in the country, but that does not translate into paying firms. The yearly club report could open a distribution channel through breed clubs, but I found no count of clubs.
competitor: I found no Costa Rica-specific tool or SENASA digital system for the records or the clinical file. No press article mentions a portal. CVO applications in general may go through the Ventanilla Única de Inversión (VUI), but I could not confirm that for breeders. General breeder software already covers most of the record-keeping: Kinvara (USD 39 a month, tracks animals, litters, vaccines and health tests), BreederHQ (vaccination tracking, buyers), BreedTracker (about USD 15 a month), the free BreedTools, and Dog Breeder Pro, which has a Spanish-language site, waitlists and e-signed contracts. None of them produces the SENASA clinical-file template or tracks the CVO number. That missing piece is small and could be handled with a template. I did not check vet clinic management software.
reason: The duty is real, new and enforced by inspection. Records are event-driven (each litter and each sale) and there is a yearly club report. But the formal market is tiny: about 20-35 registered establishments and roughly 111 known operations (2017-18 study). Informal family breeders have low willingness to pay and many would rather avoid registering. Low-cost general breeder apps (Kinvara, BreedTracker, free BreedTools, Dog Breeder Pro in Spanish) already cover inventory, litters, vaccines and buyers. What is missing is a Costa Rica clinical-file and CVO template, which is a thin add-on. Fines are not quantified. The MVP would be simple, and breed clubs or vets could help distribution, but revenue potential for a solo founder is very limited. It could work as a feature inside a K06-style SENASA CVO kit.

name: Casas de empeño and second-hand shops daily seller register
buyer: Pawnshops (casas de empeño) and second-hand goods shops, including those that buy gold
trigger: Bill 21.120, reported as passed unanimously in second debate: daily register of every seller, verified ID, a physical or digital copy of the ID document, data available to police on request, closing 19:00-06:00, fines of 3-6 base salaries, licence revoked on repeat offences. It reforms the Código Municipal art. 90 and the Código de Comercio arts. 448-449.
reason: Bill 21.120 (daily seller register, ID copy, 19:00-06:00 closing, fines of 3-6 base salaries) is confirmed only as a 2019 bill. CR Hoy, dated 27 June 2019, reports unanimous approval with the second debate still pending. I found no law number, La Gaceta publication or in-force evidence. Sources conflict on votes (39 vs 43), and I found nothing linking the bill to Código Municipal art. 90. The duty is a simple register kept by municipal licence holders, with no filing to an authority and no set format. Competition was not found in Costa Rica. Foreign pawn software such as PPSS logs customers and police reports. The market is small and unquantified, and the pawnshop association is litigating other rules. Pain and willingness to pay look low.

name: RTBF annual declaration for non-profits, co-operatives, mutuals and solidarista associations
buyer: Small associations, foundations, co-operatives, solidarista associations and other non-profits that hold a cédula jurídica
trigger: Annual Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiarios Finales declaration to the BCCR (Central Directo), due 30 April (2026 deadline passed; April 2027 cycle next). Non-profits, mutuals, co-operatives and solidarista associations were added by the 2024 joint resolution. Only the legal representative with a digital signature or a registered generalísimo apoderado may file (special powers excluded in 2026). Fines up to 2% of gross income (3-100 base salaries); non-filers cannot get Registro Nacional certifications or register documents; due-diligence records kept 5 years.
reason: Duty is real: the annual RTBF declaration to the BCCR is due 30 April. PwC reports fines of up to 2% of gross income (3 to 100 base salaries), a block on Registro Nacional certifications and document registration, and 5-year record keeping. Non-profits (associations, foundations, co-operatives, mutuals, solidarista associations) are covered, per La Nación via the search summary. Only the legal representative with a digital signature, or a registered generalísimo apoderado, may file, and special powers are excluded in 2026. That limits a third-party done-for-you product. The task was a single annual form, so there is little to automate and the market is a filing service for small fees. I found no software competitor in about 3 searches, but accountants and law firms sell the filing. Entity counts not found. 2026 extension status not confirmed.

name: Biweekly e-index filing kit for notaries (Ley 10798, INDEX platform)
buyer: Individual and small-firm notaries (number not found; unverified)
trigger: Ley 10798 reforms art. 27 of the Codigo Notarial (Ley 7764). Indices are due within 5 business days after the 15th and the last day of each month, through the Archivo Nacional platform with digital signature. In force one year after publication (publication date not found, so about end 2026 or early 2027). The Archivo Nacional will charge a platform fee. The Executive has one year to regulate.
duty: Real, and in force in its paper form since long before this law. Notaries have filed índices quincenales since the 1943 Ley Orgánica de Notariado and under Decreto 33398-C of 2006. Ley 10798 (expediente 24.809, approved in second debate on 22 Oct 2025, sanctioned 16 Nov 2025) only reforms art. 27 of the Codigo Notarial so that filing must be digital. Indices are due within 5 business days after the 15th and the last day of each month, through the Archivo Nacional platform. Penalty: the Archivo Notarial reports late notaries to the disciplinary body. I could not confirm the La Gaceta publication date, the entry-into-force date or whether the regulation has been issued, because the official PDF was not machine-readable.
market: About 4,000 notaries already used INDEX before it became mandatory (bill 24.809, as reported). I did not find the total number of active notaries in the Dirección Nacional de Notariado (DNN) register; my guess is that it is somewhat higher.
competitor: The state INDEX platform of the Archivo Nacional does the core job. It is a paid platform with digital signature that the ministry says automates more than 90% of index accreditation, and the law names the Archivo Nacional platform as the required channel. Its annual fee was cut from CRC 106,000 to CRC 44,850 (Delfino, July 2026). About 4,000 notaries already used it voluntarily, according to the bill. My searches found no Costa Rican private notary-software vendor, so the only gap left is pre-filling the index from protocol data, which is thin.
reason: The duty is real and frequent (twice a month), but it is not new: only the channel changes. The law requires filing through the state INDEX platform. INDEX is already in use, costs about CRC 44,850 a year (recently cut by 58%), and the ministry says it automates more than 90% of the process. A private tool cannot replace the filing step. It could at best prepare the data before upload, and I could not confirm that INDEX accepts imports. The market is small (about 4,000+ notaries), and they already pay the state for the core job. Willingness to pay for an extra layer looks low. A broader notary practice-management product might work, but that is a different and more generic idea.

name: RTBF annual declaration service for small companies, via accountants and lawyers
buyer: Accounting and law firms filing for many small sociedades; owners of dormant companies
trigger: Annual declaration in April on BCCR Central Directo, by the legal representative with digital signature or a registered general attorney (special powers excluded for 2026). Fine of 2% of gross income, with floor CRC 1,386,600 and ceiling CRC 46,220,000. Non-filers get no certifications and no registrations at the Registro Nacional. Next ordinary filing probably April 2027 (inferred, not confirmed). Active and inactive companies both file.
duty: Annual ordinary RTBF declaration (1-30 April) on BCCR Central Directo. It covers all legal persons with a cédula jurídica, active or inactive, plus private trusts, third-party resource administrators and non-profits. New entities file an extraordinary declaration within 20 business days. Legal basis: Ley 9416, art. 84 bis Código de Normas y Procedimientos Tributarios, the RTBF regulation and Resolución DGT-ICD-R-06-2020. Penalty: 2% of gross income, min 3 base salaries (CRC 1,386,600), max 100 (CRC 46,220,000). The Registro Nacional also stops issuing personería certificates and registering documents. For 2026, filing was limited to the legal representative with personal firma digital or an apoderado generalísimo; special powers were excluded (PwC). Sources also mention Circular DPJ-002-2026 on appointing representatives; I could not open the KPMG page (404). No official 2027 deadline found; April 2027 is expected but unconfirmed.
market: 280,743 entities were obligated for the 2021 period (El Financiero, as relayed in search results). I found no current count of obligated entities or filings for 2025 or 2026. The Registro Nacional dissolved about 335,000 companies in 2019-2022 (Diario Extra), so the current universe may differ. Not found: the size of the filing-agent market and any fee data.
competitor: The free BCCR Central Directo portal does the core filing and pre-loads the prior declaration. BCCR and Hacienda also run free online help (guides, phone 2539-4000). I found no commercial software for preparing or filing RTBF returns, and no priced filing service; law and accounting firms and Big Four advisories (PwC, KPMG, EY, RSM) only publish guides. Because filing is limited to the legal representative or a generalísimo holder, a third-party filing service is structurally hard to run. What is left is a multi-entity deadline tracker or a prep tool for accounting firms.
reason: The duty is real and in force. Art. 84 bis CNPT (Ley 9416) and the RTBF regulation require an annual filing on BCCR Central Directo by 30 April. Active and inactive entities both file. The fine is 2% of gross income (min CRC 1,386,600, max CRC 46,220,000), and non-filers are blocked at the Registro Nacional. I found no third-party RTBF software. But the free BCCR portal does the core job and pre-loads last year's return, so most annual updates take little work. Only the legal representative (personal firma digital) or an apoderado generalísimo can file in 2026, so accountants cannot simply file for clients. That leaves only a reminder and tracking tool. It runs once a year and willingness to pay is low. About 280,743 entities were obligated in 2021.

name: Compliance pack for non-traditional lodging hosts (ICT, Tributacion e-invoice and IVA, municipal patente, Salud permit)
buyer: Airbnb and Vrbo hosts and small property managers (about 44,000 listings; only 578 registered with ICT and 117 with Tributacion in late 2023)
trigger: Ley 9742 (in force June 2020, regulation October 2021). Hosts must register with ICT and DGT, issue electronic invoices, declare IVA and income tax, and hold a municipal licence. Platforms report hosts to Hacienda. Airbnb collects IVA on cross-border services and is running a Tribu-CR sign-up campaign for hosts.
market: About 44,000 listings. 578 hosts registered with ICT and 117 with Tributacion (late 2023).
competitor: No Costa Rica-specific host compliance tool found. Hacienda ATV/Tribu-CR and Airbnb IVA collection partly overlap. Chekin is Spain-only.
reason: Duty is real: Ley 9742 (in force June 2020, regulation October 2021) requires ICT registration and e-invoicing, and data goes to Hacienda. Compliance is very low (578 ICT-registered, 117 on Tributacion, of about 44,000 listings). Two weaknesses. First, enforcement is weak: one source says the law carries no sanctions for non-registration, and reform bills 24061 (would drop the ICT registration duty, status "Dictaminado") and 23766 (new sanctions, in committee) are pending. Second, hosts are fragmented and unmotivated, and Hacienda's ATV/Tribu-CR plus Airbnb's own IVA collection cover part of the job. I found no Costa Rica-specific compliance tool in two searches; the Spanish tools (Chekin) don't apply. I did not check municipal patente or Salud permit rules.

name: Solidarista association treasury and supervision compliance
buyer: About 1,382 active solidarista associations (about 401k members) and their administrators
trigger: The Asebanacio case (CRC 12 billion loss) and the Coopeservidores intervention led SUGEF to prepare a supervision regulation for solidaristas, planned from 2021. Its status is unconfirmed and a bill (exp. 22.980) sought exemption. SGF-0722-2025 changed co-op capital rules from January 2025, but those cover only about 18 supervised co-ops.
reason: The SUGEF premise has mostly collapsed. Reports say CONASSIF repealed the 2020 provisions, and that since 2021 it decided not to supervise solidarista associations. SUGEF head Rocío Aguilar said they don't do classic financial intermediation. Bill 22.980 would exempt them from supervision. A rival bill (24.053) would add supervision, and I couldn't confirm the status of either. So no confirmed mandatory SUGEF report exists. The only existing duties are Ley 6970 internal governance (fiscalía, audit) and CCSS/DESAF payroll lists, which are not a distinct recurring filing. I found no solidarista-specific software, but I only ran a thin search, so competition is unconfirmed. I did not verify the 1,382 association count. Buyers are fragmented and the duty is weak.

name: Coffee beneficio reporting and liquidation tool for ICAFE (Ley 2762)
buyer: Small beneficios and co-operative coffee mills (count not found)
trigger: Ley 2762 and its reglamento: beneficios must be registered with ICAFE, report receipts about every 15 days, register sale contracts, give an annual client list of producers, and pay the final liquidation within 8 days (figures from an undated ICAFE presentation). Receiving from non-producers is restricted.
reason: Duty is real: Ley 2762 binds beneficiadores to issue receipts, file producer client lists, and settle liquidation. The 15-day and 8-day figures come from an undated ICAFE presentation, and I could not confirm them against the current reglamento. I found no ICAFE portal and no commercial software for beneficio reporting, but that only means the searches returned nothing, not that none exists. Market is small: counts range from 172 to 304 beneficios depending on the source and year, and many are co-operatives or large firms that likely have in-house ERPs. The buyer pool is tiny and the rules are bespoke to ICAFE, so willingness to pay and distribution are weak. Frequency is seasonal, roughly Nov-Mar harvest. Score stays low.

name: Traceability and compliance kit for licensed cannabis and hemp operators (Ley 10113)
buyer: Licensed growers, processors and exporters of hemp and medicinal cannabis (few)
trigger: Ley 10113 requires full traceability, proof of lawful capital origin, THC and CBD controls and a 1% levy on profits. Regulation date is in conflict (2022 vs 12 Feb 2025). A consultancy cites a traceability mandate around February 2027 and product standard RTCR 515:2024, both unverified.
reason: Ley 10113 is real (2022). Hemp regulation was published in La Gaceta in Sept 2022 (crhoy). A medicinal/psychoactive regulation was approved 12 Feb 2025, and RTCR 515:2024 exists (observador.cr). The traceability duty is described in law summaries, but I found no official source for a Feb 2027 seed-to-sale mandate. That date appears only in a vendor guide (GrowerIQ, a seed-to-sale seller), so it is a competitor and a sales source. No state-mandated platform was found. The market is tiny: an unsourced GrowerIQ figure says 57 hemp licences by Sept 2024 (El Financiero said 3 in March 2023). Global seed-to-sale vendors (Distru, BioTrack) exist. Few buyers, an unclear deadline and a vendor-led niche make this weak for a solo founder.

name: RCD (construction and demolition waste) bitacora and quarterly-report tool for builders
buyer: Small and mid-size builders, residential developers, remodelling and demolition contractors (generators of works above and below 300 m2); possibly authorized waste gestores and haulers as a second buyer
trigger: New Ministerio de Salud construction and demolition waste regulation, reportedly in force July 2025: mandatory digital bitacora of waste type, volume and destination, quarterly and final reports through the Ventanilla Unica de Inversion (VUI), work only with authorized gestores, supervision by Ministerio de Salud and municipalities, sanctions up to work suspension, closure and fines. Decree number unconfirmed.
duty: Reported only through secondary press quoting the Camara Costarricense de la Construccion. The reglamento ambiental de residuos de construccion y demolicion is said to be in force since July 2025. It covers mayores (works over 300 m2) and menores (under 300 m2). Duties: sort waste on site; keep a mandatory digital bitacora of types, volumes and destinations; file quarterly and final reports through the VUI; work only with authorized gestores. Ministerio de Salud and the municipalities supervise. Infractions are leve, grave or gravisima, with temporary suspension, closure and fines. Per Delfino, menores must apply traceability and use authorized gestores; their other duties are unclear. The decree number, Gaceta publication and issuing ministry were not found. Decreto 44974 (found on UNEP LEAP) is a different rule on regionalized ordinary/organic waste. Whether the duty is legally in force could not be confirmed from a primary source.
market: not_reached. No register or statistic was found for how many builders or construction permits fall under the rule. The CCC trained 70+ professionals in Feb-May 2025. CFIA permit volumes would be the right proxy but were not checked.
competitor: No Costa Rican commercial bitacora or RCD reporting software found in Spanish searches. The only channel named is the state VUI (Ventanilla Unica de Inversion), which collects the quarterly and final reports. Not checked: whether the VUI provides its own free bitacora or form that already does the core job, and whether authorized gestores supply manifests or traceability certificates. Tools from other countries (a Brazilian web app, the Cuban Ambiens) were found but do not serve Costa Rica.
killer: The CFIA's Bitácora Digital (com.cfia.Bitacora), a free tool that every CFIA professional on a building site must already use, is the channel the decree names for the RCD log. The quarterly and final reports go through the state VUI portal, and compliance is checked during plan review in CFIA's APC system before a construction licence is granted (Decreto Ejecutivo 44843-S, in force from 9 July 2025).
reason: Three June 2025 press pieces (Delfino, Observador, E&N) repeat the CCC's description of a new reglamento in force July 2025: a digital bitacora of waste type, volume and destination, quarterly and final VUI reports, authorized gestores, and sanctions. None names a decree number, Gaceta date or ministry. Decreto 44974 deals with regionalized ordinary/organic waste, not this. Not checked: the official text, whether the VUI form already acts as the bitacora (which would weaken a paid tool), enforcement since 2025, and market size. No commercial CR tool turned up. Pain is real but rests on a state channel; buyers are reachable through the CCC; willingness to pay is uncertain.
challenge_reason: I found the decree: Decreto 44843-S, dated 5 December 2024, in force from 9 July 2025. A Zurcher Odio & Raven note says the log must be kept in the CFIA's free Bitácora Digital, which professionals already have to use. Compliance is checked in CFIA's APC plan review, which overlaps with K11. Reports are filed on the free state VUI portal. Per Ecopational, only obras mayores (over 300 m2) file the quarterly reports; menores have lighter duties. Environmental consultancies such as Ecopational and Wastech already sell help with compliance. What a founder could still sell is a narrow piece: collecting gestor receipts and building the VUI quarterly report for larger works. I did not see the decree text (the SCIJ fetch returned only the page shell), the VUI form, or any enforcement data.
challenge_sources: https://www.zurcherodioraven.com/es/noticias-y-opinion/87-cambios-normativos-recientes-para-el-sector-construccion-en-costa-rica ; https://ecopational.com/gestion-de-los-residuos-de-la-construccion-y-de-la-demolicion-de-obras-en-costa-rica-el-nuevo-decreto-no-44843-s/ ; https://www.ministeriodesalud.go.cr/index.php/prensa/62-noticias-2025/2033-ministerio-de-salud-publica-reglamento-para-la-gestion-de-residuos-de-la-construccion-y-la-demolicion (search snippet only) ; https://play.google.com/store/apps/details/Bit%C3%A1cora_Digital?id=com.cfia.Bitacora&hl=en_US (search snippet only) ; https://vui.cr/tramite/registro-de-gestor-de-residuos-ministerio-de-salud/ (search snippet only) ; https://delfino.cr/2025/06/el-manejo-responsable-de-residuos-de-construccion-y-demolicion-sera-obligatorio-a-partir-de-julio ; https://observador.cr/camara-empresarial-recuerda-las-nuevas-reglas-sobre-el-manejo-de-desechos-de-construcciones-y-demoliciones/

name: Driving-school training log and exam-readiness manager (if compulsory driving-school training is adopted)
buyer: Independent driving schools (number unverified)
trigger: The Interior Ministry reportedly plans to make driving-school training compulsory before the driver's licence exam (Arka; no date, adoption unconfirmed). The e-draft.am consultation (project 10579) proposes keeping self-study and not requiring a training document, so the outcome is open. Licensing standards for driving schools are under discussion (Armenpress, Aug 2026).
reason: No current legal duty exists. Arka (19 Aug 2026) says the Interior Ministry intends to make driving-school training compulsory before the licence exam. It is only a proposal, with no adoption or effective date and no penalty or frequency. A search found no adopted act. The e-draft.am consultation suggests keeping self-study. Even if adopted, the duty would be a training requirement for candidates, not a recurring compliance filing by schools, and the state or police would likely handle records. School count and competitors were not found; I did only 1 search and 1 fetch, and the Armenian-language competitor search was thin. Weak, speculative opportunity with a small buyer pool.

name: EPR reporting and PRO-registration helper for importers of tyres, batteries, e-equipment, oils and beverages
buyer: Importers and producers; initially the 300 largest of about 2,000 market participants, later small importers
trigger: Draft Law on Extended Producer Responsibility, revised and published for consultation in June 2026 on the e-draft platform. Armenia committed to implement EPR by 2024 under CEPA but missed it. A licensed producer responsibility organisation is to run collection and the Ministry of Environment oversees the system.
duty: draft only, not in force
market: about 2,000 participants; 300 largest in phase one
competitor: none found (Armenian-language search)
reason: No duty is in force. The EPR law is still a draft: the revised package went on e-draft on 11 June 2026, with a stakeholder discussion on 19 June. I found no evidence it was adopted. No start date or penalties are given. The initial phase covers only the 300 largest of about 2,000 participants, so small importers are not yet obliged. Products covered: drinks, batteries, electronics, tyres, motor oils. Market of about 2,000 is from the Ecolur page. Armenian-language search found no software or PRO products. Obligated firms would report through a single licensed PRO, so the PRO would be the only likely buyer. This is a small, uncertain market for a solo founder. Not rejected, but weak: the law is unadopted and the first phase targets large firms.

name: Foreign-worker quota and work-permit manager for small employers under the 2026 Law on Foreigners
buyer: Small employers and agencies hiring foreign workers (construction, agriculture, services)
trigger: A recruitment firm reports a new Law on Foreigners adopted 20 Jan 2026 and in force 1 Nov 2026, replacing the no-quota system with annual quotas by category. Permits are currently filed through workpermit.am; the employer starts the application and must offer local candidates first.
duty: Work permit for non-EAEU foreign hires under the Law on Foreigners, with annual quotas and job-change notices from 1 Nov 2026. Penalty not verified.
market: About 23,700 foreigners working in Armenia (law-firm citation of the Statistical Committee, undated). 2,468 work-permit grants in 2022, and 10,909 applications submitted through the online employer system that year (Council of Europe profile).
competitor: workpermit.am (state portal); law firms such as armenian-lawyer.com
reason: The duty is real. Employers need a work permit for non-EAEU foreigners, filed on the state portal workpermit.am. Amendments to the Law on Foreigners were adopted 20 Jan 2026 and take effect 1 Nov 2026 per law-firm and EY alerts (official text not opened). They replace the labour-market test with annual quotas, narrow the exemptions and add a 15-day job-change notice. Quota sizes and procedure were unpublished as of the sources found. Market is small: about 23.7k foreign workers, and 2,468 work-permit holders in 2022 (Council of Europe), so likely only a few thousand employers. The state portal does the filing, and law firms sell the service. No private software found, though the Russian search was thin and no Armenian-language vendor search was run. Weak buyer pool and low frequency (roughly annual per worker) mean a low score.

name: Water-use permit and well compliance for Ararat Valley fish farms and farms
buyer: Fish farms, orchards and farms using groundwater or artesian wells; drilling contractors
trigger: Water Code amendments HO-208-N and HO-230-N (in force 16 May 2020): drilling is subject to notification; use needs a water-use permit; the State Water Cadastre records permits. 2025 inspection results: 73 activities suspended for no permit, 147 ownerless deep wells. 574 entities were earlier found operating without a permit; a 2023 ministry proposal would criminalise unpermitted artesian use in Ararat Valley (adoption unknown).
reason: Duty is real: the Environmental and Mining Inspection Body reported for 2025 (press conference 20 Jan 2026) 202 violations, 73 activities suspended for no permits, 147 ownerless deep wells, and 15 fish-farm violations. The criminalisation proposal for the Ararat Valley was only a draft in March 2023; I found no adoption. I found no periodic reporting duty and no competitor, but my searches were thin. I did not find an e-portal and could not size the market. The work is a one-off permit and legalisation task, not a recurring filing. Few buyers (about 135 industrial fish farms get state support) and an expert-led, one-time need mean weak software demand.

name: Real estate broker registry, contract-upload and e-invoice compliance kit
buyer: Small real estate brokers and agencies, thousands of them, many informal solo agents
trigger: Draft Law on Realtor Activity: mandatory broker registry and certification; every signed brokerage contract uploaded to a unified platform that checks the cadastre; commissions invoiced through the tax e-invoice portal; separate client-fund bank accounts. Expected in force March 2027 (adoption unconfirmed). Fines up to 300x minimum wage (about 22.5M AMD) for unlicensed brokerage; platform fee about 30,600 AMD per year (one source says about 450,000, conflict).
duty: Armenian Law on Realtor Activity (Ռիելթորական գործունեության մասին). First reading noted by the brokers' association on 18 Sep 2025 (draft Կ-1098-03.06.2025-ՏՀ-011/1). In January 2026 Cadastre Committee head Suren Tovmasyan said it was among the 21 laws adopted in 2025 and will take effect in mid-2027. A search snippet (1 Oct 2026, not opened) mentions a new procedure for realtor qualification exams. Duties: qualification by exam, registration, a state electronic system that checks listings and fixes property fields before ads go out (from 2027, per a law-firm post), and logging of deals in a centralized system (law-firm post, Nov 2025). Frequency: ongoing, every listing and every deal. Not verified from the law text: the 300x fine, the fee amount (the law firm says about $1,200 per year), and the e-invoice requirement. The final adoption date was not confirmed on parliament.am or arlis.am.
market: Unverifiable. No source we found gives a count of realtors or agencies, and the registry does not exist before 2027. The draft's explanatory note (summarized in a search result) says many private intermediaries work informally online. The Armenian Association of Real Estate Agencies exists but gave no membership count.
competitor: The Cadastre Committee is building the state digital platforms itself, according to Tovmasyan in January 2026. These cover the core filing step, so private software has to be a layer on top: CRM, platform sync, document prep. We found no Armenian realtor-compliance product. The discovery pass found only generic CRMs (Bitrix24 implementers, Realty CRM START) and Hatakagits.am. Whether the platform will have an API is unknown. Our own competitor search was limited and is not_reached beyond the discovery pass.
killer: None found. Possible partial killer: the Cadastre Committee's own mandatory platform (being built, specs and API unknown).
reason: The duty is real but has not started yet. The Law on Realtor Activity (draft Կ-1098-03.06.2025-ՏՀ-011/1) passed first reading by September 2025. In January 2026 the Cadastre Committee head said it was among the laws adopted in 2025 and will take effect in mid-2027. It brings qualification exams, a registry, and state checks of listings and deals. The state is building its own platforms. The opening is a CRM or listing tool that syncs with that platform, or a done-for-you compliance service, not a replacement for it. We found no Armenian product for this, but the platform API and how easy it is to use are unknown. Many solo agents work informally, so willingness to pay is weak. The registry does not exist yet, so we have no broker count. Fine amounts and fees not verified.
challenge_reason: Nothing I found kills it, and the duty now looks firmer than the claim said. Aravot (18 Sep 2025) reports the bill passed first reading (K-1098-03.06.2025-TH-011/1). Aravot (19 Jan 2026) quotes the Cadastre Committee head listing the realtor law among the 21 laws adopted in 2025, in force mid-2027, with exams and digital platforms in preparation. I couldn't confirm this on parliament.am or arlis.am. I found no Armenian realtor-compliance product. The weak points remain. The Cadastre Committee builds the filing platform itself, it may be free and simple, and no API is known, so software is a layer on top (contracts, cadastre checks, e-invoices, CRM). The market is small and mostly informal: an iravaban headline says only about 20% operate legally. Platform fee and broker count: unverified.
