name: Food-handler health certificate and 6-month medical exam tracker for delivery firms and food businesses
buyer: Food delivery companies (2,000-3,000 couriers), restaurants, cafes, bakeries, small food producers and shops with staff handling food
trigger: Food Safety Inspection Body: from 1 Aug 2026 full-scale inspection of delivery staff; medical exam at hiring and every 6 months; personal health certificate/sanitary booklet; employer must ensure it; couriers without it face administrative liability; the inspectorate plans to publish violators and compliant company names. Legal act not identified.
duty: The duty is real and in force. Government Decision N 347-N of 27 Mar 2003 (in force since 03.05.2003, latest consolidated publication 19.02.2026 on arlis.am) sets mandatory medical exams at hiring and periodically, the list of covered activities, and the form of the paper personal sanitary booklet (Annex 3). A booklet that does not match the Annex 3 form is invalid. The underlying law is the Law on Food Safety, under which anyone working at any food-chain stage (including transport, distribution and sale) needs a pre-employment exam, an exam every 6 months, and a personal sanitary booklet. The employer must make sure food-handling staff are examined. Couriers without exams or a booklet face administrative liability. I did not find the fine amounts or the article of the Administrative Offences Code. The Food Safety Inspection Body began targeted courier checks on 1 Aug 2026, jointly with the police Patrol Service. The extra deadline it gave delivery firms has expired: in early-to-mid August it reported that of 237 workers checked, the only ones without booklets were people who do not deliver food (the platforms named were Yandex and Glovo). The booklet duty applies to all food businesses, not just delivery. In 2024, inspections of catering businesses recorded violations of the mandatory staff medical exam rule. A draft amendment to 347-N on e-draft.am (pre-employment exams also for volunteers and trainees; exams done by licensed medical organizations) appears not yet adopted.
market: I found no register total. The inspectorate inspected about 4,000 businesses in 2024 (violations at 1,100, 130 suspended), so likely several thousand food businesses (catering, retail, producers) are covered. Delivery is about 2,000-3,000 couriers, concentrated in a few platforms (Yandex, Glovo). The exact count of food business operators was not reached.
competitor: I found no dedicated software or tracking service in Armenian. The booklet is a paper form stamped and signed by the clinic, and I found no public state register or free online check tool for booklets. Risk: the Ministry of Health is rolling out the ARMED e-health system, which could later absorb exam records and kill a tracker. Clinics already sell group exams to employers, which covers the done-for-you part. The two big delivery platforms are a concentrated buyer group that already complies, so they gain little from a tool. My competitor search was limited (2 queries) and is not exhaustive.
reason: The duty is real and recurring: a Government Decision 347-N exam every 6 months plus a sanitary booklet, now actively enforced. But the pain is low. The delivery platforms already complied after the deadline (all 237 food couriers checked had booklets), and they are few and large. For small cafes and shops, the job is tracking two dates per worker a year, which a spreadsheet or the clinic can handle, so willingness to pay is weak. The paper booklet and the absence of a state register leave a gap, but ARMED e-health digitization may close it. Fines are unquantified and the market is small (likely several thousand businesses). This is best seen as a feature inside a broader food-safety compliance tool or a clinic-partnered service, not a standalone product.

name: AML/CFT procedures kit for small notary, law and accounting offices
buyer: Small notary offices, law firms and accounting/consulting firms
trigger: AML/CFT duties extended to lawyers, notaries and accounting/consulting firms from July 2025: enhanced CDD, UBO checks, suspicious-activity reports to the FMC. Draft amendments would also require notaries and the cadastre to notify the FMC of donation deeds. The MONEYVAL report on Armenia was published May 2026.
duty: Law on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, amended by HO-261-N, in force 8 Aug 2025 (PanArmenian, citing the Central Bank of Armenia). Who it covers: individual entrepreneurs and legal entities providing legal services, accountants (individuals and firms), precious-metal dealers and company-formation providers. What they must do: (1) register with the FMC within 6 months (procedure in CBA Council decision 280-N); (2) submit revised internal regulations to the FMC within 2 months; (3) ongoing CDD/EDD, UBO identification for legal-entity clients, STRs to the FMC, and no tipping-off. Penalties for non-compliance were updated, but no amounts were found. Frequency: per client and per suspicious event, so continuous and not periodic. The registration and internal-rules deadlines (about Oct 2025 and Feb 2026) have passed. Unconfirmed: the notary/cadastre duty to report every real-estate donation deed with no threshold appears only in a law-firm blog, and its status was not checked against arlis.am. I could not open the statute text itself.
market: Small. No official count found. Notaries: no national total found; a 2025 seminar had 60 notaries from 9 regions plus Yerevan, so this is likely low hundreds at most (unverified). Audit firms in the Chamber of Auditors: 33 as of 08.05.2026 (Grant Thornton study). Directories list 114 (poidata) to 264 (coresignal) accounting firms, not official counts. The number of lawyer and legal-service entities registered with the FMC was not found.
competitor: Generic, global KYC/AML screening: Shufti Pro (Armenia page, PEP/sanctions, Armenian OCR); Didit (sanctions and PEP lists incl. CBA domestic lists); Know Your Customer Ltd (live pull from the Armenian Electronic Register incl. beneficial owners); StartKyc (a G2 review mentions pre-notarization screening, Armenia coverage unclear). None found providing an Armenian-language internal-rules template, CDD record-keeping and STR drafting kit for small notary, law or accounting offices. Searches in Armenian and Russian returned only law-firm blog guides. Whether the FMC runs its own e-filing portal for STRs was not reached: the CBA pages redirected and both MONEYVAL PDFs returned 403. Council of Europe and FMC trainings exist (free, not software).
killer: No single killer found. Partial: free FMC e-learning platform (lms.fmc.am) and a free FMC report-submission channel (old.cba.am fmchelporganizations page). Notaries already had these duties before 2025, so the trigger is not new for them. Not reached: a free FMC model internal-rules template; the Notary Chamber's own tooling; the MONEYVAL PDFs (403 in the first check, not retried).
reason: The duty is real. Amended AML/CFT Law HO-261-N took effect on 8 Aug 2025, not July as the claim says. Legal-service firms, accountants and TCSPs had to register with the FMC within 6 months and submit revised internal rules within 2 months. Penalties were updated, but no amounts were found. Notaries already had reporting duties. Most of the ongoing work is event-driven: CDD/UBO checks per client and STRs. The deadline-driven rush (registration, internal rules) is already over. Global KYC APIs (Shufti Pro, Didit, Know Your Customer Ltd with Armenian registry/UBO data) cover screening, but no local, Armenian-language AML procedures/STR kit for small offices was found. The market looks small (notary count not found; directories list about 114-264 accounting firms) and supervision is still bank-focused, so willingness to pay is uncertain.
challenge_reason: I found nothing that does the core job: no Armenian product providing internal-rules templates, CDD/UBO records and STR drafting for small offices. Three things weaken the idea. (1) The FMC gives free tools for parts of it: an e-learning system (lms.fmc.am) that lists notaries, lawyers and accountants, and a free report-submission channel (Lotus Notes / e-mail), so filing itself is not a pain point. (2) Notaries are not new to this: the old CBA FMC page already lists the transactions they must report, and the FMC trained them on STRs before 2025. (3) The market is small and the work is mostly one-off. Advocates numbered about 1,580 in 2015, the latest count found; no total was found for notaries; reports are event-driven. The August 2025 law (HO-261-N, per pan.am) set one-off deadlines: registration with the FMC by about February 2026 and new internal acts within two months.
challenge_sources: https://lms.fmc.am ; http://old.cba.am/en/SitePages/fmchelporganizations.aspx ; https://www.pan.am/en/325184 ; https://www.lw.com/admin/Upload/Documents/Global Pro Bono Survey/pro-bono-in-armenia.pdf (snippet only) ; https://armenian-lawyer.com/immigration/armenia-expands-aml-cft-to-legal-and-accounting-firms-enhanced-cdd-ubo-checks-and-no-tipping-off-from-july-2025/ (snippet only)

name: e-CRM (eHDM) 2027 mandate rollout service for small shops, service firms, IEs and notaries
buyer: Small shops, service providers, IEs, notaries not yet on e-CRM
trigger: Govt decision on covered sectors, Dec 2026; effective 1 Jan 2027; fine AMD 500,000
duty: Confirmed on ARLIS (arlis.am/hy/acts/228152). Law HO-309-N of 3 July 2026 amends the Tax Code. The new Art 380.1(1.1) makes electronic cash-register (EKKM) use mandatory for sales, works and services by organisations, individual entrepreneurs and notaries, in the sectors, cases and deadlines the Government sets. The new Art 416(1.1) sets a fine of AMD 500,000 for each transaction made without an EKKM where one is required. Both take effect 1 Jan 2027. Until the Government's implementing acts take effect, the old rules apply only to ride-hailing and taxis. The sector decision (process set by PM Decision 901-A, per lookuptax) is due in late December 2026, and its text is not yet public. The duty is recurring, since a receipt is needed for every sale. Who it covers is still unknown.
market: I found no current count of individual entrepreneurs or of businesses covered. An older ARKA article quotes the SRC as saying there were over 70,000 cash registers in the country. Fip.am cites the Chamber of Notaries: 110 working notaries, 54 of them in Yerevan, so notaries are a negligible segment. The size of the market depends on the sectors named in the December 2026 decision. The lookuptax tracker presents it as a broad expansion.
competitor: Several products already exist. VCR.AM is a virtual cash register API with a PHP SDK that fiscalises sales through the SRC; I did not confirm whether it has a shop-facing app. The 'TAX SERVICE Electronic HDM' WooCommerce plugin from HK Digital Agency needs a paid identification service. The open-source hdm-am Rust client follows the SRC spec. Spyur lists many cash-register vendors and service firms. Registering a cash register with the SRC is free (hartak.am). A minfin tender clarification document (from the search snippet; the fetch returned 503) proposes scaling the MyTax electronic receipt system to self-employed people, which could become a free state tool that undercuts paid offerings. I did not check whether bank POS terminals with built-in fiscal receipts fit the new EKKM rules. I found no dedicated rollout service for offline micro sellers or notaries, but searching was limited.
killer: No killer confirmed. Main risks: (1) existing cash-register dealers and service firms (Spyur listings: HDM SHTRIKH, INNTEQ, HAKT GROUP), the VCR.AM virtual cash register API, PayMob-F devices and bank POS apps (Ardshinbank digiPOS) are well placed to sell e-HDM; (2) the SRC may launch a free e-HDM or e-receipt tool (the minfin tender document was unreachable, HTTP 503); (3) the sector list is not yet published (due late December 2026 under PM Decision 901-A), so the market size is unknown; (4) cash registers are already compulsory for retail sales, so only the device type changes for most of the target group.
reason: The duty is real and in force from 1 Jan 2027, with a heavy AMD 500k fine, which supports the claim. Two things stay unknown: the sector list (due late December 2026) and whether the SRC will offer a free EKKM through MyTax, which the tender document suggests. Paid e-HDM rails already exist (VCR.AM, the HK Digital plugin, cash-register vendors), so a founder would mostly be reselling onboarding. That is a low-margin, one-off service with a short window. It is also exposed if the state ships a free tool or banks bundle fiscal receipts into their POS terminals. Notaries number only 110. It is worth re-checking after the December decision. Until then I can't confirm that nothing already does the core job.
challenge_reason: I checked the law on arlis.am. HO-309-N (3 July 2026) amends Art 380.1(1.1): electronic cash registers (e-HDM) become mandatory for organisations, individual entrepreneurs and notaries in sectors the Government will name, with a new AMD 500,000 fine under Art 416(1.1). The general effective date is 1 Jan 2027. I found nothing that kills the idea, but it is weaker than claimed. Shops selling to the public already have to use cash registers, so for most of them this is a switch from hardware to e-HDM, not a new duty. Hardware register dealers (HDM SHTRIKH, INNTEQ, HAKT GROUP on Spyur), VCR.AM, PayMob-F and bank POS apps are in place to win that switch. Still unknown: which sectors the December 2026 decision covers, and whether the tax authority (SRC) will offer a free e-HDM app.

name: Private clinic cash-register and e-health service code integration
buyer: Small private clinics and dentists
trigger: Draft tax code amendment, April 2026
reason: The draft was adopted as Law HO-60-N (4 March 2026) and has been in force since 1 April 2026. Each medical service must carry a personalized code from the e-health system on billing documents. Medical providers and sole traders connected to e-health that take electronic payments must use an electronic cash register. The rule is a one-off integration, not a recurring workflow, so frequency is low. Penalties and the exact scope are unconfirmed. The e-health operator and existing clinic or cash-register vendors probably handle integration. I found no named product, but my search for vendors was thin. The market is small: no register count found. The pain is real but narrow, and it will be solved once by incumbents.

name: Subsoil-use volume and quarterly/annual reporting tool for small non-metallic quarry and aggregate operators
buyer: Small quarry, sand, gravel, tuff and basalt operators holding subsoil permits
trigger: Gov. Decision 191-N (2018) requires soil users to report to the Ministry of Environment; EPMIB enforcement in 2026 found 81 cases of illegal use or concealed volumes (3.88 million m3 of non-metallic minerals) and uses drones and digital monitoring
reason: Decision 191-N exists (adopted 22 Feb 2018, in force 17 Mar 2018). It covers monitoring of subsoil use and reports on the results. The Ministry of Environment publishes lists of companies that filed such reports, with annual and quarterly reports. I could not read its text, so frequency, forms and penalties are unconfirmed. The 2026 enforcement (81 cases, 3.88M m3, drones) is real but is the inspectorate's own work, not an operator duty, and it names no reporting portal. I found no competing software and no count of small non-metallic permit holders, though geo-fund.am lists over 1,400 mines. Likely a small, politically exposed buyer base, and 191-N monitoring looks more environmental than volume-focused. Score stays low.

name: Stichting and vereniging re-registration kit under the new Civil Code Book 2 and Handelsregisterwet (statutes, notarial deed prep, KKF registration, board changes)
buyer: Small stichtingen and verenigingen (churches, mosques, temples, burial and sports clubs, NGOs) and the notary offices and accountants that serve them
trigger: New Burgerlijk Wetboek Book 2 (S.B. 2024 no. 164) in force 1 May 2025; Overgangswet (S.B. 2024 no. 166); Handelsregisterwet (S.B. 2024 no. 169) and Handelsregisterbesluit (S.B. 2025 no. 46). Reportedly all stichtingen and verenigingen with full legal capacity must be in the trade register, and statute changes need a notarial deed. The transition deadline is unverified.
duty: Partly confirmed. The new BW Book 2 (S.B. 2024 no. 164) has been in force since 1 May 2025 and replaces the 1968 Wet op Stichtingen. The Handelsregisterwet (S.B. 2024 no. 169), as summarised in search snippets of its art. 4, lists stichtingen and verenigingen among the legal persons to be registered, with the KKF keeping the register. The Handelsregisterbesluit (S.B. 2025 no. 46, 22 April 2025) sets free forms set by the KKF and a filing confirmation. Not verified: any transitional deadline for existing bodies in the Overgangswet (S.B. 2024 no. 166) to re-register or amend statutes, article numbers, fines, fees, a UBO duty and an annual-accounts duty. All statute PDFs were unreadable (compressed streams).
market: Not found. No KKF statistic on the number of registered stichtingen or verenigingen was located. Suriname has about 600k inhabitants, so the count is likely in the low thousands (an estimate, not sourced). The notary profession is small and capped.
competitor: No Surinamese software was found. A notarial deed is mandatory for founding a stichting and for statute amendments, and notaries handle drafting and registration, so the core job is already a mandatory professional service. The number of notaries is capped by law (S.B. 2019 no. 119). A software opportunity would be limited to notary or accountant back-office tools. Whether KKF offers online filing was not confirmed.
reason: The framework is real and in force: the new BW Book 2 has applied since 1 May 2025, and the Handelsregisterwet (S.B. 2024 no. 169) brings stichtingen and verenigingen with full legal capacity into the KKF register. What could not be checked is the core claim: whether existing bodies must re-register or amend their statutes, and by what deadline. Every statute PDF (S.B. 166, 169, Book 2) and the two commentaries were compressed and unreadable, and no secondary source states a transition deadline or fines. A notarial deed is mandatory for founding a stichting and for statute changes, so notaries already do the core job by law. That limits software to back-office tooling for a small, capped notary profession. Churches and clubs show weak willingness to pay. Market size was not found.

name: Host-firm compliance tracker for agency labour (WTBAI): licence check of intermediaries, 3-day wage statements, worker lists
buyer: Firms that hire workers through uitzendbureaus and intermediaries (inleners), and small agencies themselves
trigger: WTBAI (2017) as amended by S.B. 2024 no. 45 of 4 Apr 2024: a host firm may not use workers from an intermediary without a licence, and the intermediary must give the host a statement of wage rates within 3 working days of the start of each placement.
reason: Duty is real. S.B. 2024 no. 45 (4 Apr 2024) amended the WTBAI to bar inleners from using workers from an unlicensed intermediary. The 2017 law introduced a licence requirement. The Chamber of Commerce listed more than 140 registered agencies in Nov 2015. I could not confirm the 3-day wage statement, the fines, enforcement, or whether a public licence register exists. The PDF text was not read. No competitor was found in two searches, but that is weak evidence. The market is small, perhaps a few hundred agencies plus their hosts. The duty is a one-time licence check rather than a recurring workflow, so willingness to pay is low and it is a thin product.

name: Gold-buyer (opkoper) purchase register and OKGS badge verification
buyer: Licensed gold buying centres (opkoopcentra) and small-scale gold traders
trigger: OKGS registration of small-scale gold workers soft-launched in July 2026 (6-month pilot) with barcode badges; the stated intent is that buyers may only purchase from registered badge holders. Gold export runs through Kaloti Suriname Minthouse under Central Bank royalty rules. Draft national strategy for artisanal and small-scale gold mining 2026-2036 and a planned cyanide and chemical import barcode register.
reason: No binding duty on gold buyers found. The gov.sr page only says the small-scale miner registration form was digitised and soft-launched on 10 July. It names the Commissie Ordening Goudsector (OGS), not OKGS. It has no buyer rule, deadline or penalty. The OKGS badge-only-purchase policy appears only as an undated plan, and OKGS said no sanctions are intended. Press (SR Herald 2024) says purchases at buying centres are not recorded. Jewellers and precious-metal firms are reportedly AML reporting entities (keynews, secondary source). I did not verify the statute (WMTF 2022 vs Wet MOT/WID). I found no competing product. Buyer count was not found. The sector is cash-based, politically sensitive and has few buyers, and the state is building its own barcode system. Weak, unproven duty.

name: Foreign-worker permit and employer registration tracker (Wet Werkvergunning Vreemdelingen, Ouderschapsverloffonds, possible Werknemersregistratiewet)
buyer: Small employers (shops, restaurants, farms, construction firms, Chinese- and Brazilian-run businesses) hiring foreign staff
trigger: Wet Werkvergunning Vreemdelingen 1981 (amended 2002): employer applies for permits; tighter enforcement announced by the minister of AWJ and a One Stop Unit with 21-day processing. Ouderschapsverloffonds employer registration (deadline 15 Feb 2023, monthly 1% contribution from 1 Mar 2023). The draft Werknemersregistratiewet (annual employer return on staff and work-permit status) is unconfirmed as enacted.
reason: The duty is real. The Wet Werkvergunning Vreemdelingen (SB 1981 no. 162, amended 2002) puts the permit application on the employer. A 2025 guide gives a penalty of up to 6 months in prison or SRD 500,000 (older source, may have changed). The AWJ notice of July 2025 says a business visa does not allow work, and a One Stop Unit promises 21-day processing. I found no local permit-tracking software. Rivermate and other employer-of-record firms cover only expats. The Werknemersregistratiewet is only a draft, so there is no enacted annual return. The duty is a per-hire application, not a recurring workflow, and no household-employer duty was found. The market is small and I found no register count. The buyer is probably consultants, willingness to pay is low, and distribution is weak. I ran only 3 searches and checked no fines or renewal cycles.

name: Tourist-accommodation technical-regulation readiness kit (guesthouses, small hotels, lodges)
buyer: Owners of guesthouses, small hotels, eco-lodges, B&Bs and short-term rentals in Suriname
trigger: Beschikking of the Minister of EZOTI of 23 Dec 2025 no. 1346/25 (S.B. 2026 no. 4) makes SSB 020:2020 parts mandatory for all tourist accommodation after a 2-year transition (about Dec 2027 by my reading of the text). Includes minimum 20 m2 bedrooms and listed articles on safety, hygiene and services.
duty: S.B. 2026 no. 4 is in the Staatsblad, signed 23 Dec 2025 by the Minister of EZOTI. It is based on Art. 6 of the Standaardenwet (S.B. 2004 no. 121, amended by S.B. 2012 no. 42) and makes SSB 020:2020 (mainly chapter 2) a technical regulation for all tourist accommodation in Suriname. I could not confirm the transition period or its start, penalties, enforcement body or the 20 m2 bedroom minimum, because WebFetch returned unreadable compressed PDF data. One search summary mentioned the 20 m2 rule but cited no text; a second search said it could not confirm it. The separate hotel (SSB 021:2021) and guesthouse (SSB 022:2021) standards are listed as voluntary. Laws SB 2023 nos. 87 and 88 created the STA and give it certification and quality-mark powers. Districts such as Para run their own registration and inspection of holiday resorts (fire service, police, health).
market: No current national register of accommodations was found. Statbase/UNWTO show 1,229 hotel rooms in 2011, down from 4,575 in 2005. An older profile lists 1,994 rooms. In Para district about 23 certified resorts had registered in the year before the report. The likely total is a few hundred hotels, guesthouses and lodges, plus informal short-term rentals. Exact count not reached.
competitor: No Suriname vendor found, and no free SSB or STA self-assessment checklist found. The SSB sells the standards and offers training. The STA has legal powers to certify and issue quality marks, and could provide the free route or set the default process. Generic hotel-inspection checklist apps (e.g. SafetyCulture templates) exist but do not cover SSB 020. Competitor check not exhaustive.
reason: The decision exists. Beschikking EZOTI no. 1346/25 of 23 Dec 2025 (S.B. 2026 no. 4) makes SSB 020:2020, the general requirements for tourist accommodation, a technical regulation for all tourist accommodation, at the SSB's request. I could not read the operative articles: the PDF text would not extract. So the 2-year transition, the 20 m2 rule, penalties and the enforcing body are still unconfirmed. I found no local software or free self-assessment tool. The market is small: old UNWTO figures show about 1,200-2,000 hotel rooms, so probably a few hundred establishments. The duty is a one-off readiness job, not a recurring one. The Suriname Toerisme Autoriteit (STA, set up in 2023) issues certification and quality marks and could become the default channel. Low recurring revenue and low willingness to pay.

name: Tour guide, tour operator and travel agency compliance pack (SSB 011:2019 and SSB 005:2019)
buyer: Tour guides, tour operators, travel agencies and booking agents
trigger: SSB regulation list shows Beschikkingen 1345/25 EZ (tour guides) and 1347/25 EZ (booking agents, tour operators, travel agencies) alongside the accommodation one. Likely the same December 2025 date and 2-year transition, which I have not confirmed.
reason: SSB lists Beschikking 1345/25 EZ (SSB 011:2019 tour guides) and 1347/25 EZ (SSB 005:2019 booking agents, tour operators, travel agencies) as technical regulations. The page gives no effective dates or transition. The decision PDFs are scanned images, so I could not read them. Transition, licensing duty, frequency and penalty are unconfirmed. SSB 005 is a quality/consumer-safety standard (revised Dec 2019). It looks like a one-off conformity or certification matter, not a recurring filing workflow. No competing software found, but I only ran one search. The operator count is not found, and the sector is small (likely hundreds of firms). Weak recurring pain and a thin market, so the score stays low.

name: AML/CFT compliance kit for notaries, real estate brokers, accountants, administration offices and lawyers (DNFBPs)
buyer: Small notary offices, property brokers, accountants and bookkeeping offices, small law offices
trigger: Wet MOT (art. 12: report unusual transactions without delay) and WID (client identification), indicators in S.B. 2013 no. 148, supervision by FIU Suriname. FIU Category E guidelines (July 2021) cover CDD, EDD and reporting. A draft replacement law (retention of at least 7 years) was reported but its status is unverified.
duty: The current law is the WMTF (Wet ter voorkoming en bestrijding van money laundering en financiering van terrorisme, S.B. 2022 no. 138 of 19 Nov 2022, amended by S.B. 2024 no. 99 of 2 Aug 2024). It replaces the old Wet MOT/WID regime the claim cites; the "draft law" in the claim was enacted and published by April 2023 (Key News, July 2023). The duty is ongoing, applies per client and per transaction, and the FIU must be notified without delay. Duties: CDD/EDD, showing source of funds, 7-year record retention, compliance officer, risk assessment. Penalties cited: fines up to SRD 100,000 per day, imprisonment, possible licence loss (per TABTO press piece, self-reported). FIU Suriname supervises DNFBPs; the July 2021 Category E guidelines apply. I could not read the WMTF PDF text, so I did not confirm the formal repeal of Wet MOT/WID or the exact in-force date. A Key News piece says the DNA passed a further WMTF amendment with 39 votes; date not confirmed.
market: Not found. No register count of notaries, brokers, accountants or lawyers was located. Suriname has roughly 600k people; covered DNFBPs are plausibly a few hundred (estimate, unverified). The notary count, probably small, is unverified.
competitor: TABTO Group N.V. (Suriname): offers custom compliance products and services, organises the National Compliance Congress, and in July 2023 launched "Know Your Customer Solutions" with Delta Capita for all reporting sectors (notaries, lawyers, brokers, accountants listed). Whether this is software or consultancy is unclear. Global screening APIs also target Suriname (Didit AML screening). FIU reporting portal (goAML or other) and whether it is free: not found, not_reached. No small-firm-specific DNFBP compliance SaaS found.
reason: The duty is real, but the claim cites the wrong law. The WMTF (S.B. 2022 no. 138, amended by S.B. 2024 no. 99) is the current law, not a draft; it was promulgated by April 2023. It requires CDD, source-of-funds checks, 7-year retention and FIU reporting, with fines up to SRD 100,000 per day. Suriname is still under CFATF enhanced follow-up, and DNFBP awareness is low (PIU chair, Dec 2023). I can't confirm nothing does the core job: local firm TABTO Group (with Delta Capita) sells compliance products, KYC solutions and services to "all reporting sectors", including notaries, brokers and accountants. The market is tiny (about 600k population, likely a few hundred DNFBPs). Low urgency in practice and weak willingness to pay make this a 3.

name: Handelsregister (KKF) compliance for sole traders and small firms under the Handelsregisterwet 2024
buyer: All Suriname-based businesses including sole proprietors and partnerships; legal entities that need to file changes
trigger: S.B. 2024 no. 169 (5 Dec 2024) and S.B. 2025 no. 46 (22 Apr 2025). Transitional or re-registration deadlines, if any, were not read.
reason: The Handelsregisterwet (S.B. 2024 no. 169) and the Besluit (S.B. 2025 no. 46) exist, and sources say the duty covers businesses, legal persons and trusts. I could not read the PDFs: the fetch returned binary. So the transitional articles, re-registration deadline, fees and penalties are unconfirmed. Registration is mostly a one-time event, plus change filings, with no clear recurring workflow. No competing software found, but also no sign of demand. The KKF only offers name search and confirmations online, and filings are in person. Buyers are tiny and the state controls the channel. A one-off re-registration deadline could change this if one exists, so check the PDFs manually. Low score.

name: Claim-billing and reconciliation tool for GPs and private labs paid by SZF
buyer: General practitioners, private medical labs, specialist clinics contracted by SZF
trigger: SZF pays providers under agreements; late payments and lab disputes are recurring; Jan 2026 board has a 2-year goal of a single-payer model with all payments through SZF, needing legal changes. Wet Nationale Basiszorgverzekering requires insurance for all residents.
duty: Contractual SZF agreement; no statutory claim-format duty found
market: not found
competitor: none found
reason: The sources I found don't show a legal duty to submit claims in a set format. The duty is contractual: GPs have an agreement with SZF, and payment is due in the last week of the month but usually arrives in the first week of the next. GPs have threatened to stop treating SZF patients over late payment (keynews.sr). The single-payer move is a two-year board priority that needs legal changes. I found no source saying those changes have passed. I found no information on how SZF receives claims, no provider portal, no competing software, and no count of GPs or labs. The pain is mostly late payment by SZF, which software can't fix. The market is small, and a mandatory electronic format could change that. Score stays at 3.

name: Well-owner extraction licence and meter compliance (quota, meter log, fee tiers, renewal)
buyer: Owners of licensed groundwater wells (farms, agricultural cooperatives, small water vendors) and small well-drilling contractors, West Bank
trigger: Regulation 2/2026 amending Regulation 8/2020 (gazette issue 235, 25 Feb 2026) under Water Law decree-law 14/2014: annual extraction licence issue/renewal at 50 JOD; per-m3 fees by tier from 5 to 50 fils above 10,000 m3/yr; no fee on drinking-water quantity; exceeding the licensed quantity is prohibited and the excess is charged at the top tier; a broken meter must be reported at once with a photo, otherwise the PWA estimates and bills the extracted volume; quota-change requests are decided within 30 days; owners must come to the PWA to regularise fees within six months of the regulation taking effect.
reason: The duty exists. Regulation 2/2026 amends Cabinet Regulation 8/2020 under Water Law decree-law 14/2014. A search snippet places it in gazette issue 235, 25 Feb 2026, and says it bars exceeding the licensed extraction quantity. I could not read the fee tiers, meter rule, 6-month window or effective date: the PDF fetch returned unreadable binary. I found no software, app or PWA e-service for well owners (two Arabic searches, not exhaustive). The market is probably tiny: PCBS tables give pumping volumes, not well counts, and I found no licensed-well count. Owners are few, farmers pay little, the duty is mostly a flat fee and visits to the PWA, and the main data (meter logs) sits with the PWA. Hard to sell.

name: Association annual compliance pack (general assembly, board election, annual administrative and financial report to the Interior Ministry registrar)
buyer: Small charitable societies, community and neighbourhood associations, sports and cultural clubs registered under Law 1/2000
trigger: Law 1/2000 on charitable associations and community bodies and Cabinet Resolution 9/2003 (executive regulation): registry kept by the Interior Ministry, records kept at HQ, board elections and filings. 2025 decree-law lets the Interior Minister appoint an interim committee that audits an association's records, which shows the ministry audits governance and records. Exact annual filing deadlines were not confirmed.
reason: Duty is real but weak. Law 1/2000 art. 23 requires an annual general assembly (board report, auditor report, board election), art. 18 requires annual admin and financial reports, and art. 11 requires records at HQ. I found no fixed filing deadline, penalty schedule or registrar form, so the claim's own gap stands. About 3,550 associations in 2012 (2,300 West Bank, 1,250 Gaza), but I found no current count. I found no Interior Ministry e-portal and no specialised tool for this job, but my search was shallow and Bisan NGO was not checked. Buyers are volunteer-run and pay little, the sector is politically sensitive, and the filing is a light paperwork task, so the MVP is simple but willingness to pay is low.

name: Gold and jewellery dealers: approved warranty/sale-certificate register (triplicate books or Directorate-approved electronic system) plus unknown-origin intake forms
buyer: Licensed traders (tajir) and goldsmiths (sa'igh) in the West Bank; the directorate's figure is about 575 factories, workshops and shops with about 3,000 workers
trigger: Ministry of Industry instructions under Decree-Law 39/2022 art. 24 (AML), Law 5/1998 on hallmarking, Consumer Protection Law 21/2005 and Supervision Regulation 5/2021: No 3/2025 (gazette 231, 27 Oct 2025) obliges every trader and goldsmith to issue Directorate-approved warranty certificates (on sale) and sale certificates (on buying from the public), on numbered triplicate carbon books whose serial ranges the Directorate pre-approves, or on an electronic system approved by the Directorate that keeps records and gives inspectors access; No 4/2025 (gazette 233, 29 Dec 2025, 30-day compliance window) bans melting or reworking suspected unknown-origin items, requires the approved form with seller ID details and ownership documents before buying or melting from unlicensed persons, and requires immediate reporting of suspicious pieces; No 2/2025 (gazette 230, 25 Aug 2025) regulates buying and selling gold grain (ribas) and requires purity and maker mark on ingots. Directorate inspects periodically and may seize items.
duty: Instructions No 3/2025 (Gazette 231, 27 Oct 2025) are confirmed from search snippets. Their legal basis is Law 5/1998 on hallmarking and Decree-Law 39/2022 on AML. Every trader and goldsmith must use Directorate-approved warranty and sale certificate forms. The approval request can be filed electronically or in writing, the Directorate decides within 10 working days, and a rejection can be appealed to a grievance committee within 10 working days. The Directorate inspects periodically and may seize suspect items. Instructions No 4/2025 (Gazette 233) on unknown-origin items, with immediate reporting of suspect pieces, are also confirmed. A later instruction, No 1/2026 (Gazette 235, 25 Feb 2026), restricts dealing in precious-metal manufacturing tools and requires traders to register their tools within 30 days. Two parts of the claim are unverified because WebFetch could not decode the gazette PDFs (compressed binary): the triplicate-book detail and the exact wording on the electronic system. The penalty amounts and current enforcement are also unverified.
market: Unverified. The claim says the Directorate counts about 575 workshops and shops with about 3,000 workers, but I found no register or PCBS figure. As context, al-Araby reports that 17.75 t of gold was hallmarked in 2022, 93% above the average of the previous five years, with 96% of it made locally. It is a small and concentrated market, mostly in the West Bank. Gaza coverage in practice is unclear.
competitor: I found no Palestinian vendor or Directorate-approved electronic certificate system. Generic Arab gold-shop accounting and POS products exist, but they are aimed at Saudi rules: Daftra (gold and jewellery module), Qoyod, and freelance builds on Mostaql. None of them shows Palestinian warranty or sale certificate compliance. I did not check Bisan ERP or the Directorate's own e-system. The main substitute is cheap printed triplicate books.
killer: None found. The partial obstacles are cheap Directorate-approved triplicate paper books, an electronic-system approval route that the instructions describe only as "when available", and a market of about 575 outlets. Not reached: whether Bisan ERP has a gold module (its pages show none), any approval of an electronic system after the rule, enforcement data for 2026, and the content of gazette 239 (June 2026), which surfaced in a search but whose PDF text could not be extracted.
reason: The duty is real. Search snippets of Gazette 231 (27 Oct 2025) confirm Palestinian Ministry of Industry Instructions No 3/2025 on unified warranty and sale certificates, issued under Law 5/1998 and Decree-Law 39/2022. Traders apply to the Directorate for approval of their form, electronically or in writing, with a 10-working-day decision, an appeal to a grievance committee, and periodic inspection. No 4/2025 (unknown-origin items, immediate reporting) is also confirmed. I found no Palestinian software with a Directorate-approved certificate module. Daftra and Qoyod gold POS products are generic and Saudi-focused. Still, the market is tiny (about 575 firms, figure unverified), cheap carbon books satisfy the duty, the approval route for vendors is unknown, and willingness to pay is low. Overlaps K03.
challenge_reason: I found nothing that kills it. Arabic searches for Palestinian gold-shop software, a Bisan gold module, the Directorate's own e-services, or a goldsmiths' union tool turned up nothing. Only Saudi or international products appeared: Daftra, Qoyod, HisabPlus and Odoo add-ons, none with Palestinian certificate approval. A search excerpt of No 3/2025 says traders apply for form approval "in writing or electronically when the approved electronic system becomes available". That suggests no approved electronic route existed when the rule was issued. It is also an approval gate any vendor must pass. Three things hold the score at 4: cheap triplicate books are the default, the market is tiny (about 575 outlets), and enforcement since January 2026 is unconfirmed.
